title: Super Wonder Boy in Monster Land

records.c: Preserved transition context: $7AB6 saves all 256 zero-page bytes into $C000–$C0FF; $7ACD clears bytes $02–$FF and $7B10 restores them. The display sort names $02 only as the base of LDY $02,X at $2C28 and LDA $02,X at $2C4E, whose X is at least 1, so both reach the order array at $03–$22 and neither reads $02 itself.

Thirty-two display-slot order bytes at $03–$22; $6B03 initializes them to 0–31. The sort at $2C16 puts these indexes in descending order of the slot Y values at $4CCF–$4CEE, which it reads directly; the final loop changes bit 0 of positions 0–29 in pairs and leaves positions 30–31 unchanged. The sprite interrupts read the order at $16EF and $17C9 with X from $45. The bytes from $04 onward are also addressed through the alias at $04.

Alias for positions 1–31 of the display-slot order array at $03–$22. The loop at $2C75 indexes $04,X with even X from 0 through 28, setting bit 0 of positions 1, 3, …, 29. The same physical bytes belong to the array at $03.

Copy of the 32 display-slot Y values: $2C1E copies $4CCF–$4CEE here when the display sort runs. The sprite interrupts read it at $16F9 and $17D3, through the order array at $03, to place each hardware sprite; the sort itself compares the values at $4CCF. Movement code also adjusts the last 28 entries; the same physical bytes serve both uses.

Alias for the final 28 bytes of the display-slot Y cache at $23–$42. The up/down adjustment loops at $0D26, $0D42, $0E05 and $0E21 scan $27,X for X=27 down to 0, skip $FF and subtract or add $4DB4 modulo 256; two loops also skip indexes saved at $0D54/$0D55. The same physical bytes are used by display sorting.

Unused zero-page byte between the display-slot Y cache $23–$42 and the sort cursor $44. No instruction in the resident code or the 31 loads names it, and the indexed loops over the cache stop at $42. Only the transition loops touch it, as they touch all of zero page: $7AB6 saves it to $C043, $7ACD clears it and $7B10 restores it.

Unused zero-page byte between the player's sprite frame $4A and the message-record pointer $4C. No instruction in the resident code or the 31 loads names it or reaches it through an index. Only the transition loops touch it, as they touch all of zero page: $7AB6 saves it to $C04B, $7ACD clears it and $7B10 restores it.

Unused zero-page byte between the interrupt target $5E/$5F and the transfer count $61. No instruction in the resident code or the 31 loads names it or reaches it through an index. Only the transition loops touch it, as they touch all of zero page: $7AB6 saves it to $C060, $7ACD clears it and $7B10 restores it.

Two unused zero-page bytes, $6A and $6B, between the unpacker's output pointer $68/$69 and the colour lookup pointer $6C/$6D. No instruction in the resident code or the 31 loads names them, and the unpacker's header loop at $7C33 writes only $67–$69. Only the transition loops touch them, as they touch all of zero page: $7AB6 saves them to $C06A/$C06B, $7ACD clears them and $7B10 restores them.
Used as an alternate-loop continuation flag and also cleared by a contact handler; the byte is shared between paths.

Thirty-nine zero-page scratch bytes $82–$A8. The scroll path at $3267 copies $D9B8–$D9DE here, and the loop at $32ED writes these bytes to $D9E0–$DA06. No other instruction in the resident code or the 31 loads names them.

Thirty-nine zero-page scratch bytes $A9–$CF. The scroll path at $326C copies $DAD0–$DAF6 here, and the loop at $32F2 writes these bytes to $DAF8–$DB1E. Two other instructions name the range without using it as data: BIT $00A9 at $22C3 is a two-byte skip over LDA #$00, and the CMP ($C1,X) pair at $7DC9/$7DCB in the serial receiver is a timing delay.

Seventeen unused zero-page bytes, $D0–$E0, between the colour-row scratch $A9–$CF and the motion gate $E1. No instruction in the resident code or the 31 loads names them, and the scratch loops at $326F and $32F2 stop at $CF (X from $26 down to 0). Only the transition loops touch them, as they touch all of zero page: $7AB6 saves them to $C0D0–$C0E0, $7ACD clears them and $7B10 restores them.

Twenty-eight unused zero-page bytes, $E4–$FF, after the entity-record pointer $E2/$E3. No instruction in the resident code or the 31 loads names them or reaches them through an index. Only the transition loops touch them, as they touch all of zero page: $7AB6 saves them to $C0E4–$C0FF, $7ACD clears them and $7B10 restores them.
Jump directly to the resident main update loop at $03F1. No state is initialized by this three-byte entry.
Initializes the title display, copies the screen template, maps its colours, formats the stored record and installs the title raster interrupt before waiting for Fire.

After the title record digit loop compares X with 6 at $02FE, branch back to $02F7 while unequal. On equality, set background colour register $D022 to 0 and enable the raster interrupt with $D01A=1 before continuing title setup at $030C.
Set the low byte of the IRQ trampoline's next target.
Set the high byte of the IRQ trampoline's next target.

Continues after the title Fire wait: the JSR $6DDE at $0324 returns here. It writes $0B to $56A7 and $D011, sets the continue count $0698 to 3 and sets up display and game state before the update loop.
Write low byte $EA to $5E, then high byte $13 to $5F, setting the IRQ trampoline target to $13EA. The target is a code address; these two stores do not by themselves measure an interrupt interval.

Set $5F to $13, write $F2 to $D012 and $08 to $D016, then write $30 to the processor port. Clear $4DBC, call $6CCC, write $35 to the port and enable interrupts before entering $0383. Write $13 to the IRQ target high byte at $5F. The preceding low-byte store sets $5E to $EA, so the pair selects $13EA.

Disable interrupts and wait until a read of $D012 returns zero. Clear $D021, call $34DD, $6ACB, $6C87, $6C04 and $4A43, write $35 to the processor port, set $D012 to $F2 and $D01A to 1, then enable interrupts.

Set $5284 to $FF and $4D69 to zero. Set $4D6A to 7 only when $7F48 is zero and $7F47 is below $AB; otherwise set it to zero. Set $46 to $C0 and call $4655, $6D17, $6E12, $4A90, $18D8, $1863 and $7979.
Set $526C to $80 and $2C15 to 1, then call $77E2 with A=1 before continuing into the main loop at $03F1.
Frame loop: updates countdowns, samples input, updates player and entities, renders display state and checks the selected player's meter before the next state dispatch.
Transfer control to the post-event tally entry at $0699. The game-exit flag at $042F–$0432 can branch here, and the status check at $044B can fall through here.

Dispatch through the little-endian pointer at $7F3F/$7F40, which each load supplies. Load 1 holds $0200 there, the jump back into the main loop; load 2 holds $9661, and the other loads hold targets of their own. The pointer’s value when the jump runs decides the target.
Converts the current grid indices and subcell offsets into four writable position bytes at $04a6–$04a9, used by entity initialization.

Low Y byte of the position prepared at $0453 from the map row $6F3D and the vertical offset $527D, plus $4A; $09B8 copies it to the entity world Y low byte $1990,X. Referenced at $0471 (STA), $09B8 (LDA).

High Y byte paired with $04A6 in the position prepared by $0453; $09BE copies it to the entity world Y high byte $197F,X. Referenced in the resident code at $0455 (STA), $045C (ROL), $0460 (ROL), $0464 (ROL), $0468 (ROL), $0474 (LDA), $0479 (STA), $09BE (LDA).

Low X byte of the prepared entity position, built from the map column $6F3C and the horizontal offset $527C, plus $1D, and paired with $04A9; $09AC copies it to the entity world X low byte $194C,X. Referenced at $049A (STA), $09AC (LDA).

High X byte of the prepared entity position, paired with $04A8; $09B2 copies it to the entity world X high byte $193B,X. Referenced in the resident code at $047E (STA), $0485 (ROL), $0489 (ROL), $048D (ROL), $0491 (ROL), $049D (LDA), $04A2 (STA), $09B2 (LDA).
Call revival routine $04B2. Carry set branches to $04DA; carry clear jumps back to main update loop $03F1.

If bit $10 in the indexed state is clear, return with carry set. Otherwise prepare the revival-medicine message, clear bit $10 in the selected player's flags, and increment an indexed value until the selected value reaches $28; return with carry clear. The first increment uses X as left by the intervening calls.
The wait routine can return X=$fe when it calls the display-copy routine with $5275=0. In that case this indexed increment writes $4ecb, not either of the two meter slots.
Start the high-byte addend at zero.
Use $ff as the high-byte addend for a negative displacement.
The immediate operand is set to $00 for a nonnegative displacement or $ff for a negative one, extending the signed byte into the high-byte addition.
Immediate byte of the ADC at $0542, patched to $00 or $FF to extend the displacement sign into the high-byte addition.

Set the sprite multicolour registers $D025/$D026 to 7 and 2, hide the player and initialize eight display slots from position and frame tables. Wait for fire, store $FF in the 29 bytes $4CD3–$4CEF, which frees display slots 4–31 and also sets the first extra-flags byte at $4CEF, and wait until fire is released. Then return to the title when the selected player's round number at $4DCB,Y, in packed decimal, is $11 or 1. Otherwise save the display, load visual resources, show the continue message and select the left choice.
On each frame refresh the HUD and sample the controls. Test left first, right second and fire third; no selected input repeats the poll.
Place the two selection sprites using X=$E6 and Y=$E1, set the selection byte to $FF and resume polling.
Place the two selection sprites using X=$6E and Y=$E1, clear the selection byte and resume polling.
Fire with a nonzero selection returns to the title; a zero selection checks the remaining continue count.
If no continues remain, show the add-credits message. Otherwise spend one, restore the player meter to its limit, clear all three BCD score bytes and initialize the game display.
Display the message at $0678 and return to the continue-choice poll.
Selection byte used by the continue/exit choice. Referenced at $0606 (STA), $0615 (STA), $061B (LDA).
Saved low player X coordinate used by the exit animation. Referenced at $04EA (STA), $053A (ADC).
Saved high player X coordinate paired with $064A during the exit animation. Referenced at $04EF (STA), $053F (LDA).
Countdown for a step of the exit animation. Referenced at $04E1 (STA), $0553 (DEC), $0560 (STA).

Message record passed to $77E0 at $05D6: three zero-terminated lines, “Continue or not” followed by byte $5F, “Use the CURSOR” and “to select”, then the control byte $FE, which $7843 stores in the display countdown $4D6B. How byte $5F is drawn depends on the game character set.

Message record passed to $77E0 at $063F: the lines “Add credits and” and “select again” followed by byte $5B, each zero-terminated, an empty third line, and the control byte $FE, which $7843 stores in the display countdown $4D6B. How byte $5B is drawn depends on the game character set.
Remaining continue counter used by the continue sequence. Referenced at $0331 (STA), $0623 (LDA), $0628 (DEC).

Prepare the post-event tally: set the sound state, save the display, load the visual resource selected at $7F81, hide the player and clear the display-sort flag. Write $01 across 39 bytes at $D940; when the selected player meter equals its limit also write $01 across 39 bytes at $D990.
When the selected player meter equals its limit, pass $10 to the middle-byte BCD score addition routine. Otherwise skip this full-meter bonus.
Set the refill counter to the selected meter plus eight with eight-bit wrap, and set the score-conversion counter to that meter shifted right once.

On each conversion pass wait for frames, refresh the HUD, pass $02 to the meter-subtraction routine and $41 to the score routine. Decrement the conversion counter and repeat until it is zero. The first pass executes even if the counter began at zero.
Wait for a frame, pass $01 to the meter-addition routine, refresh the HUD and decrement the refill counter until zero. A zero initial counter takes 256 iterations because the decrement wraps.

Wait for fire. In two-player mode, when the selected player index is zero and the second player meter is nonzero, select the second player and initialize the game display. Otherwise continue at the stage-counter path.
Countdown used while refilling the player meter in the conversion sequence. Referenced at $06E0 (STA), $070E (DEC).
Score-conversion countdown: $2B55 decrements it only while nonzero. Referenced at $06E5 (STA), $2B55 (LDA), $2B5A (DEC).

Increment the stage counter $073E, pass its new value in A to $7A6E, which stores it at $2A91 for the disk transfer at $7AF8 ($7D1B) and the patches at $2A90, and jump to the game display set-up at $0383 when the transfer returns. The tally's exits at $071B, $0723 and $0728 come here, as do JMP $0732 in 20 loads (02, 03, 05, 06, 08, 09, 10, 12, 13, 14, 15, 16, 18, 20, 21, 23, 24, 26, 28 and 29) and the two unreached key paths at $2B40 and $7BD2.
Stage-transition selector incremented modulo 256 by $0732 and passed in A to $7A6E. Referenced in the resident code at $023D (LDA), $024B (STA), $0732 (INC), $0735 (LDA), $2B2F (LDA), $7BA8 (LDA).
Runs an alternate update loop with entity and completion scans. It patches an initializer call and preserves selected state in immediate operands before restoring it on exit.
Set the low byte of the following indirect-by-patching call from the indexed table.
Set the high byte of the patched call from the indexed table.

Call the stage object's second routine, whose address $0769 and $076F patch in from $4777,X and $477D,X: bytes 6 and 7 of the stage-object record whose index $47F3 saved in $7B. The load holds JSR $FF00 here; no other instruction writes the operand.

Low byte of the target of the JSR at $0778, whose high byte is $077A. The load holds $00 here, so the instruction reads JSR $FF00 until it is patched. $0769 stores it from $4777,X, byte 6 of the stage-object record selected by $7B, and $076F the high byte from $477D,X (byte 7), just before the call, which runs after $190B has found a free entity slot and $447A has cleared it. No other instruction writes it.
High byte of the mode-selected JSR at $0778, paired with $0779. After it returns, load zero and clear horizontal speed $4DAF.
Save the current value in the immediate operand used to restore it on exit.
Saved frame-offset immediate loaded at $080B and restored to $1177. Continue with X=15 for the cleanup loop at $0812.
Preserve the cleanup loop counter in the immediate operand reloaded after the calls.

Immediate X restored by LDX at $0825 after the cleanup callbacks. Decrement X and loop to $0812, which saves the counter here again, while it is nonnegative. Once exhausted, call $370B, restore $5243 from saved state $0834 and return.
Saved active-entity action count; cleanup at $082D restores it to $5243. Referenced at $0747 (STA), $082D (LDA).
Call revival test $04B2. Carry set jumps to no-revival sequence $04DA; carry clear jumps back to alternate frame loop $079F. The decision is the callback’s returned carry.

Game-exit flag. $6C1F clears it when the player and level state are initialized, and the special-object path at $5F72 sets it to $FF. The main loop tests it at $042F and jumps to the post-event tally at $0699 when it is nonzero; after a record interaction $480D tests it and a nonzero value returns through $479B without the display restoration at $3384. Referenced at $042F (LDA), $480D (LDA), $5F72 (STY), $6C1F (STA).

Gates a down-input action on player and map state. When the action is allowed, $53E0 consumes one of the selected player’s items and returns its type, which indexes the four-entry address table at $08D8/$08DC; the routine patches that address into the jump at $08D5 and takes it, to $08F5, $0952, $096D or $08E0; the action may initialize an entity. The type is 0 to 3: every call of the item push at $536F, in the resident part and in the loads, passes 0, 1, 2 or 3. The callers are the JSRs at $0426 and $07BE.
When $6F equals 1, load the two immediates previously patched by $08E0 and restore them to $6F and $529C. Decrement $5243 modulo 256, then continue at $0853.
Immediate operand restored to $6F when $6F equals 1; another routine patches this byte before that restoration.
Immediate operand restored to $529C when $6F equals 1, after which $5243 is decremented. Otherwise this restoration is skipped.
Return if $72 is nonzero or $4DB3 is negative. A positive $4DB3 branches to $08AF; a zero value continues to the tile and position checks.
Require $527D to equal 15 and $7A to be nonzero; otherwise branch to $08AF. Compare $61D7 against six bytes at $7F77 through $7F7C, scanning from index 5 down to 0; if none matches, enter $08AF.

Return if $527C is at least 2. Otherwise store it at $4DAF and $4DB1, call $101F, set $4DB4 and $527D to 2 and call $0C2C. Clear $4DAF, $4DB1, $4DB0, $1178, $4DB5 and $4D55, set $4DB3 to $FF and return.
Return if $4DBB is nonzero; otherwise set it to $FF. Return if $5243 equals 2, or call $53E0 and return if carry is set; carry clear continues to the action dispatch at $08C5.
Patch the dispatch target low byte from the indexed table.
Patch the dispatch target high byte from the indexed table.

Store the high byte from $08DC,Y at $08D7, completing the JMP at $08D5 whose low byte $08CC stored from $08D8,Y. Y is the item type that $53E0 took from the top of the selected player's item stack, always 0 to 3 since every caller of $536F pushes a type from 0 to 3, so the jump goes to $08F5, $0952, $096D or $08E0.

Low byte of the target of the JMP at $08D5, whose high byte is $08D7. The load holds $00 here, so the instruction reads JMP $FF00 until it is patched. $08CC stores it from $08D8,Y and $08D2 the high byte from $08DC,Y, with Y the selected action index, so the jump goes to $08F5, $0952, $096D or $08E0. No other instruction writes it.

High byte of the target of the JMP at $08D5, whose low byte is $08D6. The load holds $FF here, so the instruction reads JMP $FF00 until it is patched. $08D2 stores it from $08DC,Y and $08CC the low byte from $08D8,Y, with Y the item type that $53E0 takes from the selected player's item stack, so the jump goes to $08F5, $0952, $096D or $08E0. No other instruction writes it.

Four low bytes of the entity-action dispatch table, paired with the high bytes at $08DC: the targets are $08F5, $0952, $096D and $08E0. $08C9 copies the entry for the selected action index into the operand of the JMP at $08D5.
Four high bytes paired with the action target lows at $08D8.
Copy $6F and $529C into the immediate operands at $0848 and $084C. Set $529C to $0F and $6F to 1, then return; a later pass through $0841 can restore the saved values.
Call the horizontal comparison at $72FC for this candidate. The patched branch at $0914 tests the carry it returns.

Branch whose opcode $0900 patches by the player's facing $1177: BCC ($90) when $1177 is nonzero, BCS ($B0) when it is zero, so the scan skips candidates on the side the carry from $72FC rules out. The load holds BCC ($90). $092F also reads the opcode and stores it in the spawned entity's $1B06,X.

Call $190B and then $4454 without testing the carry returned by $190B. Clear $1AA0,X. When $7A is zero, copy $47/$48/$49 to $195D,X/$196E,X/$19A1,X, set $19B2,X to 1 and return. When $7A is nonzero, enter $09AC.
Copy $04A8/$04A9 to $194C,X/$193B,X and $04A6/$04A7 to $1990,X/$197F,X, then return. This path does not set $19B2,X.
Start the eligible-entity search at slot index 16, then fall through to the predicate at $09C7. The predicate and descending scan determine whether a candidate is returned.

Scan entity slots downward from X=$10. Skip type zero, negative types and types at least $21. For types $01–$20 call $1902; if that returns carry clear, continue scanning. On carry set, copy its A result to Y and return with X at the matching slot. If none match, return with X=$FF and carry clear.
Samples action state and updates horizontal movement, deceleration and vertical state. It uses active-low joystick values and recomputes the player grid position.

Five additions to the player’s target horizontal speed, indexed by the selected player’s motion tier $4DD5,X: $09EF adds the entry to 3 and $09F2 stores the sum in $4DB2, giving 3, 4, 4, 5 and 5. The tier is 0 after the player set-up at $6BDE and 1 to 4 once boots are bought, since each shop's boots items 0–3 store their item number plus 1, so every entry is used.

Advance the alternating update counter at $1176. When its low bit is clear, reduce the player horizontal speed at $4DAF by one, clamping a negative result to zero; if speed was already zero, clear the direction at $4DB0. Continue at $0A2F to apply motion.

For the selected player, test flag $08, the fall-step value at $4DB5 and the sampled up input at $71. If the flag is set, the step is below 4 and up is pressed, decrement $4DE0. A nonzero result sets the fall step to 1; zero clears flag $08 and selects message 6, "Lost the Wing Boots." The counter advances on qualifying visits to this code, not on a verified video-frame schedule.
Animation countdown used by the negative vertical-state path. Referenced at $0B27 (DEC), $0B2A (LDA).

If $4DB3 is not 1, enter the input-edge check at $0B84. Otherwise, when $4DB7 is nonzero, select a sprite frame from $1177: add $72 when $4D55 is positive, or $70 when it is zero or negative. A zero result from the $72 addition also falls through to the $70 calculation.
If $1178 is zero, clear $4DB3 and $1178 and return. Otherwise write min($1178,8) to $4DB4, call $0D7F, decrement $1178 and return.

When $4DB7 is nonzero, $71 is zero, $76 is nonzero and $4DB5 is 2, clear $4DB8, set $1178 to 8, set $4DB3 and $4DB5 to 1, and set $4D55 to $FF. Use $4DBD to select a byte from $4DD5 and use it to index $0BC1 for $4DB4. Call $0D7F, then return to $0B41; otherwise jump to $0BC6.

Five vertical step sizes, 0 to 4, indexed by the selected player’s motion tier $4DD5,X: $0BB5 reads the entry and $0BB8 stores it in $4DB4 for the upward move that $0BBB starts. The tier is 0 after the player set-up at $6BDE and 1 to 4 once boots are bought, since each shop's boots items 0–3 store their item number plus 1, so every entry is used.

If $4DB7 is zero, clear the animation index and delay and return. Otherwise, if both $73 and $74 are nonzero, set $4A to $1177 plus $66, clear the index and delay, and return. If either input byte is zero, enter the animation tick at $0BE4.
Clear both the animation index at $0C22 and delay at $0C23, then return.
If the delay at $0C23 is nonzero, decrement it and return; otherwise advance the animation at $0BED.

Use $0C22 as Y to select a frame byte from $0C24,Y, add $1177 and $66, and write $4A. If Y is 4, reset the index and use the first frame and delay instead. Otherwise increment the index and load the delay from $0C28,Y. The CPY #$04 at $0BFC keeps the index at 0 to 4: $0BDD and $0C0C store 0, and $0C00 increments it only when it is below 4.
Reset the animation index to zero, write the first frame plus $1177 plus $66 to $4A, load the first delay from $0C28 and return.
Animation table index, incremented after a frame and reset when its value is 4 or the animation is reset.
Animation delay, decremented on nonzero ticks and reloaded from $0C28,Y when advancing.
Two overlapping indexed views: five frame values at $0c24–$0c28 and four delays at $0c28–$0c2b share the byte at $0c28.

Four walk-animation delays, 1, 1, 2 and 1, loaded into $0C23 by $0C03 with Y from 0 to 3 and, for the first, by $0C1B. The byte at $0C28 is also the fifth frame value of the $0C24,Y lookup, read when Y is 4; $0C29–$0C2B are delays only.
If $7A is zero, tail-jump to $0D56. Otherwise set $4DB6 to $FF and add $527D to $4DB4 modulo 256. A result below $10 skips the tile reads and enters $0C9D; otherwise check the next map row.
Use $6F3D+1 modulo 256 to select a pointer from $85CF/$8620, and use $6F3C as the column. Read the tile index and test bits 0 and 1 of $80CF indexed by it. If either bit is set, enter $0C81.
When $4DB3 is not $FF, repeat the attribute test for the next column. If neither low bit is set, enter $0C9D; otherwise enter $0C81. A $4DB3 value of $FF skips this second tile test.
Set $4DB4 to $0F minus $527D modulo 256. Clear $4DB3, $4DB6, $4D55, $4DB8 and $4DB9, then enter $0CA0 without calling $213E.
Call $213E for the entity-landing check, then continue at $0CA0.
Compare $49 with $A2. Equality enters $0CBD; a higher value enters $0CF6. For a lower value, add $4DB4 modulo 256: if the result is below $A3 store it at $49 and return; otherwise enter $0CB3.
Subtract $A2 from the candidate Y into $4DB4, set $49 to $A2 and continue at $0CBD.
Subtract $4DB4 from $4D69. If there is no borrow, store the result at $4D69 and tail-jump to $0D0A. Otherwise push the result and enter the map-boundary check at $0CCC.

Add 1 to $569E modulo 256, shift it right once and compare it with $7F4C. If below, call $2E77 and $0D0A, pop the saved difference, store its low three bits at $4D69 and tail-jump to $31A9. Otherwise enter $0CE8.
Pop and negate the saved difference modulo 256 into $4DB4, clear $4D69 and continue at $0CF6.
Add $4DB4 to $49 modulo 256. If the result is at least $E1, clear $4DB3 and replace the result with $E1. Store it at $49 and return.

If $4DB8 is zero or negative, update every eligible entry through $0D42. Otherwise use $4DB9 as Y, subtract 4 from each of $1A29,Y and $1A3A,Y, and store the resulting exclusion indexes at $0D54 and $0D55.
Scan X from $1B down to zero. Skip an entry at $27,X if it is $FF or X equals either exclusion index. Subtract $4DB4 modulo 256 from each remaining byte and return after the scan.
Scan X from $1B down to zero. Skip $27,X when it is $FF; otherwise subtract $4DB4 modulo 256 and store it back. Return after all 28 entries.
First exclusion index for the slot adjustments, computed from the contact entity first slot minus 4.
Second exclusion index for the slot adjustments, computed from the contact entity second slot minus 4.

Set $4DB6 to $FF and patch the comparison operand at $0D6B with ($4D69 + $C2) modulo 256. Add $4DB4 to player screen Y at $49 modulo 256, then compare that byte with the patched limit; the remaining branch is described at $0D6B.

Immediate CMP operand patched by $0D61 with ($4D69 + $C2) modulo 256. If the proposed Y is at least this unsigned byte, clear $4DB3, $4DB6 and $4D55 and store the limit to $49; otherwise store the proposed Y. Both the limit and proposed Y additions wrap to a byte before the comparison.

If $7A is zero, tail-jump to $0E33. Otherwise compare $49 with $A2: equality enters $0DA8, a lower value enters $0DDA, and a higher value subtracts $4DB4 modulo 256. Store that result and return if it is at least $A3; otherwise enter $0D99.
Patch $0DA0 with the subtraction result, set $4DB4 to $A2 minus that byte modulo 256, set $49 to $A2 and continue at $0DA8.
Immediate operand patched at $0D99 with the candidate player Y for the anchor-step calculation.
Add $4DB4 to $4D69 modulo 256. If the result is below 8, store it at $4D69 and tail-jump to $0DE9. Otherwise push the result and check $569D.
If $569D is nonzero, call $2F45 and $0DE9, pop the saved sum, store its low three bits at $4D69 and tail-jump to $325F. If $569D is zero, pop the sum and enter $0DCF.
Subtract 7 from the saved sum into $4DB4 and set $4D69 to 7. Subtract $4DB4 from $49 modulo 256, replace a result below $4B with $4B, store it at $49 and return.

If $4DB8 is zero or negative, update every eligible entry through $0E21. Otherwise use $4DB9 as Y, subtract 4 from each of $1A29,Y and $1A3A,Y, and store the resulting exclusion indexes at $0D54 and $0D55.
Scan X from $1B down to zero. Skip an entry at $27,X if it is $FF or X equals either exclusion index. Add $4DB4 modulo 256 to each remaining byte and return after the scan.
Scan X from $1B down to zero. Skip $27,X when it is $FF; otherwise add $4DB4 modulo 256 and store it back. Return after all 28 entries.
Set $1177 to $0E. Load the selected player profile from $4DD9 indexed by $4DBD; if it equals 3 and bit 0 of $5274 is set, return. Otherwise continue at $0E58.
Return if $E1 is zero. If $4DAF is nonzero and $4DB0 is negative, decrement $4DAF and return without changing direction. Otherwise enter $0E6A.
Compare $4DAF with $4DB2. Increment speed if below, decrement it if above, or leave it unchanged if equal. Set $4DB0 to 1 and return.
Applies rightward movement, testing map attributes and either moving the player or updating the view. A blocking test can shorten the step.

If the high byte at $48 is nonzero or the low byte at $47 is below $AA, enter $0F30. Otherwise subtract $4DB1 from $4D6A; store the difference and return if it does not borrow, or enter $0EED if it does.

Save the borrowed fine-scroll difference in the immediate operand at $0F07. If $569C is odd and (($569C >> 1) + 1) is at least $7F4B, enter $0F17. Otherwise call $2C8D, add 8 to the saved difference, call $0F63 and store the result at $4D6A, then call $3033.

Immediate operand of LDA at $0F06 holding the saved right-scroll difference. Add 8 with carry clear, preserve the result across $0F63 on the stack, write it to $4D6A and call $3033, then return. The earlier path patches this operand; it is not a fixed $FF constant.
Add 8 to the saved difference, XOR with 7, then add that value plus one to the two-byte player X at $47/$48. Clear $4D6A and return.

Add $4DB1 to the low byte of player X. If the result is at least $AA, enter $0F4F. Otherwise store it; the ADC #$00 on the high byte at $0F3E runs with carry clear, because the CMP #$AA has just cleared it, so $48 keeps its value. When that high byte is nonzero, clamp the low byte to at most $3A.
Set the low player X byte to $AA, subtract $AA from the candidate position and patch that remainder into the operand at $0F5E. Subtract the patched remainder from $4D6A and return.
Subtrahend operand of SBC at $0F5D, patched with the right-scroll position adjustment. Store the subtraction result to fine-scroll byte $4D6A and return.

If $4DB8 is nonnegative, subtract the horizontal step from all 28 positions through $0F9F. If it is negative, derive two exclusion indexes from the contact entity slots and subtract through $0F7D. Only the all-position path applies a further low-byte subtraction after a high-byte borrow.
Scan X from $1B down to zero, skipping both exclusion indexes. Subtract $4DB1 from the low byte at $4C73,X and the borrow from the high byte at $4C53,X; store both and return after 28 positions.

Scan all 28 positions, subtracting $4DB1 from $4C73,X and the borrow from $4C53,X. If that high-byte subtraction borrows, subtract another 8 from the low byte modulo 256: SBC #7 executes with carry clear. The extra subtraction does not update the high byte.
Add $4DB1 to the 16-bit player X at $48:$47 modulo 65536. If the resulting high byte is nonzero and the low byte is at least $3A, replace the low byte with $3A. Return.
Set $1177 to zero. Load the selected player profile from $4DD9 indexed by $4DBD; if it equals 3 and bit 0 of $5274 is set, return. Otherwise continue at $0FF2.
Return if $E1 is zero. If $4DAF is nonzero and $4DB0 is positive, decrement $4DAF and return without changing direction. Otherwise enter $1006.
Compare $4DAF with $4DB2. Increment speed if below, decrement it if above, or leave it unchanged if equal. Set $4DB0 to $FF and return.
Applies leftward movement, testing map attributes and either moving the player or updating the view. A blocking test can shorten the step.
If the high player-X byte $48 is nonzero or the low byte $47 is at least $AB, enter $10C4. Otherwise add $4DB1 to $4D6A; store the sum and return if below 8, or enter $1082.
Patch the sum into the operand at $108E. When $569B is nonzero, call $2D82, subtract 8 from the patched sum, call $1107, store the result at $4D6A and tail-jump to $30EE. A zero $569B enters $109D.

Immediate operand of the LDA at $108D. $1082 stores here the sum of the fine scroll $4D6A and the step $4DB1 when it reaches 8 or more; no other instruction writes it, and the load holds $FF. This path subtracts 8, keeps the result on the stack across $1107, writes it to $4D6A and tail-jumps to $30EE; the map-start path at $109D reads the same sum and subtracts 7.

Subtract 7 from the patched sum at $108E and patch the result into the immediate subtraction at $10A8. Subtract that byte from player X at $47/$48, with the carry the first subtraction leaves set: $1082 is the only writer of $108E and stores only sums of 8 or more, so the result is 1 or more and nothing borrows. If the high byte is zero and the low byte is below $1C, clamp the low byte to $1C. Set $4D6A to 7 and return.

Immediate operand of the SBC at $10A8, patched by $10A3 with ($108E - 7) modulo 256. The carry from that earlier subtraction is still live, and always set: $1082, the only writer of $108E, stores only sums of 8 or more (the CMP #$08 at $107A), so the player X subtraction never borrows. The result at $47/$48 is clamped to $001C when its high byte is zero and its low byte is below $1C.
Subtract $4DB1 from player X into the temporary bytes $1104/$1105. If the temporary high byte is zero and its low byte is below $AA, enter $10EB; otherwise store both bytes at $47/$48 and return.
Set the low player X byte to $AA. Patch the temporary low byte into $10F6, calculate $AA minus that value, patch the result into $10FF and add it to $4D6A.
Patched subtrahend of SBC at $10F5, used after carry is set to compute the left-scroll anchor adjustment. Save the result as operand $10FF, load $4D6A and clear carry for adding the adjustment back.
Added operand of ADC at $10FE, patched with the left-scroll anchor adjustment. Store the sum to $4D6A and return; the preceding instruction clears carry.
Temporary low X coordinate used by the left-scroll boundary arithmetic. Referenced at $10CA (STA), $10D9 (LDA), $10E0 (LDA).
Temporary high X coordinate paired with $1104 during left-scroll boundary handling. Referenced at $10D1 (STA), $10D4 (LDA), $10E5 (LDA).
One byte, $00, between the temporary coordinate pair at $1104/$1105 and the routine at $1107. No instruction in the resident code or the 31 loads names it.

If $4DB8 is nonnegative, update all positions through $1143. If it is negative, use $4DB9 as Y, subtract 4 from each of $1A29,Y and $1A3A,Y, and save the resulting exclusion indexes at $0D54 and $0D55.
Scan X from $1B down to zero, skipping the two exclusion indexes. Add $4DB1 to the low byte at $4C73,X, add the carry to the high byte at $4C53,X, and store both.
Scan all 28 positions, adding $4DB1 to $4C73,X and propagating carry into $4C53,X. Store both bytes and return after the scan.
Subtract $4DB1 from the 16-bit player X at $48:$47 modulo 65536. If the resulting high byte is zero and the low byte is below $1C, replace the low byte with $1C. Return.
Counter whose low bit selects alternating update passes. Referenced at $0A0E (INC), $0A11 (LDA).

Sprite-frame offset for the way the player faces: $0FDE sets it to 0 when accelerating left and $0E44 to $0E when accelerating right, and the frame selections at $0AF2, $0AFB, $0B54, $0B5E, $0BD3, $0BF4 and $0C13 add it to a base frame. $6C52 initializes it to $7F46 minus $66, modulo 256, and $0780/$080D save and restore it around the alternate loop. The recoil code at $11D7 and the spawn at $08F5 test whether it is zero to choose a direction.
Countdown used by the player’s vertical animation state. Referenced in the resident code at $08A0 (STA), $0B66 (LDA), $0B77 (DEC), $0B80 (STA), $0B9F (STA), $6122 (STA), $6B77 (STY), $7298 (STA).
Return with carry clear if $4DDD is nonzero, or if the selected $4DD7,Y byte is zero, or if $4DB7 is zero. Y is loaded from $4DBD for the latter two checks.
Clear carry and return without calling the contact checker.
Read $4A. If it is at least $74, set $762A to $4DAE plus 10 and subtract 14 from A; otherwise set $762A to $4DAE. If the resulting A is at least $6C, return with carry clear.
Set $762B to $49 plus 6, $762D to 11 and $762C to 4. Call $75E3 and return if carry is clear.
When $75E3 returns carry set, load Y from $4DBD and set $4DAF to 5 minus $4DD7,Y. Read $1177 and set $4DB0 to 1 if it is zero or $FF otherwise; return with carry set.

NMI entry saves A, X, Y and the CPU port in immediate operands, maps I/O in, tests the CIA2 timer source and transfers through a patched target or handles the non-timer path. Save A in the immediate operand used by the NMI return path.
Save Y in the immediate operand used by the NMI return path.
Save X in the immediate operand used by the NMI return path.
Save the CPU port value in the immediate operand restored on return.
Jump to the CIA 2 timer NMI's current handler, patched into $1202/$1203 at three places: $1266 ($123F/$1244), $130A ($127C/$1281) or $121C ($1523/$1528). The load holds JMP $FF00.

Low byte of the target of the JMP at $1201, whose high byte is $1203. The load holds $00 here, so the instruction reads JMP $FF00 until it is patched. Three places set the CIA 2 NMI target: $123F stores $66 and $1244 the high byte $12 ($1266), $127C stores $0A and $1281 $13 ($130A), and $1523 stores $1C and $1528 $12 ($121C). No other instruction writes it.

High byte of the patched JMP at $1201, paired with $1202. The alternative NMI path begins at $1204: if either $5275 or $56A7 is zero, restore through $1211; when both are nonzero, jump to title initialization at $0203.
Saved processor-port operand of LDA at $1211. Restore it to $01 before loading the saved A operand at $1216 in the NMI return path.

Immediate operand of the LDA at $1215 in the NMI exit $1211–$121B, which reloads the port $01, A, Y and X and returns with RTI; the non-timer path at $1204 and the timer handlers (JMP $1211 at $1263, $12B7, $1306 and $13C7) end there. $11E8, the NMI's first instruction, stores the interrupted A here (with Y at $1218, X at $121A and $01 at $1212); no other instruction writes it. The load holds $FF here.

Immediate operand of the LDY at $1217 in the NMI exit $1211–$121B, which reloads the port $01, A, Y and X and returns with RTI. $11EB, in the NMI's entry $11E8, stores the interrupted Y here (with A at $1216, X at $121A and $01 at $1212); no other instruction writes it. The load holds $FF here.
Immediate operand that restores X before RTI; the NMI entry patches it with the interrupted X value.

Copy 17 bytes from $50BE–$50CE to VIC position and X-high registers $D000–$D010. Copy eight sprite pointers from $50CF–$50D6 to $C3F8–$C3FF and eight colour bytes from $511F–$5126 to $D027–$D02E, then write zero to $D01C. The timer setup for the next NMI follows at $123D.
Patch the low byte of the CIA2 timer NMI dispatch target.
Patch the high byte of the CIA2 timer NMI dispatch target.
Patch the low byte of the next CIA2 timer NMI dispatch target.
Patch the high byte of the next CIA2 timer NMI dispatch target.
Countdown controlling sprite-colour toggles in the interrupt display path. Referenced in the resident code at $12A0 (DEC), $12B4 (STA), $12CA (DEC), $12DE (STA), $12EF (DEC), $1303 (STA).

Wait for raster line $56, run two short delay loops around writes of $78 and $78 OR vertical scroll to $D011, then wait for the raster line to change. Set $D016 to $10 OR the low three horizontal-scroll bits, set background colour from $6F, and select timing operands from tables indexed by $5294 according to whether vertical scroll is zero. $5294 is 0 to 7, the number of the seven sprites 0–6 whose Y register lies from $4A to $5F, counted at $1779, so the eight-entry tables cover every value.
Select the raster comparison value from the zero-scroll table.
Select the delay loop count from the zero-scroll table.
Select the raster comparison value from the nonzero-scroll table.
Select the delay loop count from the nonzero-scroll table.

Clear sprite priority, copy the two shared background colours from $529C/$529D to $D022/$D023, and write $04 to $D018 when $46 equals $C0, otherwise $14. The following raster wait and sprite repositioning continue at $1383.

Wait for the raster line selected by the patched immediate operand, then read $D011, clear bits 5 and 6, wait the patched delay count, and write the value back. Copy the sprite X-high mask and seven sprite X coordinates from $4D68 and $4D64 down to $4D58 to their VIC registers, then jump to the NMI restore path.

Patched raster-line operand of LDA at $1383. Compare that line with $D012 until equal, then read $D011, clear bits 5 and 6 with AND $9F, and load the separately patched delay counter at $1390. The parent routine documents the later sprite writes and return.

Immediate delay count for the Y decrement loop at $1391, patched from a scroll-dependent table. After the loop the routine writes the masked $D011 value, the X-high mask and seven sprite X coordinates, then jumps to the NMI restore path.
Eight delay counts selected when vertical scroll is nonzero, indexed by $5294: 10, 9, 7, 7, 7, 6, 6, 6.
Eight raster values selected when vertical scroll is nonzero, indexed by $5294: each is $60.
Eight delay counts selected when vertical scroll is zero, indexed by $5294: 1, 10, 10, 9, 8, 8, 7, 7.
Eight raster values selected when vertical scroll is zero, indexed by $5294: $60 followed by seven $5F values.

Raster interrupt initializes the sprite multiplexer, display state and next IRQ, scans the keyboard and updates frame counters. It saves register and port state in patched immediates. Save the interrupted register or CPU port value in the immediate operand restored on return. Save the interrupted register or CPU port value in the immediate operand restored on return.
Save the interrupted register or CPU port value in the immediate operand restored on return.

Save the CPU port for the interrupt return and select $35, then wait for raster $F3 and the next line. Acknowledge the VIC interrupt and move the eight hardware sprites away. While the no-contact countdown $4DDD is nonzero, decrement the blink counter $16B6 and clear the X values of display slots 2 and 3 when the result is even; clear them too when the damage cooldown $4DE1 is odd, and skip the update when the player Y is $FF. Otherwise assign the player frame and its adjacent frame to display slots 2 and 3, adjust their X coordinate by five for frames $80, $72, $7C and $6E, and copy the player Y coordinate. At raster $FA clear bit 3 of VIC control register 1.
Set a byte of the NMI dispatch target.

Finish setting the CIA 2 timer A NMI target to $121C, load its $0900 latch and enable its interrupt, then set background colours. When world mode is zero and the effect cursor $4D50 is nonnegative, scan the eight object flags at $4D21 circularly from the cursor and give up to two objects that are still out, flag zero, a pair of display slots each as two sprite layers; a pair with no object gets Y=$FF. Save the cursor and sort the display slots before scheduling the next raster interrupt.
Write low byte $B7 to $5E, then high byte $16 to $5F, setting the IRQ trampoline target to $16B7. The target is a code address; these two stores do not by themselves measure an interrupt interval.
Write $16 to the IRQ target high byte at $5F. The preceding low-byte store sets $5E to $B7, so the pair selects $16B7.

Clear $DC02. If $5275 is nonzero increment $526C; always increment $5274. Write $FF to $D015, zero to $D01D, $18 to $D016 and $02 to $D018, then continue into the saved-port and register restoration at $16AB.
Saved processor-port operand loaded at $16AB and stored to $01. Continue by loading the saved A operand at $16B0 in the frame IRQ return path.

Immediate operand of the LDA at $16AF in the exit $16AB–$16B5 of the frame raster interrupt $13EA, which reloads the port $01, A, X and Y and returns with RTI. $13EA, the interrupt's first instruction, stores the interrupted A here (with X at $16B2, Y at $16B4 and $01 at $16AC); no other instruction writes it. The load holds $FF here.

Immediate operand of the LDX at $16B1 in the interrupt exit $16AF–$16B5, which reloads A, X and Y from patched operands and returns with RTI. $13ED stores the interrupted X here (and $13F0 stores Y at $16B4); no other instruction writes it. The load holds $FF here.

Immediate operand of the LDY at $16B3 in the exit $16AB–$16B5 of the frame raster interrupt $13EA, which reloads the port $01, A, X and Y and returns with RTI at $16B5. $13F0, in that interrupt's entry, stores the interrupted Y here (with A at $16B0, X at $16B2 and $01 at $16AC); no other instruction writes it. The load holds $FF here.

Blink counter for the player’s sprite pair: while the no-contact countdown $4DDD is nonzero the frame interrupt decrements it at $1456 and, when the result is even, clears the X values of display slots 2 and 3 for that frame. It wraps freely and is never reloaded. Referenced at $1456 (DEC), $1459 (LDA).

First sprite-multiplexer stage loads slots, updates sprite masks and pointers, schedules a reuse interrupt and records positions for the raster split. Save the interrupted register or CPU port value in the immediate operand restored on return. Save the interrupted register or CPU port value in the immediate operand restored on return.
Save incoming X in the immediate operand at $1796 and incoming Y at $1798. The following code saves CPU port $01 at $179A and selects port value $35 for the sprite IRQ work.

Save the value read from CPU port $01 in the restore operand at $179A, write $35 to the port, and acknowledge VIC interrupt bit 0. Write $FF to sprite coordinate registers $D000–$D00D, set $D010 and its shadow $4D68 to $7F, copy the meter X byte $6E to $D00E, and set $D01D and $D01B to $80. The CPU-port read can reflect input pins.
Save the hardware sprite index in the immediate operand used later in this handler.
Write A to $D001,X and the slot byte $4C6F,Y to $4D58,X. X is the doubled hardware-sprite index here; $170D then restores the undoubled index.
Immediate operand patched at $16F4 with the hardware-sprite index. Use it to replace one bit of the cached X-high mask at $4D68 from bit 0 of $4C4F,Y.
Use bit 0 of $4C2F,Y to replace the selected bit of $D01C using the clear and set masks at $4D0F/$4D17.
Use bit 0 of $4CEF,Y to replace the selected bit of $D01D using the same indexed masks.
Copy $4C8F,Y to $C3F8,X and $C7F8,X, then copy $4CAF,Y to $D027,X before continuing at $1753.
Decrement $45. If the result is negative, enter the end-of-frame path at $17A0; otherwise continue at $1757.

Take the low three bits of $45, double them into X and add $15 modulo 256 to the sprite Y register at $D001,X. If the result is at or below the raster value read from $D012, jump to $16ED. If it is at least $E9, enter $17A0; otherwise write it to $D012 and set the next target at $5E/$5F to $17B0 before entering $1779.
Write low byte $B0 to $5E, then high byte $17 to $5F, setting the IRQ trampoline target to $17B0. The target is a code address; these two stores do not by themselves measure an interrupt interval.
Write $17 to the IRQ target high byte at $5F. The preceding low-byte store sets $5E to $B0, so the pair selects $17B0.

Clear $5294 and scan the seven sprite Y registers at $D001, $D003, $D005, $D007, $D009, $D00B and $D00D. Increment $5294 for each value from $4A through $5F inclusive, then enter the interrupt-context restore at $1795.

Immediate operand of the LDX at $1795 in the exit $1795–$179F of the first sprite-multiplexer interrupt, which reloads X, Y, the port $01 and A and returns with RTI. $16BA, in that interrupt's entry $16B7, stores the interrupted X here (with A at $179E, Y at $1798 and $01 at $179A); no other instruction writes it. The load holds $FF here.

Immediate operand of the LDY at $1797 in the exit $1795–$179F of the first sprite-multiplexer interrupt, which reloads X, Y, the port $01 and A and returns with RTI. $16BD, in that interrupt's entry $16B7, stores the interrupted Y here (with X at $1796, A at $179E and $01 at $179A); no other instruction writes it. The load holds $FF here.
Saved processor-port operand loaded at $1799 and stored to $01. Load the saved A at $179D and return from the split interrupt with RTI.

Immediate operand of the LDA at $179D in the exit $1795–$179F of the first sprite-multiplexer interrupt, which reloads X, Y, the port $01 and A and returns with RTI at $179F. $16B7, the interrupt's first instruction, stores the interrupted A here (with X at $1796, Y at $1798 and $01 at $179A); no other instruction writes it. The load holds $FF here.
Write $F2 to $D012, set $5E/$5F to $13EA and jump to $1779.

Write low byte $EA to $5E, then high byte $13 to $5F, setting the IRQ trampoline target to $13EA. The target is a code address; these two stores do not by themselves measure an interrupt interval. Load low IRQ target byte $EA and store it in $5E. The following $17A9 store supplies high byte $13, selecting $13EA for the end-of-frame handler.
Write $13 to the IRQ target high byte at $5F. The preceding low-byte store sets $5E to $EA, so the pair selects $13EA.

Later sprite-multiplexer stage updates hardware positions, masks, colours and pointers, then schedules another reuse or the end-of-frame interrupt. Save incoming A in the immediate operand at $1851 before the reused-sprite interrupt work. The following stores save X and Y, and $17B9 saves the CPU port.
Save incoming X in the immediate operand at $1849 and incoming Y at $184B for restoration at the end of the reused-sprite interrupt handler.

Read CPU port $01 and save it in the immediate restore operand at $184D. Select port value $35, write 1 to VIC interrupt status $D019 and load the display-sort index from $45; interrupt timing is separate.
Mask the display-sort index in A with 7 and save that hardware-sprite index in the immediate operand at $17E4. Shift it left and transfer to X for paired VIC position registers.
Write A to $D001,X and $4C6F,Y to $D000,X, where X is the doubled hardware-sprite index. The following immediate operand restores the undoubled index.
Immediate operand patched at $17CE with the hardware-sprite index. Use it to replace one bit of $D010 from bit 0 of $4C4F,Y.
Use bit 0 of $4C2F,Y to replace the selected bit of $D01C using the indexed masks at $4D0F/$4D17.
Use bit 0 of $4CEF,Y to replace the selected bit of $D01D using the indexed masks.
Copy $4C8F,Y to $C3F8,X and $C7F8,X, then copy $4CAF,Y to $D027,X before continuing at $182A.
Decrement $45. If the result is negative, enter the end-of-frame path at $1853; otherwise continue at $182E.

Take the low three bits of $45, double them into X and add $15 modulo 256 to $D001,X. If the result is at or below the raster read from $D012, jump to $17C7. If it is at least $E9, enter $1853; otherwise write it to $D012 and continue at $1848.

Immediate operand of the LDX at $1848 in the exit $1848–$1852 of the next sprite-multiplexer interrupt, which reloads X, Y, the port $01 and A and returns with RTI. $17B3, in that interrupt's entry $17B0, stores the interrupted X here (with A at $1851 and Y at $184B); no other instruction writes it. The load holds $FF here.

Immediate operand of the LDY at $184A in the exit $1848–$1852 of the next sprite-multiplexer interrupt, which reloads X, Y, the port $01 and A and returns with RTI. $17B6, in that interrupt's entry $17B0, stores the interrupted Y here (with X at $1849, A at $1851 and $01 at $184D); no other instruction writes it. The load holds $FF here.
Saved processor-port operand loaded at $184C and stored to $01. Load saved A at $1850 and RTI from the sprite-reuse interrupt.

Immediate operand of the LDA at $1850 in the exit $1848–$1852 of the next sprite-multiplexer interrupt, which reloads X, Y, the port $01 and A and returns with RTI at $1852. $17B0, the interrupt's first instruction, stores the interrupted A here (with X at $1849, Y at $184B and $01 at $184D); no other instruction writes it. The load holds $FF here.
Write $F2 to $D012, set $5E/$5F to $13EA and jump to $1848.

Write low byte $EA to $5E, then high byte $13 to $5F, setting the IRQ trampoline target to $13EA. The target is a code address; these two stores do not by themselves measure an interrupt interval. Load $EA and store the low IRQ target byte at $5E. The following $185C path supplies high byte $13 and restores the sprite-reuse interrupt context.

Write $13 to the IRQ target high byte at $5F. The preceding low-byte store sets $5E to $EA, so the pair selects $13EA. Load $13 into the IRQ trampoline high byte $5F, paired with $EA already stored in $5E at $185A. Jump to context restoration at $1848; the target vector is $13EA.

Load the load's entity records into the slot arrays. Set the record pointer $E2/$E3 from $7F4F/$7F50 and the slot limit $4DBA from $7F51, release slots 0–16 through $4454, then copy records into slots 1 upward through $369E and clear each slot's state bytes. The loop stops when the next record's first byte is zero or when the slot reaches the limit (CPX $4DBA at $18CB), and stores the next record's number in $7C. The limit is 1 to 9 in the 31 loads' headers, so the records fill slots 1 to 9 at most.

Clear slot zero of entity type, eight type-state fields, auxiliary state, display effect, animation countdown and direct-coordinate state: $1919, $1AB1, $1AC2, $1AD3, $1AE4, $1AF5, $1B06, $1B17, $1B28, $1A7E, $1A8F, $1AA0 and $19B2. Return after the thirteen stores; adjacent slot-one bytes are untouched by this routine.
Test the entity’s first display-slot byte $1A29,X. Zero returns carry clear; every nonzero byte returns carry set. A retains the tested byte and X/Y are unchanged.
Search the 17 entity-type slots $1919–$1929 from index 16 down to 0. Return the first zero slot in X with carry set. If every slot is nonzero, return X=$FF with carry clear. Y is not changed.

Entity type, one byte for each of the 17 entity slots, $1919–$1929, the first of the parallel entity arrays spaced 17 bytes apart. Zero marks a free slot, which the search at $190B finds from slot 16 down to 0; the update loop at $1FDC skips it, runs a positive type's handler from the load's tables at $7EDF/$7F0F ($2027) and a negative type's from $2062/$2074 ($203C). $369E copies record byte 0 here. The record loaders $1863 and $3622 fill slots 1 to the load's limit $4DBA, at most 9 (CPX $4DBA at $18CB and $3629), and spawned entities take the slots 16 down to 0 that the free-slot search $190B finds.

Seventeen-byte entity array for the flags, indexed by entity slot. The ten-byte record copier at $369E installs record byte 8 here. The record loaders $1863 and $3622 fill slots 1 to the load's limit $4DBA, at most 9 (CPX $4DBA at $18CB and $3629), and spawned entities take the slots 16 down to 0 that the free-slot search $190B finds.

Seventeen-byte entity array for the world X high byte, indexed by entity slot. The ten-byte record copier at $369E installs record byte 2 here. The record loaders $1863 and $3622 fill slots 1 to the load's limit $4DBA, at most 9 (CPX $4DBA at $18CB and $3629), and spawned entities take the slots 16 down to 0 that the free-slot search $190B finds.

Seventeen-byte entity array for the world X low byte, indexed by entity slot. The ten-byte record copier at $369E installs record byte 3 here. The record loaders $1863 and $3622 fill slots 1 to the load's limit $4DBA, at most 9 (CPX $4DBA at $18CB and $3629), and spawned entities take the slots 16 down to 0 that the free-slot search $190B finds.

Seventeen per-entity low bytes of the screen X coordinate, paired with high bytes at $196E. The direct display builder at $1DC8 copies the pair to the display slots ($1EA5, $1EE3, $1F43, $1F7F). The spawn at $0997 sets it from the player position $47/$48 when $7A is zero, and the movers at $43BC and $440A subtract from and add to it; loaded handlers also store it. The world builder at $1B5B does not use it: it keeps its computed X in $1DC4/$1DC5.

Seventeen per-entity high bytes of the screen-relative X coordinate, paired with low bytes at $195D. The display builders consume these with the indexed low byte; the high-byte value is distinct from the world-coordinate high byte at $193B.

Seventeen-byte entity array for the world Y high byte, indexed by entity slot. The ten-byte record copier at $369E installs record byte 4 here. The record loaders $1863 and $3622 fill slots 1 to the load's limit $4DBA, at most 9 (CPX $4DBA at $18CB and $3629), and spawned entities take the slots 16 down to 0 that the free-slot search $190B finds.

Seventeen-byte entity array for the world Y low byte, indexed by entity slot. The ten-byte record copier at $369E installs record byte 5 here. The record loaders $1863 and $3622 fill slots 1 to the load's limit $4DBA, at most 9 (CPX $4DBA at $18CB and $3629), and spawned entities take the slots 16 down to 0 that the free-slot search $190B finds.

Seventeen per-entity screen Y bytes, read by the direct display builder at $1DC8 ($1E99, $1ED7, $1F34, $1F70). The spawn at $09A1 sets the byte from the player Y $49 when $7A is zero; the movers at $3617, $435C and $4382 subtract from and add to it, and loaded handlers store it. The world builder at $1B5B does not use it: it computes Y from $197F/$1990 into $1DC6/$1DC7.

Seventeen per-entity flags, zero or nonzero, marking an entity that is placed by the screen coordinates $195D/$196E/$19A1. The spawn at $09A6 and loaded handlers store 1; record loading ($188A, $3654, $368D), $18FE and the release at $446E clear it. The direct display builder skips a slot whose byte is zero ($1DCF), and when $7A is zero so do the update loop ($1FED) and the contact scan ($74EA). Every reader tests only zero against nonzero.
Seventeen primary sprite-frame bytes, indexed by entity slot. The display builder uses this field for the first layer; loaded type handlers can update it separately from the base frame at $19E5.
Seventeen secondary sprite-frame bytes, indexed by entity slot. The display builder uses this field for the second layer, alongside the primary frame at $19C3.

Seventeen-byte entity array for the base sprite frame, indexed by entity slot. The ten-byte record copier at $369E installs record byte 1 here. The record loaders $1863 and $3622 fill slots 1 to the load's limit $4DBA, at most 9 (CPX $4DBA at $18CB and $3629), and spawned entities take the slots 16 down to 0 that the free-slot search $190B finds.

Seventeen-byte entity array for the first display attribute, indexed by entity slot. The ten-byte record copier at $369E installs record byte 6 here. The record loaders $1863 and $3622 fill slots 1 to the load's limit $4DBA, at most 9 (CPX $4DBA at $18CB and $3629), and spawned entities take the slots 16 down to 0 that the free-slot search $190B finds.

Seventeen second display-attribute bytes, indexed by entity slot. Record initialization clears the selected slot; the display builder consumes this runtime attribute separately from the first and third attributes copied from the record.

Seventeen-byte entity array for the third display attribute, indexed by entity slot. The ten-byte record copier at $369E installs record byte 7 here. The record loaders $1863 and $3622 fill slots 1 to the load's limit $4DBA, at most 9 (CPX $4DBA at $18CB and $3629), and spawned entities take the slots 16 down to 0 that the free-slot search $190B finds. The callback path at $68D9 also uses this byte as a target low byte, paired with the byte at $1A6D,X.

Seventeen first display-slot indexes. $1902 reads the indexed byte and returns carry clear for zero, or carry set with A holding the nonzero slot index. Allocation, display building and release share this field.
Seventeen second display-slot indexes. The two-layer entity display path reads this separately from the first index at $1A29; the record copier clears both before later allocation.
Seventeen third display-slot indexes used by the optional additional display layers. The record copier clears this indexed byte along with the other three display-slot fields.
Seventeen fourth display-slot indexes used by the optional additional display layers. The record copier clears this indexed byte; it is separate from the third index at $1A4B.

Seventeen-byte entity array for the type-dependent parameter, indexed by entity slot. The ten-byte record copier at $369E installs record byte 9 here. The record loaders $1863 and $3622 fill slots 1 to the load's limit $4DBA, at most 9 (CPX $4DBA at $18CB and $3629), and spawned entities take the slots 16 down to 0 that the free-slot search $190B finds. The path at $68DF uses it as a callback high byte, while the contact-health path at $74C0 subtracts damage from the same indexed storage.

Seventeen fall-speed bytes, one per entity slot. While $1A7E,X is nonzero the update loop at $2019 calls $44C7, which moves the entity down by that amount through $44DE and then stores 1 if it landed (carry set) or one more than before, 8 staying 8, if it is still falling. Zero means the entity does not fall: the slot set-ups at $18B1, $3657 and $3690 and $447A's clear at $4499 store 0, and type handlers start a fall by storing 1 when the byte is zero (for example $420D, $605D and $6091, and load 1's $B1E9).

Seventeen display-effect bytes. Initialization clears the selected slot and the display builders test the field when selecting colour/effect paths. The meaning of a value depends on the consuming path.
Seventeen entity animation countdown bytes. The record-loading path initializes the selected byte to 0 for type $FF and 7 for other types; animation paths subsequently update it.

Seventeen per-entity bytes for type-specific working field 1. Slot zero is cleared by $18D8; loaded handlers give the field its meaning. For example, load 25 reads this array at $9C84, where it is used as the dispatch index. A role established in one handler does not apply automatically to every entity type.

Seventeen per-entity bytes for type-specific working field 2. Slot zero is cleared by $18D8; loaded handlers give the field its meaning. For example, load 25 reads this array at $A106, where it is decremented as the state-4 timer. A role established in one handler does not apply automatically to every entity type.

Seventeen per-entity bytes for type-specific working field 3. Slot zero is cleared by $18D8; loaded handlers give the field its meaning. For example, load 25 reads this array at $A098, where it is decremented in the type-$1E state-2 path. A role established in one handler does not apply automatically to every entity type.

Seventeen per-entity bytes for type-specific working field 4. Slot zero is cleared by $18D8; loaded handlers give the field its meaning. For example, load 25 reads this array at $A122, where it is copied back to the current state. A role established in one handler does not apply automatically to every entity type.

Seventeen per-entity bytes for type-specific working field 5. Slot zero is cleared by $18D8; loaded handlers give the field its meaning. For example, load 25 reads this array at $9D53, where it is read as a type-$05 working counter. A role established in one handler does not apply automatically to every entity type.

Seventeen per-entity bytes for type-specific working field 6. Slot zero is cleared by $18D8; loaded handlers give the field its meaning. For example, load 25 reads this array at $9D66, where it is decremented by a type-$05 handler. A role established in one handler does not apply automatically to every entity type.

Seventeen per-entity bytes for type-specific working field 7. Slot zero is cleared by $18D8; loaded handlers give the field its meaning. For example, load 25 reads this array at $9CAA, where it is read by the type-$05 initialization path. A role established in one handler does not apply automatically to every entity type.

Seventeen per-entity bytes for type-specific working field 8. Slot zero is cleared by $18D8; loaded handlers give the field its meaning. For example, load 25 reads this array at $9F8E, where it is read by the type-$1E state-0 path. A role established in one handler does not apply automatically to every entity type.
Seventeen entity record-index bytes. After copying a record, the loader stores the current entity slot number here with TXA/STA; record-reload paths subsequently use the indexed value.

Seventeen entity reload-counter bytes. The record-loading paths clear the selected slot after installing a record ($188D, $3651). The reload at $367D increments it each time the slot is refilled from its saved record and adds half the new count to the record's last byte for $1A6D,X; $5DCE reads it to choose a handler table, and releases the entity at 2 or more. No loaded code references it.
Transforms world-relative entity positions into display-slot state, allocates or releases slot pairs and updates sprite coordinates, frames and colours.

Store the first free display slot, found by the search at $1C22 from slot 31 down to 0, as the entity's first link $1A29,X, then search on from the slot below it for the second. Slot 0 is the life meter, whose Y $6B14 sets to $40. If the first search ever stopped at slot 0, DEY would wrap Y to $FF and $4CCF,Y would read $4DCE, the second player's life meter (the load holds $00): unless that byte is $FF, the next DEY leaves Y negative and the search gives up through $1C3E; if it is $FF, $1C42 records $FF as the second link.

Use $1A29,X as the first display slot. Store bit 0 of $192A,X at $4CEF,Y. If $1A8F,X is negative, toggle its low bit and use Y position $FE when that bit is set; otherwise use $1DC6. Copy $1DC5/$1DC4 to the slot coordinates, $19C3,X plus 1 to its pointer, $19F6,X to its colour and 1 to $4C2F,Y.
Use $1A3A,X as the second display slot. Store bit 0 of $192A,X at $4CEF,Y, use the same blink and position fields, and store $19C3,X as its pointer.

If $1A8F,X is positive, save the slot index in the immediate operand at $1D02, decrement the effect byte, use its previous value minus 1 as an index at $1FBA and restore the slot index. Otherwise use colour 7 when $1AA0,X is nonzero or $1A07,X when it is zero.
Immediate operand of LDY at $1D01, patched by $1CF6 to restore the second primary display slot after indexing the colour table.
Skip the secondary pair when $1919,X is $FF or bit 0 of $192A,X is clear; otherwise proceed to the third display slot.

Use $1A4B,X as the third display slot. Apply the blink test, use $1DC6 plus 21 for its visible Y, and copy the same coordinates. Store $19D4,X plus 1 as its pointer, $1A18,X as its colour and 1 at $4C2F,Y and $4CEF,Y.
Use $1A5C,X as the fourth display slot. Apply the blink and secondary-position rules and store $19D4,X as its pointer.

If $1A8F,X is positive, save the slot index at $1DA4, index $1FBA with the effect byte and restore the slot. Otherwise use colour 7 when $1AA0,X is nonzero or $1A07,X when it is zero. The first primary pair can already have decremented the effect byte.
Immediate operand of LDY at $1DA3, patched by $1D9C to restore the fourth display slot after indexing the colour table.
Store the selected fourth-slot colour, clear $4C2F,Y, set $4CEF,Y to 1 and jump to $1B62.

Low byte of the entity’s computed screen X coordinate. Referenced in the resident code at $1BDD (STA), $1BF4 (LDA), $1BFA (STA), $1C09 (LDA), $1C13 (LDA), $1CA5 (LDA), $1CE3 (LDA), $1D4D (LDA), $1D89 (LDA).
High byte paired with $1DC4 for the computed screen X coordinate. Referenced in the resident code at $1BE6 (STA), $1BFD (LDA), $1C02 (STA), $1C9F (LDA), $1CDD (LDA), $1D47 (LDA), $1D83 (LDA).
Low byte of the entity’s computed screen Y coordinate. Referenced in the resident code at $1BB8 (STA), $1BCB (LDA), $1C99 (LDA), $1CD7 (LDA), $1D3E (LDA), $1D7A (LDA).
High byte paired with $1DC6 for the computed screen Y coordinate. Referenced at $1BC1 (STA), $1BC6 (LDA).
Updates display-slot state for entities using direct coordinates, including allocation, release and optional second pairs. Slot availability and indexes are runtime state.

Use $1A29,X as the first display slot and store bit 0 of $192A,X at $4CEF,Y. If $1A8F,X is negative, toggle its low bit and use Y position $FE when that bit is set; otherwise use $19A1,X. Copy $196E,X/$195D,X to the slot coordinates, $19C3,X plus 1 to its pointer, $19F6,X to its colour and 1 to $4C2F,Y.
Use $1A3A,X as the second display slot. Store bit 0 of $192A,X at $4CEF,Y, use the same blink and position fields, and store $19C3,X as its pointer.

If $1A8F,X is positive, save the slot index in the immediate operand at $1F02, decrement the effect byte, use its previous value minus 1 as an index at $1FBA and restore the slot index. Otherwise use colour 7 when $1AA0,X is nonzero or $1A07,X when it is zero.
Immediate operand of LDY at $1F01, patched by $1EF6 to restore the second display slot after indexing the colour table.
Skip the secondary pair when bit 0 of $192A,X is clear; otherwise proceed to the third display slot. Unlike the world-position path, this check does not inspect $1919,X.

Use $1A4B,X as the third display slot. Apply the blink test, use $19A1,X plus 21 for its visible Y, and copy the same coordinates. Store $19D4,X plus 1 as its pointer, $1A18,X as its colour and 1 at $4C2F,Y and $4CEF,Y.
Use $1A5C,X as the fourth display slot. Apply the blink and secondary-position rules and store $19D4,X as its pointer.

If $1A8F,X is positive, save the slot index at $1F9A, index $1FBA with the effect byte and restore the slot. Otherwise use colour 7 when $1AA0,X is nonzero or $1A07,X when it is zero. The first pair can already have decremented the effect byte.
Immediate operand of LDY at $1F99, patched by $1F92 to restore the fourth display slot after indexing the colour table.
Store the selected fourth-slot colour, clear $4C2F,Y, set $4CEF,Y to 1 and jump to $1DD7.

Eight flash colours, alternately 0 (black) and $0B (dark grey), for the second sprite of each pair while $1A8F,X is positive. $1CFE and $1EFE index it with the effect byte minus 1 and decrement the byte; $1DA0 and $1F96 index it with the byte after that decrement; each stores the result to $4CAF,Y. The contact handler at $74CF sets the byte to 8, giving indices 7 down to 0. The lookups have no bound: load 31 sets the byte to $20 at $968A, and the indices from 31 down then read $1FC2 and the instruction bytes at $1FC3-$1FD9 as colours.

One byte, $00, after the eight flash colours at $1FBA. No instruction names it. The colour lookups at $1CFE, $1DA0, $1EFE and $1F96 reach it with index 8: the resident never asks for that (its effect byte starts at 8, indices 7 to 0), but load 31 sets $1A8F,X to $20 at $968A and the countdown then passes through index 8, reading this byte as colour 0.

Update the entities once a pass. When $7A is zero and the effect cursor $4D50 is positive, update each of the eight effect objects whose $4D21 flag is zero ($3EC6) and then the group at $3F76. Then scan entity slots 16 down to 0: skip type 0, and in world mode $7A zero an entity whose $19B2,X is zero; run the frame countdown $1AA0,X; call the fall step $44C7 while $1A7E,X is nonzero; then call the type's handler, a positive type's from the load's tables at $7EDF/$7F0F (JSR $2036) or a negative type's from $2062/$2074 (JSR $204E). After slot 0 jump to $3622, which refills empty slots from the load's entity records.
Read the low byte of the handler address for this positive entity type from the load's table at $7EDF,Y (Y is the type from $1919,X) and patch it into the low operand byte of the JSR at $2036.
Read the high byte of the handler address for this positive entity type from the load's table at $7F0F,Y and patch it into the high operand byte of the JSR at $2036.

Call the positive entity type's handler: $202A and $2030 patch the operand from the load's tables $7EDF,Y and $7F0F,Y, with Y the type from $1919,X, and A holds the entity's first display slot $1A29,X. The load holds JSR $FF00 here.

Low byte of the target of the JSR at $2036, whose high byte is $2038. The load holds $00 here, so the instruction reads JSR $FF00 until it is patched. $202A stores it from the load's handler table at $7EDF,Y and $2030 the high byte from $7F0F,Y, with Y the positive entity type; the call passes A=$1A29,X. No other instruction writes it.

High operand byte of the positive-type JSR at $2036. Its low byte is $2037. After return jump to the next-slot scan $1FE3. The separate negative-type path at $203C computes the two’s-complement magnitude into Y before indexing its tables.
Read the low call-target byte from $2062,Y and store it at $204F. The following high-byte lookup uses $2074,Y; together they patch the JSR at $204E.
Read the high call-target byte from $2074,Y and store it at $2050, pairing it with the low byte at $204F for JSR $204E.

Store the high byte read from $2074,Y at $2050, completing the operand of the JSR at $204E; $2045 stored the low byte from $2062,Y, with Y the negated entity type. The bytes as loaded read JSR $FF00 until the first patch.

Low byte of the target of the JSR at $204E, whose high byte is $2050. The load holds $00 here, so the instruction reads JSR $FF00 until it is patched. $2045 stores it from $2062,Y and $204B the high byte from $2074,Y, with Y the negated entity type. No other instruction writes it.
High byte of the negative-type JSR at $204E, paired with $204F. When the selected handler returns, jump to the next entity scan at $1FE3.

Entries 0 and 1 of the countdown frame table indexed at $2001, both $AB. The countdown path at $1FF2 never selects them: a countdown of 0 skips the path and a countdown of 1 reaches zero and restores the base frame at $200D instead, so the lookup takes indices 2 to 6 only.

Entries 2–6 of the countdown frame table at $2054: $AB, $AB, $A9, $A9 and $A7. $2001 reads $2054,Y with Y the countdown $1AA0,X before $1FF7 decrements it, which is 2 to 6 there, so a countdown of 6 shows frame $A7, 5 and 4 show $A9, and 3 and 2 show $AB, stored as both sprite frames $19C3,X and $19D4,X.
Entry 7 of the countdown frame table at $2054, $A7. The countdown path does not select it: $1FFC skips the lookup when the countdown before the decrement is 7 or more.
Increment the border colour register $D020 and jump back to $205C indefinitely. This local loop has no return or input test.

Eighteen low bytes of the negative-type handler table, paired with the high bytes at $2074 and indexed at $2042 by the negated entity type: $FF goes to $68CB, $FE to $41EE, $FD to $4250, $FC to $4BBC, $FB to $4C1A, $FA and $F5–$EF to $603F, $F9 and $F8 to $6086, and $F7 and $F6 to the endless border flash at $205C. Entry 0, $0000, is never read: only a negative type reaches $203C.

Eighteen high bytes of the negative-type handler table, paired with the low bytes at $2062: $2048 reads $2074,Y with Y the negated entity type, and $204B stores it at $2050, the high byte of the JSR at $204E. The pairs send $FF to $68CB, $FE to $41EE, $FD to $4250, $FC to $4BBC, $FB to $4C1A, $FA and $F5–$EF to $603F, $F9 and $F8 to $6086, and $F7 and $F6 to $205C. The first pair, $0000, is never read, since only a negative type reaches $203C.
Mirrors pairs of sprite images: one representation reverses individual bits and its companion reverses two-bit groups. It uses patched immediates to preserve indices.

For one row of the first 63-byte source sprite, visit byte offsets 2, 1 and 0. Reverse the eight bits of each byte and write it to the opposite byte offset in the destination row; $213B contains the byte-order table.
Saved row-byte index restored into Y by $20C3. Store the reversed byte through ($52),Y, map the index through $213B,Y and decrement it to continue the first-plane row while nonnegative.

Add $40 to both source and destination pointers to select the companion sprites. For the same three byte positions, reverse the order of the four two-bit groups in each byte and write to the opposite byte offset.

Saved row-byte index restored into Y by $2107 for the multicolour companion. Store the reversed pair-order byte through ($52),Y, map the index through $213B,Y and decrement it to continue the row while nonnegative.

Subtract $3D from each pointer, moving from the companion row to the next row in the first sprite. Repeat for 21 rows, then load the saved source and destination indices, increment each twice and return.
Saved source-sprite index operand restored by LDX at $2132. Increment X twice before restoring the destination index at $2136, advancing beyond the two mirrored planes.
Saved destination-sprite index operand restored by LDY at $2136. Increment Y twice and return after the pair of sprite planes has been mirrored.

Byte-order map $02,$01,$00 used by sprite mirroring. $20B2 and $20EE read it to find the destination byte for the source byte being reversed, and $20C7 and $210B read it again to get back to the source index. It exchanges the left and right bytes of each 24-pixel row and keeps the middle byte in place.
Tests downward player movement against a candidate entity and can shorten the step, record the entity index and set support state. Arithmetic uses 8-bit values and carry.
Immediate operand of ADC at $219A, patched by $2173 with the selected horizontal contact width. The following comparison skips the candidate when the player lies beyond the computed upper bound.

Add $14 plus the carry left set by the successful horizontal comparison to player Y. Equal to the display-slot Y takes the zero-step path; greater or equal skips the candidate. Otherwise add the vertical step and 3 with carry as produced by the preceding instructions, and skip if still below the slot Y. For contact, set the step to slot Y minus player Y minus $15 modulo 256.

Clear downward-move, vertical-animation and vertical-motion state, store entity flags OR 2 as support flags, record the entity index and return. This continuation is reached with A=0 from either contact path.
The preceding LDA #0 sets Z and STA preserves it, so this BEQ is unconditional. The following bytes at $21df–$21e0 are scratch data, not fall-through instructions.
Player half-X coordinate saved for the platform contact comparison; dividing coordinates by two fits the comparison in a byte. Referenced at $2178 (STA), $217E (ROR), $2194 (CMP), $219C (CMP).
Scratch byte holding the selected entity display-slot X coordinate shifted right one bit for the contact check at $2173.

Save caller X in immediate operand $21EE. Index the selected player with $4DBD, AND incoming A with that player’s flags at $4DE2,X, store the result through $21EA and restore X at $21ED. Y is unchanged.
Restore X from the immediate operand patched by either flag-update entry.

Immediate operand of the LDX at $21ED, which restores the caller's X before the RTS at $21EF. $21E1 (in $21E1, which ANDs A into the selected player's flags $4DE2,X) and $21F0 (in $21F0, which ORs A into them) store the caller's X here before X is loaded from $4DBD; no other instruction writes it. The load holds $FF here.
Return from the selected-player flag update after restoring X at $21ED.
Save caller X in immediate operand $21EE, index the selected player from $4DBD and OR incoming A with $4DE2,X. Jump to the shared store at $21EA, which writes the new flags and restores caller X.
Shift A right four times, yielding the original high nibble as a value from 0 to 15. X and Y are unchanged; carry holds original bit 3.
Three-voice SID sequencer: selects or initializes pointer lists, advances event streams and updates voice registers. Several counters and branch operands are modified in place.
