Voice 1, offset 0 of its record in the first bank: low byte of the pointer to the pattern being played, set by the list reader at $22F5 and copied to $4E at $230B. The first bank is three seven-byte records one after another, for voices 1, 2 and 3 at $2225, $222C and $2233; the sequencer indexes them with X or Y = 0, 7 and 14.

Voice 1, offset 1 of its record in the first bank: high byte of the pointer to the pattern being played, set at $22FB and copied to $4F at $2310. The first bank is three seven-byte records one after another, for voices 1, 2 and 3 at $2225, $222C and $2233; the sequencer indexes them with X or Y = 0, 7 and 14.

Voice 1, offset 2 of its record in the first bank: low byte of the pointer to the voice's list of pattern addresses, set at $2259-$2277 or $2297 when a sequence starts and read by the list reader at $22DF. The first bank is three seven-byte records one after another, for voices 1, 2 and 3 at $2225, $222C and $2233; the sequencer indexes them with X or Y = 0, 7 and 14.

Voice 1, offset 3 of its record in the first bank: high byte of the pointer to the voice's list of pattern addresses, read by the list reader at $22E4. The first bank is three seven-byte records one after another, for voices 1, 2 and 3 at $2225, $222C and $2233; the sequencer indexes them with X or Y = 0, 7 and 14.

Voice 1, offset 4 of its record in the first bank: instrument number, the low five bits of an event byte of $C0 or more ($2350); it indexes the parameter tables at $2401-$2428. Low-nibble display code produced by the packed-nibble splitter. Referenced in the resident code at $02B6 (LDA), $02C8 (LDA), $02DA (LDA), $36F3 (STY), $390A (LDA), $391C (LDA), $392E (LDA), $3A46 (LDA), $3A58 (LDA), $3A6A (LDA), $3B02 (LDA), $3B14 (LDA), $3B26 (LDA), $531D (LDA), $5363 (LDA), $7740 (LDA), $7798 (LDA). 54 instructions in 18 loads also use it, the first at $A520 in load 1.

Increment the byte at $3718 and test its low bit. Even values branch to status-panel update $3719; odd values jump to amount-and-score display $3897. Thus these two display paths alternate per call, without this entry alone establishing a frame rate.
HUD alternation counter incremented at $370B; its low bit selects which display path runs. Referenced at $370B (INC), $370E (LDA).

Update the selected player’s status panel. When the message countdown at $4D6B is nonzero, copy five rows of message cells and colours from $4EE4–$4F7D; otherwise compare the player’s flags at $4DE2,Y with the cache at $4DAD and, on a change, call $408A and copy the status rows. Continue at $37C2 to check the remaining fields.

Immediate operand of LDA at $3868, patched by $3860 with the current meter threshold. After loading it, add 8 with carry clear, increment X and continue testing segments at $385B; when X reaches 5, replace X with $28 before continuing. The separate exit at $3877 jumps to the meter sprite update.

Number of hearts beyond the first five. When the meter limit $4DCF,Y divided by 8 is at least 6, $380D stores that quotient minus 5 here. $382D reloads it, capped at 5, as the number of second-row cells from $C079 that $3838 fills with glyph $17. Referenced at $380D (STA), $382D (LDX).

Seven character codes, $19, five of $18 and $1A, for the second meter row. When the meter limit is six hearts or more, $3812 copies them to screen cells $C078–$C07E; $3838 then writes glyph $17 over one to five of the middle cells, and the loop at $385B writes $7B over the filled ones. The rows at $3889 and $3890 hold the matching colours.

Seven character codes, $14, five of $15 and $16, for the row under the meter. With a limit of six hearts or more $381E copies them to screen cells $C0A0–$C0A6; with a smaller limit $3848 copies them to $C078–$C07E and $3845 clears $C0A0–$C0A6. The rows at $3889 and $3890 hold the matching colours.

Seven colour-RAM values, $0F, five of $07 and $0F, for the second meter row. When the meter limit is six hearts or more, $3818 copies them to $D878–$D87E, the colour cells of the characters copied from $387B.

Seven colour-RAM values, all $0F, for the row under the meter. With a limit of six hearts or more $3824 copies them to $D8A0–$D8A6; with a smaller limit $384E copies them to $D878–$D87E. They colour the characters copied from $3882.

Refresh the selected player’s four-digit amount and score display. Compare the packed digits at $4DC7,Y and $4DC9,Y with their cached values; on a change, split them into nibbles, add $24 to form screen codes at $C059–$C05C, and blank up to three leading zeroes. Continue at $38F3 to update the meter and select a score display.
Split the first player’s three packed score bytes at $4DC1, $4DC3 and $4DC5 into six nibble-plus-one glyph indexes at $3BAC–$3BB1, most significant byte first, then suppress leading zeroes.
Replace each leading glyph index 1 among the first five digits with blank glyph 0, stopping at the first other index. Keep the sixth digit even when the entire score is zero.

For each of the first three glyph indexes, compare against the corresponding cached index at $4DA6–$4DA8. Only a changed index is cached and drawn through $39E7, to $D819, $D81A or $D858 respectively.
Compare the fourth and fifth glyph indexes with the cached values at $4DA9–$4DAA. A change updates the corresponding cache and draws that glyph at $D859 or $D85A.
Compare the sixth glyph index with the cache at $4DAB and draw it at $D898 only when changed. Draw fixed glyph 1 at $D899 on every visit, then continue to the record-or-alternate score selection.

Set $01 to $30, multiply A by eight with eight-bit wrap and copy eight rows from the $C800 character set to the address patched into $39FA, writing destination offsets 0, 3, 6, 9, 12, 15, 18 and 21. Restore $01 to $35 before returning; the caller supplies the glyph index and destination.
Low address operand of STA at $39FA. Paired with $39FC, it selects the destination of the glyph-copy rows written with a stride of three bytes.
High byte of the writable destination address in STA at $39FA. After a glyph-row store, increment X three times and Y once, then compare Y with the patched end operand at $3A02.
Immediate operand of CPY at $3A01. The glyph-copy routine patches it with the start index plus eight, modulo 256, to stop after eight rows.

If $4DBC is zero, compare the three record-score bytes at $4DBE–$4DC0 against the cache at $4DA3–$4DA5. Return without redrawing if all three match; otherwise update the cache and decode the score. If $4DBC is nonzero, jump to the second-player branch at $3AF0.
Copy the record-score bytes into the cache and split each packed byte into two nibble-plus-one glyph indexes at $3BAC–$3BB1, most significant byte first. Continue to leading-zero suppression.
Walk the first five glyph indexes at $3BAC: turn each leading value 1 into glyph 0 and stop at the first value other than 1. The sixth position is left intact so a zero score still has a zero digit.

Draw the six record-score glyphs through $39E7 at $D8D9, $D8DA, $D918, $D919, $D91A and $D958; then draw glyph 1 at $D959. Each address is the start of eight bytes written three apart under the I/O area.
When $4DBD is zero, return. Otherwise decode the three alternate score bytes at $4DC2, $4DC4 and $4DC6 into six glyph indexes and draw them in the same seven destinations used by the record score.
Split the three alternate-score packed bytes into six nibble-plus-one glyph indexes at $3BAC–$3BB1, most significant byte first, then suppress leading zeroes.
Walk the first five alternate-score glyph indexes, replacing each leading index 1 with blank glyph 0 until a different index appears. Leave the sixth index untouched.
Draw the alternate score using glyphs $3BAC–$3BB1 at $D8D9, $D8DA, $D918, $D919, $D91A and $D958. Draw fixed glyph 1 at $D959; $39E7 banks out I/O for each column copy.
Six 1-based digit codes reused when displaying player scores and the record.
Decoded score digit 2 retained by the score formatter before drawing.
Decoded score digit 3 retained by the score formatter before drawing.
Decoded score digit 4 retained by the score formatter before drawing.
Decoded score digit 5 retained by the score formatter before drawing.
Decoded score digit 6 retained by the score formatter before drawing.

First of the three title-screen raster interrupt stages, which the title set-up at $030C and the third stage at $3C17 install through the trampoline $5E/$5F with raster $5A: save A in the operand at $3BCD, acknowledge the VIC interrupt, set background colour 2 ($D023) to 9, point the trampoline at the second stage $3BCF with raster $91, then reload A and return with RTI at $3BCE.
Write low byte $CF to $5E, then high byte $3B to $5F, setting the IRQ trampoline target to $3BCF. The target is a code address; these two stores do not by themselves measure an interrupt interval.
Write $3B to the IRQ target high byte at $5F. The preceding low-byte store sets $5E to $CF, so the pair selects $3BCF.
Saved A immediate byte loaded by the raster-return instruction at $3BCC; the following RTI restores processor flags and the interrupted address.
Return from the first raster handler with RTI, after its saved A has been restored.

Second raster IRQ stage: switch character data and schedule the third stage; A and Y are restored from patched immediate operands. Save the interrupted A register into the immediate operand at the end of this IRQ stage. Save the interrupted Y register into the immediate operand at the end of this IRQ stage.
Write low byte $0A to $5E, then high byte $3C to $5F, setting the IRQ trampoline target to $3C0A. The target is a code address; these two stores do not by themselves measure an interrupt interval.
Write $3C to the IRQ target high byte at $5F. The preceding low-byte store sets $5E to $0A, so the pair selects $3C0A.
Saved A immediate operand for the second raster-handler return, patched by $3BCF.
Saved Y immediate operand for the second raster-handler return, patched by $3BD2.
RTI at the end of the second raster handler, after restoring A and Y.
Third raster IRQ stage: restore character data, schedule the first stage and increment the cycle counter. Save the interrupted A register into the immediate operand at the end of this IRQ stage.
Write low byte $B2 to $5E, then high byte $3B to $5F, setting the IRQ trampoline target to $3BB2. The target is a code address; these two stores do not by themselves measure an interrupt interval.
Write $3B to the IRQ target high byte at $5F. The preceding low-byte store sets $5E to $B2, so the pair selects $3BB2.
Saved A immediate operand for the third raster-handler return, patched by $3C0A.
RTI at the end of the third raster handler, after restoring A.

If $5275 is zero, call the message-panel copy at $4828. Read counter $526C and repeat from $3C2A while it is below 3; once it reaches at least 3, clear $526C and return. A counter already at the threshold does not require a further increment; the message copy still runs first when $5275 is zero.
Wait until the raster counter is at least 3, then clear it. If it is already at or above the threshold, return without waiting.
Samples active-low joystick port 2, preserves previous values, and reads a CIA1 keyboard row whose Fire bit is shared with joystick port 1.
Gates and dispatches the Fire-action state machine. The mode controls patched jump targets and the code responds to input edges and held directional values.
Replace the low byte of the input-handler jump.
Replace the high byte of the input-handler jump.

Jump to the fire-action handler for the state $3D4A, whose address $3CB3 and $3CB9 patch in from $3D4B,Y and $3D4E,Y: $3CBF for state 0, $3CEA for 1 and $3CFB for 2. Every store to $3D4A writes 0, 1 or 2 ($3CD7, $3CEC, $3D08, $3D29, $3D34 and $3D45).

Low byte of the target of the JMP at $3CBC, whose high byte is $3CBE. The load holds $00 here, so the instruction reads JMP $FF00 until it is patched. $3CB3 stores it from $3D4B,Y and $3CB9 the high byte from $3D4E,Y, with Y the input mode $3D4A, so the jump goes to $3CBF, $3CEA or $3CFB. No other instruction writes it.

High byte of the target of the JMP at $3CBC, whose low byte is $3CBD. The load holds $FF here, so the instruction reads JMP $FF00 until it is patched. $3CB9 stores it from $3D4E,Y and $3CB3 the low byte from $3D4B,Y, with Y the input mode $3D4A, so the jump goes to $3CBF (the next instruction), $3CEA or $3CFB. No other instruction writes it.

Fire-action state 0, reached through the table at $3D4B: look for a new Fire press. The sampled inputs are zero while pressed. Return when Fire was already down at the previous sample ($78 is zero). With Fire up now, write $FF to $4DB7 and return. On a new press with Down held ($72 is zero), clear the latch at $4DBB and return. Otherwise set the action state at $3D4A and the contact budget at $5285 to 1, clear $4DB7 and select sprite frame $6C plus the offset byte at $1177 by storing the sum at $4A.
Countdown used by the fire/action state dispatcher. Referenced at $3CEF (STX), $3CFB (LDA), $3D02 (DEC), $3D38 (DEC).
Index selecting the fire/action state handler. Referenced in the resident code at $3CAD (LDY), $3CD7 (STX), $3CEC (STX), $3D08 (STA), $3D29 (STA), $3D34 (STA), $3D45 (STA).
Three low bytes of the fire-action handler addresses $3CBF, $3CEA and $3CFB, indexed by the state at $3D4A and paired with the high bytes at $3D4E.
Three high bytes paired with the input-handler target lows at $3D4B.

Handler of entity type $27. Load its state $1AB1,X into Y for the split-table dispatch at $3D54: state 0 goes to $3D69, 1 to $3D7F and 2 to $3D9F. These are the only states: the spawn at $0952 starts the entity with state 0, which $4454 cleared, and $3D7B and $3D84 step it to 1 and 2.
Patch the low byte of the dispatch target from the entity-state table.
Patch the high byte of the dispatch target from the entity-state table.

Store the high byte from $3D66,Y at $3D62, completing the JMP at $3D60. Y is the entity's state $1AB1,X, and the tables send state 0 to $3D69, 1 to $3D7F and 2 to $3D9F. Those are the only states this type's code produces: the slot is set up with state 0, and $3D7B and $3D84 step it to 1 and 2.

Low byte of the target of the JMP at $3D60, whose high byte is $3D62. The load holds $00 here, so the instruction reads JMP $FF00 until it is patched. $3D57 stores it from $3D63,Y and $3D5D the high byte from $3D66,Y, with Y the entity state $1AB1,X, so the jump goes to $3D69, $3D7F or $3D9F. No other instruction writes it.

High byte of the target of the JMP at $3D60, whose low byte is $3D61. The load holds $FF here, so the instruction reads JMP $FF00 until it is patched. $3D5D stores it from $3D66,Y and $3D57 the low byte from $3D63,Y, with Y the entity state $1AB1,X, so the jump goes to $3D69, $3D7F or $3D9F. No other instruction writes it.
Three low bytes of the entity-mode state-dispatch table, paired with high bytes at $3D66.
Three high bytes paired with state target lows at $3D63. The entry $3D51 loads the state into Y before the lookup.
Set $1AF5,X to $FC, $1B17,X to zero and $1B28,X to $32. Call $3EA8, increment $1AB1,X and return.
If $1B17,X is nonzero, enter $3D84. Otherwise call $3E60, call $3E94 with A=4, and call $3E88. A carry-set result enters $3D84; carry clear tail-jumps to $3E54.
Increment $1AB1,X, set $1AC2,X to 2 and tail-jump to $3D9F.

Load Y from $1AC2,X. If it is zero, tail-jump to $3E5A. Otherwise set $1A07,X to 7, copy $3DB6,Y to $19C3,X, decrement $1AC2,X and return. Y is 2 and then 1: $3D89 sets the count to 2 on entering this state, and at zero $3E5A removes the entity, so entry 0 of the table is never read.

Frames for state 2 of the entity handled at $3D51: $3D9F reads $3DB6,Y with Y the countdown $1AC2,X, which $3D89 sets to 2, and stores the byte as the sprite frame $19C3,X, so the entity shows frame $A9 and then $A7 before $3E5A removes it at zero. Entry 0, $00, is never read.
If $1B17,X is nonzero, tail-jump to $3E5A. Otherwise, if $1B28,X is nonzero, call $35C1 with that byte in A and tail-jump to $3E54. A zero byte enters trajectory initialization at $3DCF.
Copy $1AC2,X and $1AD3,X to $35BD and $35BE. Read the display-slot index from $1A29,X; return if it is zero, otherwise use it as Y and enter $3DE1.
Shift $4CCF,Y right once into $35C0. Shift the low nine bits of $4C4F,Y:$4C6F,Y right once into $35BF. Call $34EA, OR the returned A with $C0, store it in $1B28,X and tail-jump to $35C1.
Patch the low byte of the dispatch target from the entity-state table. At $3E02, load A from $3E11,Y and write it to $3E0F.
Patch the high byte of the dispatch target from the entity-state table. At $3E08, load A from $3E13,Y and write it to $3E10.

Store the high byte from $3E13,Y at $3E10, completing the JMP at $3E0E. Y is the entity's state $1AB1,X, and the tables send state 0 to $3E15 and 1 to $3E2B. Those are the only states this type's code produces: the slot is set up with state 0, and $3E27 steps it to 1.

Low byte of the target of the JMP at $3E0E, whose high byte is $3E10. The load holds $00 here, so the instruction reads JMP $FF00 until it is patched. $3E05 stores it from $3E11,Y and $3E0B the high byte from $3E13,Y, with Y the entity state $1AB1,X, so the jump goes to $3E15 or $3E2B. No other instruction writes it.

High byte of the target of the JMP at $3E0E, whose low byte is $3E0F. The load holds $FF here, so the instruction reads JMP $FF00 until it is patched. $3E0B stores it from $3E13,Y and $3E05 the low byte from $3E11,Y, with Y the entity state $1AB1,X, so the jump goes to $3E15 or $3E2B. No other instruction writes it.
Two low bytes of the secondary entity dispatch table, paired with high bytes at $3E13.
Two high bytes paired with secondary dispatch target lows at $3E11.
Set $1AF5,X to $FC, $1B17,X to zero and $1B28,X to $5A. Call $3EA8, increment $1AB1,X and return.
If $1B17,X is nonzero, call $3E7F to toggle direction and clear $1B17,X. In either case continue at $3E38.
Call $3E60, call $3E94 with A=5, then call $3E88. If the countdown returns carry set, branch to $3E5A. Otherwise add bit 1 of $1B28,X to $19E5,X, store it in $19C3,X and tail-jump to $3E54.
Return if $1A29,X is nonzero; otherwise enter $3E5A.
Decrement $5243 modulo 256 and tail-jump to $4454.

Read $1AF5,X. If negative, negate it modulo 256 and call $4342; otherwise call $44DE with the original value. If $44DE returns carry set, first set $1AF5,X to $FE. In either path increment $1AF5,X and return.
Toggle bit 7 of $1B06,X and return.
If $1B28,X is zero, return carry set. Otherwise decrement it and return carry clear, even when the decrement makes it zero.
Save A on the stack. If $1B06,X is nonnegative, restore A and call $4574; if negative, restore A and call $45BC. On carry set, branch to $3E7F to toggle the direction bit; otherwise return.
Call $4342 with A=8. If $1177 is nonzero, call $43F0 with A=8 and store zero in $1B06,X. If $1177 is zero, call $43A2 with A=8 and store $80 in $1B06,X. Return.

If $4D51 is nonnegative, compare $4D52 with $0B, $12, $17 and $19; on a match decrement $4D43,X only if it is nonzero. If $4D51 is negative, skip the speed update. Both paths then select motion from $4D3B,X.
A zero $4D3B,X returns. A positive value calls $3F56 with $4D43,X in A; a negative value calls $3F2E with the same speed. If the callback returns carry set, go to $3F25; otherwise return.
Alternate-mode motion uses the same zero, positive and negative direction paths as $3EE9 but skips the phase-dependent speed decrement.
Toggle bit 7 of $4D3B,X and return. This path is entered when a movement callback returns carry set.

Patch the immediate operand at $3F36 with A, then subtract it from $4D29,X and subtract the borrow from $4D31,X. If bit 0 of the resulting high byte is set or the low byte is at least $1C, return carry clear. Otherwise write $1C to $4D29 without X and return carry set.
Immediate subtraction operand patched by $3F2E with the requested leftward step.
The left-limit clamp writes slot zero without X; the corresponding right-limit clamp writes the indexed slot. The effect when X is nonzero depends on whether this path is reached.

Add A to $4D29,X and propagate carry into $4D31,X. If bit 0 of the resulting high byte is clear, return carry clear. Otherwise compare the low byte with $3D: below it return carry clear; at or above it write $3D to $4D29,X and return carry set.
If $4D53 is zero, write 1 to each of the eight bytes at $4D21 through $4D28 and return. Otherwise decrement $4D53; if $4D51 is negative tail-jump to $402F, else continue at $3F91.

If $4D54 is zero, replace $4D3A with $99 when it is $9F, or otherwise add 2 to it. Shift the decremented $4D53 right four bits, patch that value into $3FB2, and set $4D54 to 12 minus the patched value modulo 256.
Immediate operand patched from the upper nibble of $4D53 for the animation-delay subtraction at $3FB1.

Decrement $4D54. If $4D52 is negative enter the fall path at $3FDF. Otherwise use it as Y into the byte table at $4013. A nonzero byte is added to $4D39, $402D is cleared and $4D52 is incremented; zero sets bit 7 of $4D52 instead.
Add $402D to $4D39 modulo 256 and increment $402D if it is below 8. Compute $C2 plus $4D69 modulo 256; if that value is at or below $4D39, enter the landing path at $4000, otherwise return.
Set $4D39 to the computed floor value, clear bit 7 of $4D52, then increment the result unless it equals $19. Return.

Twenty-six signed displacement bytes for the effect vertical-motion routine at $3FB6: -10 through 0, then -6 through 0, -4 through 0, and -2 through 0. A nonzero byte is added to $4D39 modulo 256 and advances $4D52; zero instead sets bit 7 of $4D52 to enter the fall phase. The index comes from $4D52. Starting from the 0 that $5F06 stores, repeated calls use every entry in turn: the landing at $4000 clears bit 7 and steps the index past each zero, and leaves it at $19, the last zero.
Fall-speed byte used by $3FDF; the nonzero displacement path at $3FCD clears it.
One byte, $60, between the fall-speed byte at $402D and the routine at $402F. No instruction in the resident part or in any load names it.

Load Y from $4D52. If it is nonnegative, read $4077,Y, choose $A1 for a negative displacement or $A3 otherwise, store that frame in $4D3A, and add the displacement to $4D39 modulo 256. A negative Y skips those writes.
Compute $C2 plus $4D69 modulo 256 and compare it with $4D39. If the floor value is at or below the position, enter $4056; otherwise enter $406C.
Store the computed floor value at $4D39, clear all eight bytes at $4D3B through $4D42, and set both $4D52 and $4D3A to $A5 before returning.

Reached from $4054 while the effect group's floor ($C2 plus $4D69) is still below it on screen, that is greater than its Y $4D39, with Y the phase $4D52 loaded at $402F. Read $4077,Y: if it is $08, the last displacement, return; otherwise increment $4D52 and return. $5F06 starts the phase at 0, so in flight it climbs to $12 and stops at that entry's $08. After a landing $4065 leaves $A5 in $4D52; if the floor value later rises above $4D39 again, this path reads $4077+$A5 = $411C, inside the code at $408A, and counts the phase on from there.

Nineteen signed displacements, −10 ($F6) up to +8 ($08), one per phase of the effect group's flight. $4034 reads $4077,Y with Y the phase $4D52 and adds the byte to the group's Y $4D39, choosing frame $A1 for an upward (negative) step and $A3 otherwise; $406C stops advancing the phase at the $08 of index $12. $5F06 starts the phase at 0, and after a landing $4065 sets it to $A5, which $4032 skips.
Builds status-display rows from current-player flag bits, copying or blanking icon fragments and caching the low flag bits.

Save incoming A on the stack. For X=0–2, copy $41DF,X to $4F8A,Y and $41E2,X to $4F9F,Y, incrementing Y after each column. Restore A and return with X=3 and Y advanced by three. The three callers, at $40BE, $40DE and $40FE, pass Y = 0, 3 and 6.

Save incoming A on the stack. For X=0–2, copy $41E5,X to $4FB4,Y, $41E8,X to $4FC9,Y and $41EB,X to $4FDE,Y, incrementing Y after each column. Restore A and return with X=3 and Y advanced by three. The three callers, at $4124, $414A and $4159, pass Y = 0, 3 and 6.
Cached low three player-flag bits, compared and updated by the status renderer at $4098/$409D. Referenced at $4098 (CMP), $409D (STA).
Nine character codes for row 1 of three two-row flag icons. $40A7–$40F6 selects columns 0–2, 3–5 or 6–8 according to the tested high flag bits and copies them to $4F8A plus the same column.
Nine character codes for row 2 of three two-row flag icons. $40A7–$40F6 selects columns 0–2, 3–5 or 6–8 according to the tested high flag bits and copies them to $4F9F plus the same column.

Nine character codes for row 1 of three three-row status icons. The loops at $4107, $412D and $4162 select three-column groups and copy this row to $4FB4; the choice depends on flag bits and the low-three-bit field.

Nine character codes for row 2 of three three-row status icons. The loops at $4107, $412D and $4162 select three-column groups and copy this row to $4FC9; the choice depends on flag bits and the low-three-bit field.

Nine character codes for row 3 of three three-row status icons. The loops at $4107, $412D and $4162 select three-column groups and copy this row to $4FDE; the choice depends on flag bits and the low-three-bit field.
Three replacement character codes for row 1 of a two-row icon. $417D copies them to $4F8A, offset by incoming Y, when the corresponding flag group is absent.
Three replacement character codes for row 2 of a two-row icon. $417D copies them to $4F9F, offset by incoming Y, when the corresponding flag group is absent.
Three replacement character codes for row 1 of a three-row icon. $4194 copies them to $4FB4, offset by incoming Y; the other two rows come from the adjacent replacement tables.
Three replacement character codes for row 2 of a three-row icon. $4194 copies them to $4FC9, offset by incoming Y; the other two rows come from the adjacent replacement tables.
Three replacement character codes for row 3 of a three-row icon. $4194 copies them to $4FDE, offset by incoming Y; the other two rows come from the adjacent replacement tables.

Decrement $1AF5,X, then read Y from $1AC2,X. If Y is 7, go to $4226; otherwise read $4249,Y. A nonzero byte increments $1AC2,X, calls $4342 with that byte in A, copies $19E5,X to $19C3,X and returns without checking the decremented countdown.

For a zero animation-table byte, set $1A7E,X to 1, increment $1AC2,X and set $19C3,X to $19E5,X plus 2. If the decremented $1AF5,X is zero, jump to $4454; if it is $20 set $1A8F,X to $FF; otherwise return.
When the animation index is 7 and $1A7E,X is 1, set $19C3,X to $19E5,X plus 4. Then test $1AF5,X: zero jumps to $4454, $20 sets $1A8F,X to $FF, and any other value returns.
Set the entity display-effect byte $1A8F,X to $FF and return.

Seven upward step sizes read at $41F9, indexed by $1AC2,X: $14, $08, $05, $03, $02, $01 and 0. $4201 passes each nonzero byte to $4342 as the distance to move up; the zero at index 6 instead enters $420B, which selects the second frame. The reader tests for index 7 first and does not exclude larger starting indexes.

Update entity slot X. Decrement $1AF5,X and release the slot when the result is zero; a result of $20 sets $1A8F,X to $FF. When the frame timer $1B06,X is zero, reload it from the table at $4331 indexed by the high nibble of the remaining count, advance the frame offset in steps of 2 with a reset at 6, and add the offset to $19E5,X for the frame at $19C3,X. Decrement the timer and use $1AC2,X to read the movement sequence at $4319; a nonzero byte advances the index and calls $4342. A zero byte enters phase and tile-row handling. When $1AD3,X is nonzero, the sign of $1B17,X selects a horizontal collision routine; carry on return reverses that sign. The index starts at 0 for the hidden coin that $5C35 sets up in slot 0 (whose release cleared it) or at 9 from $5CBA, and stays within the 24-byte table: it advances past a nonzero byte, past a zero at $42E3 only below $17 (CMP #$17 at $42DF), or $42CC sets it back to 9.

Twenty-four upward step sizes read at $4296, indexed by $1AC2,X, in four runs that each end in zero: $14, 7 down to 1, 0; 6 down to 1, 0; 4 down to 1, 0; 2, 1, 0. $429E passes each nonzero byte to $4342 as the distance to move up. A zero enters the phase handling at $42A7, which steps the index past the zero, stopping at $17, or sets it back to 9 at $42CC. The set-ups start the index at 0 (the hidden coin in slot 0 at $5C35) or 9 ($5CBA), so it stays within the table.

Sixteen frame-timer reload values: 8, 6, 4, 3, 3, 2, 2, then nine of 1. $4270 indexes them with the high nibble of the remaining lifetime $1AF5,X and stores the value in $1B06,X, which $428F counts down between frame changes. The step read at $4296 uses indexes 0–$17 of the table at $4319 and reaches these bytes only from a larger starting index.

One byte, $01, after the 16-entry frame-timer table at $4331. The lookup at $4270 masks its index to 0–15 and does not reach it, and no instruction names it. The step read at $4296 would address it only with Y=$28; the update at $42DF stops that index at $17.

Patch the immediate operand at $434E with incoming A. If $7A is nonzero, subtract it from the 16-bit value $197F,X:$1990,X with carry set, clear carry and return. If $7A is zero, continue at $435C. Arithmetic is binary with decimal mode clear.
Immediate operand of the SBC at $434D, patched from incoming A by $4342 and also read by $435C.
Subtract the patched byte at $434E from $19A1,X with carry set, store the wrapped result at $19A1,X, clear carry and return. Arithmetic is binary with decimal mode clear.

Patch the immediate operand at $4374 with incoming A. If $7A is nonzero, add it to the 16-bit value $197F,X:$1990,X with carry clear, clear carry and return. If $7A is zero, continue at $4382. Arithmetic is binary with decimal mode clear.
Immediate operand of the ADC at $4373, patched from incoming A by $4368 and also read by $4382.

Add the byte at $4374 to $19A1,X with carry clear and store the wrapped result. Patch the operand at $4398 with $4D69 plus $C2, wrapping at eight bits, then compare the result with that limit. If the result is at least the limit, store the limit in $19A1,X and return with carry set; otherwise return with carry clear. Arithmetic is binary with decimal mode clear.
Immediate operand of the CMP at $4397, patched at $4393 with $4D69 plus $C2; the clamp path also reads this byte directly.

Patch $43AE with A. If $7A is nonzero, subtract it from the 16-bit position $193B,X:$194C,X modulo 65536 and return carry clear with the high byte in A. If $7A is zero, enter the screen-position path at $43BC.
Immediate operand patched with the incoming leftward step at $43A2; the screen-position path also reads this byte.

Subtract the saved step from $196E,X:$195D,X modulo 65536. If bit 0 of the resulting high byte is set, or the low byte is at least $1F, return A=3 and carry clear. Otherwise, type $28 tail-jumps to $4454; other types clamp the low byte to $1F and return A=$0F with carry set.
Patch $43FC with A. If $7A is nonzero, add it to $193B,X:$194C,X modulo 65536 and return carry clear with the high byte in A. If $7A is zero, enter the screen-position path at $440A.
Immediate operand patched with the incoming rightward step at $43F0; the screen-position path also reads this byte.
Add the saved step to $196E,X:$195D,X modulo 65536. If bit 0 of the resulting high byte is clear, return A=3 and carry clear. Otherwise choose the bound from $192A,X.
If $192A,X is nonzero, compare the low byte with $1F; below it return A=3 and carry clear, otherwise clamp to $1F and return A=$0F with carry set. If $192A,X is zero, use the $40 bound at $4436.
If the low byte is below $40, return A=3 and carry clear. At or above $40, type $28 tail-jumps to $4454; other types clamp the low byte to $40 and return A=$0F with carry set.
Load Y from $1A29,X. If it is nonzero, write $FF to $4CCF,Y, then load Y from $1A3A,X and write $FF there too, even if that second index is zero. Continue at $4466.
Clear $1A29,X, $1A3A,X and $19B2,X. If X is nonzero set $1AA0,X to 7; then fall through to $447A for the optional extra-slot writes and entity-state reset.
Set $1AA0,X to 7 for a nonzero entity index, then continue into $447A.

If bit 0 of $192A,X is set and $1A4B,X is nonzero, write $FF to $4CCF,Y for Y=$1A4B,X and again for Y=$1A5C,X. The second index is used even when zero. Otherwise skip these slot writes. Both paths enter the reset at $4494.
Clear the entity bytes at $1A07, $1A7E, $192A, $1A8F, $1A4B, $1A5C, $1AB1, $1AC2, $1AD3, $1AE4, $1AF5, $1B06, $1B17, $1B28, $1919 and $1A6D, each indexed by X, then return.

Copy A to Y and call the downward collision routine at $44DE. If it returns carry set, store 1 at $1A7E,X. Otherwise increment the returned Y, decrement it again only when the incremented value equals 9, and store it at $1A7E,X. The increment wraps at 255; values already above 8 are not generally clamped.
Save A at $4571. If $7A is zero, reload A and tail-jump to $4368; otherwise enter the tile check at $44EB.

Save Y, subtract $005A from the 16-bit coordinate $197F,X:$1990,X into $4570:$456F, and add the requested amount to the low nibble. If the sum is below 16, restore the saved amount and Y and tail-jump to $4368.

Clear $4573, call $71DB, push its returned A and set $4573 to 1 if carry is set. Save the returned X, form $52/$53 from the indexed bytes at $85D1/$8622 plus that X, and read the first tile. If its $80CF-indexed value has either low bit set, clamp; if not, check the next tile only when $4573 is nonzero.
Pop the saved A into X. Set $1990,X to the high nibble of $456F plus $69 and $197F,X to $4570 plus the carry; restore Y from $456E, set carry and return.
Pop the saved A into X. Reload the movement amount from $4571 and Y from $456E, then tail-jump to $4368.
Saved Y for the downward tile check; restored on both its clamp and fallback paths.
Low byte of the coordinate after subtracting $005A, used for the tile boundary and clamp.
High byte of the coordinate after subtracting $005A, used for the clamp.
Movement amount saved from A on entry, passed to $4368 on fallback.
X returned by $71DB, added to the indexed row pointer for the tile check.
Flag set from carry returned by $71DB; when nonzero the clear first-tile path checks the next tile.
Save A at $45BB. If $7A is zero, reload it and tail-jump to $43F0. Otherwise call $43F0, save its returned Y at $45BA, and call $71DB.

Save the A returned by $71DB on the stack and set $7E to $0F. Increment its returned X; if it equals $7F4B, enter rollback at $45A2. Otherwise decrement X and call $460C. Store its result at $7E; bit 2 set enters rollback, clear enters $45B1.
Restore the saved entity index into X, call $43A2 with the saved amount, restore Y from $45BA, load A from $7E and return carry set.
Restore the saved entity index into X and Y from $45BA, load A from $7E and return carry clear.
Y saved after the initial rightward movement call for restoration by $4574.
Incoming movement amount saved by $4574 for its initial move and possible rollback.
Save A at $460B. If $7A is zero, reload it and tail-jump to $43A2. Otherwise call $43A2, save its returned Y at $460A, and call $71DB.

Save the A returned by $71DB on the stack and set $7E to $0F. If returned X is $FF, enter rollback. Otherwise subtract 1 from X: a borrow stores 3 at $7E and returns clear; without borrow call $460C with that index. Store its result at $7E; bit 2 set enters rollback, clear returns without rollback.
Restore the saved entity index into X, call $43F0 with the saved amount, restore Y from $460A, load A from $7E and return carry set.
Restore the saved entity index into X and Y from $460A, load A from $7E and return carry clear.
Y saved after the initial leftward movement call for restoration by $45BC.
Incoming movement amount saved by $45BC for its initial move and possible rollback.

Clear $7D and call $4632 at Y-1, Y, Y+1 and Y+2, with Y arithmetic modulo 256. Pack bit 1 of the first two returned attributes into result bits 3 and 2, and bit 0 of the last two into bits 1 and 0. Return that result in A, Y advanced by two and carry clear.

Patch $463D with X and $4650 with Y. Add X to the row pointer formed from $85D0,Y and $8621,Y, then read the byte one position beyond the resulting address. Use that byte as an index into $80CF and return its value in A, restoring X and Y from the patched operands.
Immediate addition operand patched with X by $4632; it also stores the X restored before return.
Immediate operand patched with Y by $4635 and restored before $4632 returns.

Copy the load's stage-object records, $7F57 of them from the pointer at $7F55/$7F56, sixteen bytes each: bytes 0–11 go into the twelve six-entry arrays at $4747–$478E, and bytes 12–15 to $7D–$80, which $46D6 writes as the record's two-by-two block of map cells. A count of zero returns at once; otherwise the CPX $7F57 at $46CD ends the loop, and every load's count is 0 to 6, so the records fill at most the six entries.

Save Y into the operand at $4745. Using X from $7B, copy $474D,X into the row operand at $471C and $4747,X into the column operand at $4723. If $4753,X is nonnegative, use the four bytes already in $7D–$80. Otherwise select a replacement set using $7A.
When $7A is zero copy the four bytes at $7F6D–$7F70 to $7D–$80; otherwise copy $7F71–$7F74. Continue at $471B.

Load the patched row byte into Y and decrement it. Add the patched column byte to the little-endian row pointer read from $85CF,Y and $8620,Y, storing the result in $54/$55. Write $7D and $7E at offsets 0 and 1, then $7F and $80 at offsets $7F4A and ($7F4A+1) modulo 256. Restore Y from the operand at $4745 and return.
Immediate operand of the LDY at $471B, patched from $474D,X at $46DE; the following DEY selects a row-pointer entry.
Immediate operand of the ADC at $4722, patched from $4747,X at $46E4 and added to the low row-pointer byte with carry clear.
Immediate operand of the LDY at $4744, patched with incoming Y at $46D6 and loaded before return.

Six-slot parallel stage-record field 1, holding record byte offset 0 (zero-based). Its role is map column: $47A2 compares it with the player tile column $6F3C, and $46E1 patches it into the column operand at $4723. The loader at $4655 copies twelve such fields from each 16-byte record into six-byte arrays from $4747 to $478E; it does not check its runtime record count against six, and a larger count overlaps the following fields.

Six-slot parallel stage-record field 2, holding disk-record byte offset 1 (zero-based). The loader at $4655 copies that byte from each 16-byte record into this array. Its role is map row: $47AA compares it with the player's tile row $6F3D, and $46DE patches it into the row operand at $471C. The loader's loop ends at the CPX $7F57 at $46CD, and every load's record count $7F57 is 0 to 6, so it fills at most these six entries.

Six-slot parallel stage-record field 3, holding disk-record byte offset 3 (zero-based). The loader at $4655 copies that byte from each 16-byte record into this array. Its role is interaction state: $47B2 skips a record whose state is negative, $47EE subtracts 2 per interaction, and $46D6 and $4801 draw the alternate cells $7F6D–$7F74 when it is negative. The loader's loop ends at the CPX $7F57 at $46CD, and every load's record count $7F57 is 0 to 6, so it fills at most these six entries.

Six-slot parallel stage-record field 4, holding disk-record byte offset 2 (zero-based). The loader at $4655 copies that byte from each 16-byte record into this array. Its role is visual resource selector, which $47F5 passes to $7119. The loader's loop ends at the CPX $7F57 at $46CD, and every load's record count $7F57 is 0 to 6, so it fills at most these six entries.

Six-slot parallel stage-record field 5, holding disk-record byte offset 10 (zero-based). The loader at $4655 copies that byte from each 16-byte record into this array. Its role is interaction callback low byte, patched by $47DE. The loader's loop ends at the CPX $7F57 at $46CD, and every load's record count $7F57 is 0 to 6, so it fills at most these six entries.

Six-slot parallel stage-record field 6, holding disk-record byte offset 11 (zero-based). The loader at $4655 copies that byte from each 16-byte record into this array. Its role is interaction callback high byte, patched by $47E4. The loader's loop ends at the CPX $7F57 at $46CD, and every load's record count $7F57 is 0 to 6, so it fills at most these six entries.

Six-slot parallel stage-record field 7, holding disk-record byte offset 4 (zero-based). The loader at $4655 copies that byte from each 16-byte record into this array. Its role is record-specific value. The loader's loop ends at the CPX $7F57 at $46CD, and every load's record count $7F57 is 0 to 6, so it fills at most these six entries.

Six-slot parallel stage-record field 8, holding disk-record byte offset 5 (zero-based). The loader at $4655 copies that byte from each 16-byte record into this array. Its role is record-specific value. The loader's loop ends at the CPX $7F57 at $46CD, and every load's record count $7F57 is 0 to 6, so it fills at most these six entries.

Six-slot parallel stage-record field 9, holding disk-record byte offset 6 (zero-based). The loader at $4655 copies that byte from each 16-byte record into this array. Its role is record-specific callback/value. The loader's loop ends at the CPX $7F57 at $46CD, and every load's record count $7F57 is 0 to 6, so it fills at most these six entries.

Six-slot parallel stage-record field 10, holding disk-record byte offset 7 (zero-based). The loader at $4655 copies that byte from each 16-byte record into this array. Its role is record-specific callback/value. The loader's loop ends at the CPX $7F57 at $46CD, and every load's record count $7F57 is 0 to 6, so it fills at most these six entries.

Six-slot parallel stage-record field 11, holding disk-record byte offset 8 (zero-based). The loader at $4655 copies that byte from each 16-byte record into this array. Its role is record-specific callback/value. The loader's loop ends at the CPX $7F57 at $46CD, and every load's record count $7F57 is 0 to 6, so it fills at most these six entries.

Six-slot parallel stage-record field 12, holding disk-record byte offset 9 (zero-based). The loader at $4655 copies that byte from each 16-byte record into this array. Its role is record-specific callback/value. The loader's loop ends at the CPX $7F57 at $46CD, and every load's record count $7F57 is 0 to 6, so it fills at most these six entries.
Scans stage records for a position match and input, updates the selected record and calls a target patched from that record's fields.

Immediate operand of the LDX at $47DC, which reloads the stage-object record index before $47DE–$47E7 patch the interaction callback from $475F,X and $4765,X. $47B7 stores the record index X here; no other instruction writes it. The load holds $FF here.
Read stage-record field $475F,X and store it at $47FD as the low byte of the callback JSR at $47FC. The high byte is read from $4765,X by the following path.

Load record field $4765,X and patch it into the callback high-byte operand at $47FE. Subtract 2 from $4753,X modulo 256, save the record index in $7B, load X from $4759,X and call the visual-resource loader at $7119. The selected callback follows at $47FC.
Call the fixed visual-resource loader at $7119 with X from the selected stage record’s field 4. The loader uses that selector to choose the screen and character tables.

Call the stage object's interaction routine, whose address $47E1 and $47E7 patch in from $475F,X and $4765,X (fields 5 and 6: bytes 10 and 11 of the stage-object record), after $7119 has loaded the visual resources that the record's field 4 selects. The load holds JSR $FF00 here.

Low byte of the target of the JSR at $47FC, whose high byte is $47FE. The load holds $00 here, so the instruction reads JSR $FF00 until it is patched. $47E1 stores it from $475F,X, byte 10 of the stage-object record, and $47E7 the high byte from $4765,X (byte 11): the record's interaction callback. No other instruction writes it.

High byte of the JSR operand at $47FC, patched from selected record field 6 at $47E4–$47E7; $47FD is its low byte. After the selected callback returns, reload X from $7B and inspect $4753,X. If negative, call $46D6. Set $7A to $FF; if $0840 is nonzero branch to $479B, otherwise jump to $3384.
Call the display-step wait at $3C2A four times, then tail-jump to the same wait for a fifth pass. This counts calls to the wait routine; it does not independently establish five video frames.

For X from 21 down to 0, fill $C00E,X and $C0AE,X with the same byte at $5092. Copy $5050,X, $5066,X and $507C,X to $C036,X, $C05E,X and $C086,X respectively. Write $5092,X to colour RAM $D886,X and $D836,X, and $50A8,X to $D85E,X. After the loop, decrement X once more, store $FE at $4DAD and return.

Sixteen bytes of trigger columns, the first of six parallel arrays 16 bytes apart: column $485F, row $486F, remaining count $487F, callback low $488F, callback high $489F and argument $48AF. The loader at $7979 fills them from the load's six-byte trigger records (pointer $7F52/$7F53, count $7F54); it does not cap the count at 16. The dispatcher compares the column with the player's tile column $6F3C at $48C3, and the converter at $5D2C shifts it left four bits and adds $1B to make a world X at $194C/$193B.

Sixteen bytes of trigger rows. The six-byte record loader at $7979 fills the array from the load's trigger records; its loop ends at the CPX $7F54 at $79B0, and every load's count is 1 to 12, so entries 0–11 at most are used. The dispatcher compares the row with the player's tile row $6F3D at $48CB, and the converter at $5D2C reads it at $5D57, shifts it left four bits and adds $59 to make the 16-bit world Y of entity slot 0 at $1990/$197F. Only the loader writes it.

Sixteen bytes of trigger remaining counts. The six-byte record loader at $7979 fills the array from the load's trigger records; its loop ends at the CPX $7F54 at $79B0, and every load's count is 1 to 12, so entries 0–11 at most are used. The dispatcher skips a record whose count is zero ($48D3) and decrements the count before it jumps to the callback ($48E4). A callback that cannot act on this pass adds one back: $5BE7, $5C30, $5CD1 and $5D04 when entity slot 0 is in use, and $7975 when the selected player lacks flag $40. The recoil callback adds one back at $72AC on every call, so its records never run out. The INC at $77D8 would do the same, but nothing reaches $77D0. Load 22 writes a count at $938D and increments one at $939C.

Sixteen bytes of trigger callback low bytes. The six-byte record loader at $7979 fills the array from the load's trigger records; its loop ends at the CPX $7F54 at $79B0, and every load's count is 1 to 12, so entries 0–11 at most are used. Each forms a callback pointer with $489F, which the dispatcher copies into the JMP operand at $48EB/$48EC. Only the loader writes it.

Sixteen bytes of trigger callback high bytes. The six-byte record loader at $7979 fills the array from the load's trigger records; its loop ends at the CPX $7F54 at $79B0, and every load's count is 1 to 12, so entries 0–11 at most are used. Each forms a callback pointer with $488F, which the dispatcher copies into the JMP operand at $48EB/$48EC. Only the loader writes it.

Sixteen bytes of trigger arguments. The six-byte record loader at $7979 fills the array from the load's trigger records; its loop ends at the CPX $7F54 at $79B0, and every load's count is 1 to 12, so entries 0–11 at most are used. The dispatcher loads the matching record's argument into A at $48E7, just before it jumps to the callback. Only the loader writes it.

Scans six-field trigger records, matches positions and jumps through a patched callback. Count zero starts with X=$ff and tests one entry before exiting; counts $81–$ff likewise start negative, while $80 scans $7f down to zero.
Copy the matching trigger record's callback low byte from $488F,X into the low operand byte at $48EB of the JMP at $48EA.
Copy the matching trigger record's callback high byte from $489F,X into the high operand byte at $48EC of the JMP at $48EA. The DEC at $48E4 then takes one from the record's remaining count.

Load the matching record's argument from $48AF,X into A and jump to its callback through the JMP at $48EA, whose operand $48DB and $48E1 have just patched from $488F,X and $489F,X. The callback's RTS returns to the dispatcher's caller, so the scan ends at the first record that fires.

Low byte of the target of the JMP at $48EA, whose high byte is $48EC. The load holds $00 here, so the instruction reads JMP $FF00 until it is patched. $48DB stores it from $488F,X, the matching map-trigger record's callback low byte, and $48E1 the high byte from $489F,X; the jump runs with the record's argument $48AF,X in A. No other instruction writes it.
High byte of the record-selected JMP at $48EA, paired with $48EB. The separate scan continuation at $48ED decrements X and returns when it becomes negative, otherwise branching to $48C3.
Call $447A, copy $7F65 to $19E5,X, set $19F6,X to 1 and enter $49D0 with A=$F4.
Call $447A, copy $7F64 to $19E5,X, set $19F6,X to 1 and enter $49D0 with A=$F5.
Call $447A, copy $7F66 to $19E5,X and preserve X and Y in patched operands. Call $77E2 with A=$10, restore X and Y, set $19F6,X to 7 and enter $49D0 with A=$F3.

Immediate operand of the LDX at $492B, which restores X after the $77E2 call for message $10. $4920 stores the entity slot X here (with Y at $492E); no other instruction writes it. The load holds $FF here.

Saved Y immediate operand at $492D. After restoring it, set entity attribute $19F6,X to 7 and tail-jump to common item initialization $49D0 with A=$F3. The variant entry at $4917 sets the saved registers before this continuation.
Call $447A, copy $7F67 to $19E5,X and preserve X and Y in patched operands. Call $77E2 with A=$0F, restore X and Y, set $19F6,X to 7 and enter $49D0 with A=$F2.

Immediate operand of the LDX at $494D, which restores X after the $77E2 call for message $0F. $4942 stores the entity slot X here (with Y at $4950); no other instruction writes it. The load holds $FF here.
Saved Y immediate operand at $494F. After restoring it, set $19F6,X to 7 and tail-jump to item initialization $49D0 with A=$F2; the variant entry at $4939 supplies the saved registers.
Call $447A, copy $7F68 to $19E5,X and preserve X and Y in patched operands. Call $77E2 with A=$0D, restore X and Y, set $19F6,X to 1 and enter $49D0 with A=$F1.

Immediate operand of the LDX at $496F, which restores X after the $77E2 call for message $0D. $4964 stores the entity slot X here (with Y at $4972); no other instruction writes it. The load holds $FF here.
Saved Y immediate operand at $4971. After restoring it, set $19F6,X to 1 and tail-jump to item initialization $49D0 with A=$F1; the variant entry at $495B supplies the saved registers.
Save Y in the immediate operand at $4987, then use $4DBD as an index into $4DE2. Restore Y and test bit $10 of the selected byte. If set, tail-jump to $49E3; if clear, continue at $498F.
Saved Y operand of LDY at $4986. Test bit $10 in the selected player’s flags already loaded in A; clear enters initialization at $498F, set jumps to the next available-entry dispatch at $49E3.
Call $447A, copy $7F69 to $19E5,X and preserve X and Y in patched operands. Call $77E2 with A=$11, restore X and Y, set $19F6,X to 1 and enter $49D0 with A=$F0.

Immediate operand of the LDX at $49A3, which restores X after the $77E2 call for message $11. $4998 stores the entity slot X here (with Y at $49A6); no other instruction writes it. The load holds $FF here.
Saved Y operand at $49A5. Restore Y, set $19F6,X to 1, load A=$F0 and jump to item initialization $49D0.
Call $447A, copy $7F6A to $19E5,X and preserve X and Y in patched operands. Call $77E2 with A=$0E, restore X and Y, set $19F6,X to 7 and continue at $49D0 with A=$EF.

Immediate operand of the LDX at $49C5, which restores X after the $77E2 call for message $0E. $49BA stores the entity slot X here (with Y at $49C8); no other instruction writes it. The load holds $FF here.
Saved Y operand of LDY at $49C7. Set $19F6,X to 7, load A=$EF and fall through to the common entity type store at $49D0.
Store A as the entity type at $1919,X, set $1AF5,X to $A0, copy $19E5,X to $19C3,X and tail-jump to $4342 with A=$0C.
Call $3020, mask its result to 0–7 and use it as Y. Test $7F5E,Y; if zero, increment Y, mask it to 0–7 and repeat. The scan has no exit if all eight bytes are zero.
Use the selected Y to patch the jump operand at $4A00/$4A01 from the low and high tables at $4A02/$4A0A, then jump through it.
Read the selected high byte from $4A0A,Y and continue to the store at $49FC. It pairs with the low byte already copied from $4A02,Y.

Hourglass tick, called once in each pass of the main loop at $0437 and of the alternate loop at $07B2, and once from the display setup at $039A. Decrement the countdown at $4B0D and return if it is nonzero. If it reaches zero, the flag at $4DD3 selects the forward step at $4A50 or the backward step at $4A74. An initial zero wraps to $FF and returns.

Forward step of the hourglass. Set $4B0D to $96 (150) and load X from the picture number at $4DD4. If X is 6 the glass has run out: call $77BC with A=8, which takes 8 from the selected player’s meter, and set X to $FF. Increment X and store it in $4DD4; if the new picture is 6, set $4B0D to 3, so the last picture lasts three calls. Call $4A90 to draw the picture and return.

Backward step of the hourglass, taken while $4DD3 is nonzero. If $4DD4 is zero, clear $4DD3, set $4B0D to $96 and return without drawing. Otherwise decrement $4DD4, set $4B0D to 8, call $4A90 and return, so the glass goes back one picture every eight calls until it shows picture 0.

Draw the hourglass at the right of the status panel. Use $4DD4 as X to load a source pointer from the low-byte table at $51B3 and high-byte table at $51BA into $52/$53. Pictures 0 and 5 take the colour-13 path; picture 6 takes the colour-15 path; other pictures skip both. $4DD4 is always 0 to 6, one value per picture: the hourglass tick steps it up and wraps 6 to 0 at $4A58, the turn-back path at $4A84 decrements it only while it is nonzero, $6C81 stores 6, and loads 4, 9, 19, 20 and 30 store 0.
Write 13 to four consecutive colour RAM cells on each of three rows starting at $D84C, $D874 and $D89C. The loop leaves X as $FF before the following comparisons.
Write 15 to four consecutive colour RAM cells on each of three rows starting at $D84C, $D874 and $D89C.
Copy 20 bytes from the pointer at $52/$53 in five rows of four, to $C024, $C04C, $C074, $C09C and $C0C4 respectively; return after the fifth row.

Hourglass countdown; $4A43 decrements it and steps the hourglass only when the result reaches zero. Referenced in the resident code at $302C (EOR), $4A43 (DEC), $4A52 (STA), $4A6D (STA), $4A80 (STA), $4A89 (STA), $6140 (LDA), $6147 (DEC), $6C7E (STA), $7650 (STA). 5 instructions in 5 loads also use it, the first at $A5A0 in load 4.
Adds packed-BCD score bytes, compares against the record, and can increase meter thresholds. The later meter addition has a carry-dependent edge case documented at $4bae.

Clear carry, select player Y from $4DBD, set decimal mode and add incoming A to the middle packed-BCD score byte at $4DC3,Y. If carry is set, pass A=0 with that carry to the high-byte addition at $4B37; otherwise continue at $4B3D. The common comparison path handles the remaining effects.

Third entry of the score adder: clear carry, select the player with Y from $4DBD, set decimal mode and fall into $4B37, which adds A to the high packed-BCD score byte at $4DC1,Y before the record comparison at $4B3D. No instruction in the resident part or in any load names $4B32; the adder reaches $4B37 from its own carry path at $4B2F.
The meter-limit update and subsequent current-meter addition depend on the carry from the comparison at $4ba2.
ADC #8 inherits carry from the limit comparison. On the path that clamps the limit to $50, carry is set, so this adds nine before comparing with the limit.
Signed movement sequence; the updating routine increments its index and wraps at 28.

Signed horizontal displacements for directional motion: 13 rows of 16 bytes at $56A8–$5777. The index is speed × 16 + direction, with the speed 0–12 in the high nibble and the direction 0–15 in the low nibble, counted clockwise in sixteenths of a turn from straight up. Each entry is the speed times the sine of the direction, rounded; positive is to the right. $35C1 takes the index in A, reads $56A8,Y and moves the entity left or right by the value, then applies the vertical table at $5778 with the same index; load 24 reads both tables itself at $A0CD–$A0ED. This note takes in rows 0–11, $56A8–$5767; row 12 is at $5768. An index of $D0 or more would read the vertical table.

Row 12, the last, of the horizontal displacement table at $56A8: sixteen signed values for speed 12, indexes $C0–$CF, one for each direction: 0, 5, 8, 11, 12, 11, 8, 5, 0, −5, −8, −11, −12, −11, −8 and −5. The resident trajectory at $3DE1 uses this row: it ORs the direction returned by $34EA with $C0, stores the index in $1B28,X and passes it to $35C1.

Signed vertical displacements for directional motion: 13 rows of 16 bytes at $5778–$5847, with the same index as the horizontal table at $56A8, speed × 16 + direction. Each entry is the speed times the cosine of the direction, rounded; positive is up. $35FB, $3609 and $361B read $5778,Y and subtract the value from the entity's Y coordinates at $1990,X/$197F,X and $19A1,X; load 24 subtracts it at $A0ED. Y is the index $35C1 was given, except that when a type-$28 entity reaches a screen bound the horizontal mover releases it through $4454, which loads Y with a display-slot number, and the vertical reads then use that. This note takes in $5778–$5796; the table continues at $5797.
Continuation of the vertical displacement table at $5778: indexes $1F–$BF, from direction 15 of the speed-1 row to the end of the speed-11 row, at $5797–$5837. The speed-12 row follows at $5838.

Row 12, the last, of the vertical displacement table at $5778: sixteen signed values for speed 12, indexes $C0–$CF, one for each direction: 12, 11, 8, 5, 0, −5, −8, −11, −12, −11, −8, −5, 0, 5, 8 and 11. It is the vertical counterpart of the horizontal row at $5768, which the resident trajectory at $3DE1 selects.

Character $00, eight zero rows: the start of the character set for visual selector 0, which the continue screen loads at $05D1–$05D3. Entry 0 of the character-source table at $7FAC/$7FB3 is $5848 in every load. $717C copies eight pages from here, $5848–$6047, to $D000–$D7FF; the screen at $5B28 uses characters $00–$3E less $0E, which end at $5A3F, and the rest of the copy takes in the metatiles, colour lookup, screen stream and code that follow.

Resident: characters $01–$0D of the eight-page character copy for visual selector 0, which starts at $5848, 104 bytes. $717C copies them to $D008–$D06F. Entry 0 of the character-source table at $7FAC/$7FB3 is $5848 in every load, and the continue screen selects it at $05D1. The screen at $5B28, through the metatiles at $5A40, draws every one of them.

Character $0E of the character set for visual selector 0, which starts at $5848: eight rows of $AA. $717C copies it to $D070–$D077 with the rest. No metatile at $5A40 holds $0E, so the screen at $5B28 does not draw it.

Resident: characters $0F–$3E of the eight-page character copy for visual selector 0, which starts at $5848, 384 bytes. $717C copies them to $D078–$D1F7. Entry 0 of the character-source table at $7FAC/$7FB3 is $5848 in every load, and the continue screen selects it at $05D1. The screen at $5B28, through the metatiles at $5A40, draws every one of them.

Metatile table for visual selector 0: 38 entries of four bytes at $5A40–$5AD7, each the character codes of a two-by-two block in the order top left, top right, bottom left, bottom right. Entry 0 of the pointer table at $7F82/$7F89 is $5A40 in every load; $7064 multiplies the metatile number by four and copies the four codes to the screen. The screen at $5B28 uses every entry but $02. The eight-page character copy from $5848 also takes these bytes in, as characters $3F–$51.

Colour lookup for visual selector 0: 63 bytes at $5AD8–$5B16, one colour for each character code $00–$3E. Entry 0 of the pointer table at $7F9E/$7FA5 is $5AD8 in every load. After the screen is drawn, $70D0 takes each of the 800 cells of screen rows 5–24, uses its character code as the index here and writes the colour to colour RAM from $D8C8. The seventeen bytes after it, from $5B17, are the entries for codes the metatiles do not use.

Seventeen bytes of $08 at $5B17–$5B27, between the last colour entry the selector-0 screen uses ($5B16, character $3E) and its screen stream at $5B28. As entries of the colour lookup at $5AD8 they would serve character codes $3F–$4F, which no metatile at $5A40 holds. The eight-page character copy from $5848 takes them in with everything else up to $6047.

Compressed screen for visual selector 0: 184 bytes at $5B28–$5BDF, which $7011 expands to 200 metatiles, ten rows of twenty. A byte other than $FF is one metatile number; $FF is followed by a metatile number and a repeat count. The decoder stops after the 200th metatile, which is the end of the last token. Entry 0 of the pointer table at $7F90/$7F97 is $5B28 in every load, and the continue screen selects it at $05D1.

One byte, $BD, between the end of the selector-0 screen stream at $5BDF and the trigger callback at $5BE1. The decoder at $7011 stops before it, and no instruction names it. The eight-page character copy from $5848 takes it in with the bytes around it.

Trigger callback for a hidden money bag, entity type $FE drawn with sprite $A1; trigger records name it with the bag's reward byte as the argument in A. Save A on the stack. If slot zero at $1919 is occupied, increment $487F,X modulo 256, restore A and return, so the record fires again on a later pass. Otherwise set slot zero type to $FE and call $5D2C.

For type $FE, set the base sprite to $A1, display attributes to 1 and 0, restore the saved reward byte into $1AB1 and set $1AF5 to $A0. Continue into the input-edge test at $5C0C, which can replace that reward byte with $FF.

For a slot-zero $FE or $FD reward created by the record dispatcher, this checks the two most recent joystick samples. A reversal from left to right or right to left, with $4DB3 nonnegative, replaces the reward byte at $1AB1 with $FF. In the main loop input is sampled at $0407 before the dispatcher at $0434. This is a condition at creation, not at collection.

Trigger callback for a hidden coin, entity type $FD drawn with sprite $99; trigger records name it with the coin's reward byte as the argument in A. Save A on the stack. If slot zero at $1919 is occupied, increment $487F,X modulo 256, restore A and return, so the record fires again on a later pass. Otherwise set slot zero type to $FD and call $5D2C.

For type $FD, set the base sprite to $99, display attributes to 7 and 0, restore the saved reward byte into $1AB1 and set $1AF5 to $A0. Set $1B17 to 1 when $1177 is nonzero or $FF when it is zero, then jump to the input-edge test at $5C0C.

Save A across $447A and store it in $1AB1,X. Set type $1919,X to $FE, both frame bytes $19E5,X and $19C3,X to $A1, attributes $19F6,X/$1A07,X to 1/0, and $1AF5,X/$1AC2,X to $A0/1. Tail-jump to $4342 with A=$0C.

Save A across $447A and store it in $1AB1,X. Set type $1919,X to $FD, both frame bytes $19E5,X and $19C3,X to $99, attributes $19F6,X/$1A07,X to 7/0, and $1AF5,X/$1AC2,X to $A0/9. Call $4342 with A=$0C, then call $71DB; use its returned A as X and store its returned Y at $1AD3,X.

Trigger callback for a hidden heart, entity type $FC; the record's argument in A is its sprite number. Save A on the stack. If slot zero at $1919 is occupied, increment $487F,X modulo 256, restore A and return. Otherwise set slot-zero type to $FC and call $5D2C. Its contact handler, through the table at $754E, is $763E, which adds 8 to the meter.
Set X=0 and call $43A2 with A=8. Restore the saved byte into $19C3; set $19F6 to 1, $1A07 and $1AE4 to 0, and $1AF5 to $A0, then return.

Trigger callback for a hidden hourglass, entity type $FB; the record's argument in A is its sprite number. Save A on the stack. If slot zero at $1919 is occupied, increment $487F,X modulo 256, restore A and return. Otherwise set slot-zero type to $FB and call $5D2C. Its contact handler, through the table at $754E, is $7646, which turns the status-panel hourglass back.
Set X=0 and call $4342 with A=$20. Restore the saved byte into $19C3; set $19F6 to 7, $1A07 to 0 and $1AF5 to $60, then return.
Clear $5D79 and shift $485F,X left four bits as a 16-bit value using $5D79 for the high byte. Add $1B, propagate carry, and store the resulting low and high bytes at $194C and $193B without X.

Clear $5D79 and shift $486F,X left four bits as a 16-bit value using $5D79 for the high byte. Add $59, propagate carry, and store the resulting low and high bytes at $1990 and $197F without X. Return.
Scratch high byte for the four-bit coordinate shifts at $5D2C and $5D52.

Patch A and X into the immediate operands at $5DAC and $5DB7. If cooldown $4DE1 is nonzero, clear carry and return without applying damage. Otherwise save Y in the operand at $5DAA and inspect bit 7 of the selected player flags at $4DE2,Y.

When protection bit 7 is set, decrement $4DDE modulo 256. If the result is zero, clear that bit in the selected player flags and call $77E2 with A=$0A. Shift the patched damage amount right once whether or not the charge reached zero.

Restore the saved Y, load the patched damage amount and call $77BC. Set cooldown $4DE1 to $28, set carry, restore the original X from the patched operand and return. The subtraction routine selects its own player index and floors a result whose sign bit is set.

Immediate operand of the LDY at $5DA9, which restores the Y the caller passed to $5D7A. $5D87 stores the incoming Y here once the damage cooldown at $4DE1 is zero, beside A at $5DAC and X at $5DB7; the load holds $FF. The restored Y does not survive: the meter subtraction at $77BC, called next, loads Y from $4DBD as its second instruction.
Patched damage value loaded by $5DAB and passed to meter subtraction $77BC. After that call set cooldown $4DE1 to 40, set carry and restore X through $5DB6.
Immediate operand restoring the entity index X after damage processing; $5D7D patches it before any damage branch.

Save the incoming A in $58. If entity flag bit 0 is set, call $43F0 with A=$0C. With world mode $7A zero, jump to $5E71; otherwise use the entity reload counter to choose release for values 2 or more, or a selector table for values 0 and 1. No resident instruction calls it: the loads' entity handlers jump here, 91 jumps in 30 loads, the first at $B230 in load 1.

Read $1B4A,X. Values 2 or more jump to $4454; zero selects the first handler selector table and one selects the second. Only the loads' handlers for types $01 to $21 jump to $5DB9 (91 JMP instructions), so the type that indexes either table stays within its 38 entries for types 0 to $25.

Use entity type $1919,X as an index into the first selector table at $5DFD when the counter is zero; otherwise use the second table at $5E23. Pass the resulting byte as Y to the handler-pointer dispatch at $5DEB. The type is $01 to $21, since only those types' handlers in the loads jump to $5DB9, and the bytes those types select are 0, 1, 2, 3, 8, $12 and $13, entries of the twenty-entry pointer tables at $5E49 and $5E5D.
Patch the low byte of the dispatch target from the indexed table.
Patch the high byte of the dispatch target from the indexed table.

Jump to the entity's handler with A = $58, the value passed to $5DB9. $5DEF and $5DF5 patch the target from $5E49,Y and $5E5D,Y, with Y the handler index (0–19) at $5DEB: taken from the type selector $5DFD (reload counter 0) or $5E23 (counter 1), from the stage callback's result ($5EB3, $5F6D), or 0 from $5F75, which releases the entity at $4454. The load holds JMP $FF00.

Low byte of the target of the JMP at $5DFA, whose high byte is $5DFC. The load holds $00 here, so the instruction reads JMP $FF00 until it is patched. $5DEF stores it from $5E49,Y and $5DF5 the high byte from $5E5D,Y, with Y the value in A at $5DEB; the jump runs with $58 in A. No other instruction writes it.

High byte of the JMP at $5DFA; the load holds $FF. $5DF5 stores it from $5E5D,Y and $5DEF stores the low byte at $5DFB from $5E49,Y, with Y the handler index the TAY at $5DEB takes from A, so the jump reaches one of the twenty entity handlers listed at $5E49.

Handler index for each entity type 0–$25 while the entity's reload counter $1B4A is 0, read by $5DDF with Y the type from $1919. The indexes name entries in the handler tables $5E49/$5E5D: 0 releases the entity ($4454), 1 runs $5C94, 2 runs $5C66, $12 runs $49E3 and $13 runs $4A12. The table for reload counter 1 follows at $5E23.

Handler index for each entity type 0–$25 while the entity's reload counter $1B4A is 1, read by $5DE8 with Y the type from $1919. The indexes name entries in the handler tables $5E49/$5E5D: 0 releases the entity ($4454), 3 runs $5F88, 8 runs $5FB0, $12 runs $49E3 and $13 runs $4A12.

Low bytes of twenty entity handlers, paired with the high bytes at $5E5D and copied by $5DEC into the jump at $5DFA. Index 0 to 19: $4454, $5C94, $5C66, $5F88, $5F90, $5F98, $5FA0, $5FA8, $5FB0, $5FE2, $6008, $4904, $48F1, $4917, $4939, $495B, $497D, $49B1, $49E3 and $4A12.

High bytes paired with the twenty handler-pointer low bytes at $5E49; $5DF2 reads entry Y into the high byte of the JMP at $5DFA. Y is the selector byte from $5DFD or $5E23, which is 0, 1, 2, 3, 8, $12 or $13, or, from $5EB3, $5F6D and $5F75, the result of the room record's callback after $5E71: 0, 9 (from 9 or from $F7 negated at $5EDE) or $0A. Entries 4–7 and $0B–$11 are never read here; their addresses are reached through the tables at $4A02 and $4A35.

Reached from $5DCB while world mode $7A is zero, which only the alternate update loop at $073F sets ($0799). If entity flag bit 0 is clear, jump to the release routine at $4454. Otherwise save the entity index in the operand at $5EAB and scan indices 16 down to 0: call $4454 for each whose $19B2 byte is nonzero and whose flag bit 0 is clear.

Call the meter-add routine with A=8, write $FE to sound-control state $2C15, then patch a JSR target from stage-record fields $4783,X and $4789,X selected by $7B. Restore the original entity index before invoking that callback.
Read $4783,X and patch the low operand byte at $5EAD of JSR $5EAC. The following lookup reads the high byte from $4789,X.
Read $4789,X and patch the high operand byte at $5EAE of JSR $5EAC, pairing it with the low byte at $5EAD.

Reload X with the entity index that $5E7B saved in the operand at $5EAB, then call the stage callback at $5EAC, whose address $5EA1 and $5EA7 patch from $4783,X and $4789,X for the stage record in $7B. The load holds JSR $FF00. A zero result goes to $5EB6, carry set to $5EC4, and any other value is used as a handler index at $5DEB.

Immediate operand of the LDX at $5EAA, which restores the entity index just before the record's result callback is called through the JSR at $5EAC. $5E7B stores the entity index X here before $5E7E–$5E90 use X to scan the 17 entity slots; no other instruction writes it. The load holds $FF here.

Low byte of the target of the JSR at $5EAC, whose high byte is $5EAE. The load holds $00 here, so the instruction reads JSR $FF00 until it is patched. $5EA1 stores it from $4783,X, byte 8 of the stage-object record selected by $7B, and $5EA7 the high byte from $4789,X (byte 9): the record's result callback, called after the LDX at $5EAA has restored the entity index that $5E7B saved. No other instruction writes it.
High operand byte of the JSR at $5EAC. The selected stage record supplies this byte at $5EA4; it is not a standalone instruction.
Use the callback flags to select effect setup: zero enters the zero-result path, a nonzero result with carry clear skips the setup, and a nonzero result with carry set branches according to its sign.

Save the zero callback result on the stack and clear the effect kind at $4D51, of which only the sign is read. Carry clear leaves it zero and selects the coin configuration at $5ECA; carry set decrements it to $FF and jumps to the money-bag configuration at $5EE4.

For a nonzero callback result with carry set, a negative value branches to $5EDB. A positive value is saved on the stack and stored in the effect kind at $4D51, where only its sign is read, and the coin configuration at $5ECA follows.
Set the positive effect frame base to $99, animation delay to $0A and sprite colour to $07, then initialize its sprite arrays.

Store the negative result in the effect kind at $4D51, where only its sign is read, negate it with eight-bit arithmetic and save the magnitude on the stack. The money-bag configuration at $5EE4 follows.
Set the negative effect frame base to $A1 and sprite colour to $01, then initialize its sprite arrays.
Copy eight motion speeds and directions, set lifetime to $C0 and animation phase to zero, and copy the selected entity position into eight effect positions.
Search display slots from index 31 down for the first free Y byte ($FF); save its index as effect slot 1. If none is free, the descending scan exits at $FF and saves that out-of-range index.
Search below the first saved index for the second free display slot and save it as effect slot 2. The loop has no separate failure check before storing the resulting Y value.
Search below the second saved index for the third free display slot and save it as effect slot 3. The loop has no separate failure check before storing the resulting Y value.
Search below the third saved index for the fourth free display slot and save it as effect slot 4. The loop has no separate failure check before storing the resulting Y value.

Clear the effect cursor at $4D50 and the eight flags at $4D21–$4D28, which puts all eight objects of the effect out: zero means an object is still out and nonzero that it is gone. Pull the saved callback-derived value; if it is zero, set the game-exit flag $0840 to $FF. Jump to the special-object dispatcher at $5DEB with that value in A as the handler index.

Eight initial effect speeds, $04,$03,$02,$01,$01,$02,$03,$04. The effect setup selects a speed by its slot index; the companion direction table at $5F80 makes the first and second halves travel oppositely.
Eight initial effect directions: four $FF bytes followed by four $01 bytes. These pair with the symmetric speed table at $5F78.
Load A=$05 and Y from $7F5E, then jump to the type-$FA initializer at $5FB5.
Load A=$10 and Y from $7F5F, then jump to $5FB5.
Load A=$10 and Y from $7F62, then jump to $5FB5.
Load A=$20 and Y from $7F60, then jump to $5FB5.
Load A=$50 and Y from $7F61, then jump to $5FB5.
Load A=$00 and Y from $7F63, then fall through to $5FB5.
Push the incoming A and patch the immediate operand at $5FC6 with Y. Call $447A, pop A into $1AB1,X and set $1919,X to $FA.
Immediate operand patched with the incoming Y at $5FB6. Copy it to $19E5,X and $19C3,X; set $19F6,X to 7, $1A07,X to zero and $1AF5,X to $A0. Call $4342 with A=$0C and return.
Call $447A and set $1919,X to $F9. Copy $7F6B to $19E5,X and $19C3,X; set $19F6,X to 7, $1A07,X to zero and $1AA0,X to 7. Call $4342 with A=$0C and return.
Call $447A, set $1919,X to $F8 and patch the immediate operand at $6020 with X. Load the selected player index from $4DBD, add $11 to $4DDB,X modulo 256 and call $77E2 with the result.

Immediate operand patched at $6010 to restore the entity index after $77E2. With that X, copy $7F6C to $19E5,X and $19C3,X; set $19F6,X to $0F, $1A07,X to zero and $1AA0,X to 7. Call $4342 with A=$0C and return.

Pickup types $FA and $F5–$EF, which the negative-type table at $2062/$2074 sends here: decrement the lifetime $1AF5,X and copy $19E5,X to $19C3,X. Load Y from $1AC2,X; if it is 7, check the lifetime at $606D. Otherwise read $607F,Y: a nonzero entry increments $1AC2,X, calls $4342 with that byte in A to move the pickup up, and returns without testing the lifetime.
For a zero table entry set $1A7E,X to 1, increment $1AC2,X and check the decremented countdown. Zero tail-jumps to $4454; $20 sets $1A8F,X to $FF; any other value returns.
For phase 7, a zero $1AF5,X tail-jumps to $4454; $20 sets $1A8F,X to $FF; any other value returns.

Rise amounts for the pickups at $603F, indexed by $1AC2,X: 6, 5, 4, 3, 2 and 1, each passed to $4342 to move the pickup up, then 0, which ends the rise: $605B sets $1A7E,X to 1 and the index steps to 7, after which $603F only counts down the pickup's lifetime.
Pickup types $F9 and $F8, which the negative-type table at $2062/$2074 sends here: copy $19E5,X to $19C3,X. If $1A7E,X is zero set it to 1; otherwise leave it unchanged. Return.
Patch $60D4 with the incoming X, load selected player index from $4DBD and store $4DCD,X shifted right one bit in the countdown at $60D6. Enter the conversion loop even when that countdown is zero.
Call $3C2A, $370B and $3C2A, then call $77BC with A=2 and $4B0E with A=8. Call $370B and $2B4C. Repeat while $2B4C returns with the zero flag clear; then enter the refill loop.
Call $3C2A and $370B, reload X from $4DBD, increment $4DCD,X and compare it with $4DCF,X. Repeat until they are equal, so this loop executes at least once. Restore the saved X from $60D4 and return.
Immediate operand patched at $6097 with the incoming X for restoration at $60D3.
Conversion countdown initialized from the selected $4DCD byte shifted right one bit and decremented, when nonzero, by $2B4C.

Check the first sampled map value at $61D6 against the six entries at $7F77–$7F7C and other per-load values. Matching entries can set or clear the negative $4DB3 movement latch, depending on $71 and horizontal offset $527C. A match with $7F76 decrements $4B0D only when it is at least 2. When $4DDD and $4DE1 permit it, matches with $7F75 or $7F7D invoke damage and set cooldown $50 or $3C. Otherwise the second sampled value at $61D7 and $7F7E–$7F80 select the value stored at $61D5; $7F7E=$FF stores $FF directly.

If the sampled map value equals the load’s tile at $7F76, decrement the hourglass countdown at $4B0D once more, provided it is at least 2. The hourglass tick at $4A43 decrements it again in the same pass of the main loop, so the glass runs at twice the speed while the player is at that tile. Loads 2, 8, 9, 11, 15, 17, 22, 25 and 28 set $7F76 to the tile that draws the top row of their pools; the other loads hold $FF there.
Movement modifier used after collision/map sampling. Referenced at $0A37 (LDA), $61D1 (STA), $6C42 (STA).
First sampled map value used by movement checks. Referenced at $60D7 (LDA), $6E86 (STA).
Second sampled map value used by movement checks. Referenced at $086C (LDA), $61BD (LDA), $6E9C (STA).

Copy 39 bytes from the address in $54/$55 to the address in $52/$53, starting at index Y. Each unrolled load/store increments Y; on return Y has advanced by 39 modulo 256. Entry $61DD skips the first copy and copies 38 bytes.
Alternate entry to the unrolled forward copy at $61D8: copy 38 bytes from ($54/$55),Y to ($52/$53),Y and leave Y advanced by 38 modulo 256.
