Copy 38 bytes from the address in $54/$55 to the address in $52/$53, starting at index Y and decrementing Y after each byte. Y has decreased by 38 modulo 256 on return.
Copy 38 bytes in ascending address order: for each base $D8C8–$D8ED, read base+X and write base+Y. The CPU memory configuration determines what these addresses access.
Copy 38 bytes in ascending address order: for each base $D9E0–$DA05, read base+X and write base+Y. The CPU memory configuration determines what these addresses access.
Copy 38 bytes in ascending address order: for each base $DAF8–$DB1D, read base+X and write base+Y. The CPU memory configuration determines what these addresses access.

Copy 39 bytes in descending address order: for each base $D8EE–$D8C8, read base+X and write base+Y. The entry six bytes later skips the first copy. The CPU memory configuration determines what these addresses access.
Alternate entry to the descending copy at $660A: copy 38 bytes from bases $D8ED down to $D8C8, reading base+X and writing base+Y. The CPU memory configuration determines what these addresses access.

Copy 39 bytes in descending address order: for each base $DA06–$D9E0, read base+X and write base+Y. The entry six bytes later skips the first copy. The CPU memory configuration determines what these addresses access.
Alternate entry to the descending copy at $66F5: copy 38 bytes from bases $DA05 down to $D9E0, reading base+X and writing base+Y. The CPU memory configuration determines what these addresses access.

Copy 39 bytes in descending address order: for each base $DB1E–$DAF8, read base+X and write base+Y. The entry six bytes later skips the first copy. The CPU memory configuration determines what these addresses access.
Alternate entry to the descending copy at $67E0: copy 38 bytes from bases $DB1D down to $DAF8, reading base+X and writing base+Y. The CPU memory configuration determines what these addresses access.
Updates an entity from a patched callback's displacement and can move an attached player or record contact. Its call target and intermediate values depend on entity state.
Read $1A18,X and patch the low operand byte at $68E6 of JSR $68E5. In this callback path, the matching high byte comes from $1A6D,X; the same fields have other uses in display and contact paths.
Read $1A6D,X and patch the high operand byte at $68E7 of JSR $68E5. Pair it with the callback low byte taken from $1A18,X.

Store the high byte read from $1A6D,X at $68E7, completing the operand of the JSR at $68E5; $68DC stored the low byte from $1A18,X. $68CB runs only for entity type $FF, from the negative-type table at $2062/$2074, and a type-$FF entity's record carries the callback address in bytes 7 and 9, which $369E copies to $1A18 and $1A6D. The bytes as loaded read JSR $FF00 until the first patch.
Low byte of the absolute JSR operand at $68E5, patched from $1A18,X at $68DC.
High byte of the absolute JSR operand at $68E5, patched from $1A6D,X at $68E2.

Reached when bit 7 of the entity's flags $192A,X is clear; a set bit goes to the horizontal path at $69DA instead. Pull the callback result from the stack. A negative value branches to $690F. Otherwise patch the immediate operand at $6905 with A, call $4368 and test $4DB8. If that byte is zero or X differs from $4DB9, continue at $6931; otherwise continue at $6904.
Load the immediate displacement patched at $6905, store it at $4DB4, call $0C2C and jump to $6931.
Immediate operand of the LDA at $6904, patched with the nonnegative callback result at $68F4.

If $4DB8 is zero, branch to $6939. Otherwise negate the negative callback result using EOR $FF, CLC and ADC 1, patch the immediate operand at $692A and call $4342. If $4DB8 is nonzero and X equals $4DB9, load the patched value into $4DB4 and call $0D7F; then continue at $6931. The negation is binary with decimal mode clear.
Immediate operand of the LDA at $6929, patched with the negated callback result at $6919.
Write $FF to $6A39, restore X from the immediate operand at $6937, and return.
Immediate operand of the LDX at $6936, patched with the entry X by $68CB.

Immediate motion byte patched from A at $6939. If player vertical-motion state is nonzero, or the display-slot test returns carry clear, the code negates this byte and calls the upward movement routine instead of checking overlap. With a display slot, it chooses width 25 when entity flag bit 0 is set, otherwise 17, and patches $6989.

With decimal mode clear, compare the halved player and display-slot X coordinates as eight-bit values. Subtract 10 from the entity coordinate; reject when that result is at least the player coordinate. Add the patched width and reject when the wrapped result is less than the player coordinate.

Immediate horizontal width patched to 17 or 25 at $6961. If the horizontal comparison passes, add 21 to player Y: ADC #20 receives carry set from the preceding successful comparison. Equality with the slot Y attaches immediately; a greater result rejects. Otherwise add the patched motion byte from $6942 with carry clear and attach when the result reaches or exceeds slot Y. Arithmetic wraps at eight bits and assumes decimal mode clear.

Subtract 21 and then $6942, with the borrow from the first subtraction, from $4CCF,Y. Store the result in the immediate operand at $69B2. Subtract that patched value from $49, negate the result and store it in $4DB4; call $0D7F.

Immediate operand patched at $69AB with the calculated attachment target. After $0D7F returns, restore X from $6937, clear $4DB6, $4D55 and $4DB3, set $4DB8 to $192A,X OR 2, save X in $4DB9, and jump to $6941 to move the entity.
Low temporary byte used while calculating entity motion. Referenced in the resident code at $6966 (STA), $696C (ROR), $6982 (CMP), $698A (CMP), $69DB (STA), $6A1B (ADC).
High temporary byte paired with $6A37 for entity motion. Referenced at $6972 (STA), $6979 (ROR), $697C (LDA).
Control byte used by the entity-motion collision path. Referenced at $0AD0 (STA), $213E (LDA), $68D6 (STA), $6933 (STA).

Read a byte from the sequence addressed by $54/$55, using entity slot X. $1AB1,X holds the sequence index, $1AC2,X a remaining repeat count and $1AD3,X the cached byte. Values $00–$7F and $C0–$FF are returned directly. $81–$BF consumes the next byte and returns it 1–63 times in total; $80 resets the index to zero and reads again. A stream that repeatedly resets without yielding a value does not terminate.

Machine set-up: SEI and CLD, $00=$0F and $01=$35 (RAM throughout with I/O at $D000), screen blanked with $D011=$0B and VIC interrupts off with $D01A=$F0. It points the RAM vectors at NMI $11E8, reset $121B (an RTI) and IRQ $005D, turns off both CIAs' interrupts with $7F to $DC0D and $DD0D and reads them to clear any pending, selects VIC bank 3 ($C000–$FFFF) by clearing the low two bits of $DD00, and acknowledges the VIC with $D019=1. Called from $7A73 and jumped to from $2B6F and $7B55.

Set sprite multicolours $D025 to 2 and $D026 to 5, then reset the 32 display slots from $1F down to 0: clear each slot’s X low and high bytes, flags and extra flags, write $FF to its Y-or-free byte, colour and sprite pointer, and store its own index in the order list at $03,X. Each pass also clears $4CCE, sprite priority and both expansion registers, and writes $FF to sprite enable and multicolour select. Then seed slots 0 and 1: X low $20 and $00, Y $40 and $41, sprite pointer $10 for both, colour 2 for slots 0 to 2, and extra flag 1 for slot 0.

Write zero to six runs of 24 bytes, 64 bytes apart: $D818–$D82F, $D858–$D86F, $D898–$D8AF, $D8D8–$D8EF, $D918–$D92F and $D958–$D96F. Its one caller, at $033A in the title setup, runs with $35 in the processor port, so the writes go to colour RAM. A screen row is 40 cells, so the runs are not rows: they start at offsets 24, 88, 152, 216, 280 and 344 from the top-left cell.
Initializes shared state and both player slots, including score, item, status and meter values. Some fields are reused by later paths.
Set $4D9E/$4D9F/$4DA0/$4DA1/$4DA2/$4DAC and $7A to $FF. Clear $4DBB, $0840, $4DE1, $4DDD, $5243, $4DB0 and $4C31.
Copy $7F49 to $49, $7F47 to $47 and $7F48 to $48. Set $61D5, $E1 and $4C32 to 1. Copy $7F46 to $4A and store that byte minus $66, modulo 256, at $1177.
Clear $4CB1, set $4CB2 to 7 and call $370B. The callback may change memory before execution continues.
Copy $7F45 to $6F and $7F43/$7F44 to $529C/$529D.

Reset the hourglass for a new area: add 8 to $4DCD with eight-bit wrap, set $4B0D to 1 and $4DD4 to 6, then return. The display setup at $0383 calls the hourglass tick at $4A43 next, which finds picture 6, takes the 8 back from the selected player’s meter and draws picture 0. The addition goes to $4DCD, the first player’s meter, whichever player is selected.

Draws the status panel. Copies the 200-byte screen template $4DE4–$4EAB to the top five screen rows at $C000–$C0C7, copies the colour templates $4EAC, $4EBA (used for rows 1 and 2), $4EC8 and $4ED6 to columns 0–13 of colour rows 0–4, writes colour $0F to columns 35–39 of rows 0 and 4, and clears the meter sprite $C400–$C43F. The colour stores reach colour RAM only while I/O is switched in. Called from $0394.
Prepares sprite fragments through one of two paths selected by state. Its $d8xx addresses are RAM beneath I/O when its caller banks I/O out.
Expands a 20-by-10 map window into 2-by-2 metatiles in the alternate screen buffer, adjusts odd origins and updates colour data.
Patch the low byte of the map-row source address.
Patch the high byte of the map-row source address.

Read the next metatile number from the map row, with X as the column. $6D33 and $6D39 patch the row's address into the operand from the load's row tables $85CF,Y and $8620,Y, with Y the map row (half of $7F4E) and X starting at half of $7F4D; the routine draws 20 columns of 10 rows. The load holds $FF00.
Low byte of the address operand of the LDA at $6D41, which reads the next metatile number from the map row. $6D33 patches it for each row from the table at $85CF,Y.
High byte of the address operand of the LDA at $6D41, which reads the next metatile number from the map row. $6D39 patches it for each row from the table at $8620,Y.
Save the current Y index in the immediate operand restored after drawing.
Save the current X index in the immediate operand restored after drawing.

Immediate operand of the LDY at $6D65, which restores the map-row index after the four character stores at $6D4D–$6D63 used Y as a screen offset. $6D44 stores it, and $6D47 saves X at $6D68 beside it; the load holds $FF.
Immediate operand holding the map-column X saved at $6D47. After restoring X and Y, increment X and add 2 to the 16-bit destination pointer at $56/$57.
Decrement the 20-column counter and repeat at $6D41 while it is nonzero. At the end of a row, increment Y and add 40 to $56/$57, carrying into the high byte.
Decrement the 10-row counter and reload the map-row pointer at $6D2B while it is nonzero. Each metatile uses the indexed bytes from $81CF, $82CF, $83CF and $84CF as a two-by-two character block.
Set temporary visible bounds from $7F4D and $7F4E, with right equal to left plus $25 and bottom equal to top plus $12, modulo 256.
If bit 0 of $7F4E is set, put $C4 in $46 and call $2E77. If bit 0 of $7F4D is set, toggle bit 2 of $46 and call $2C8D.
Store final bounds from $7F4D and $7F4E, with right equal to left plus $26 and bottom equal to top plus $13, modulo 256, then tail-jump to $6F3E.
Remaining metatile columns in the screen expansion loop. Referenced at $6D3E (STA), $6D75 (DEC).
Remaining metatile rows in the screen expansion loop. Referenced at $6D23 (STA), $6D86 (DEC).

Waits for port-2 Fire to be released and then pressed. While it waits for the press, each pass scans the 200 screen bytes from $C0C8 down to $C001 for the code $60; every sixth pass that finds one toggles bit 0 of that cell's colour at $6DFC. Called from the title at $0324, from $05A3 and $0713, from the message wait at $786B and from load 31 at $99AA.
Return to the caller: Fire on port 2 has been released and then pressed. The BNE at $6DF9 falls through to here when $70, the Fire bit that $3C4C samples from $DC00, is zero.

For the first matching screen byte in offsets 200 through 1, decrement the counter; on zero, toggle bit 0 of the matching colour RAM cell and reload six. With no match, leave the counter and colours unchanged.

Countdown for the colour blink in the Fire wait at $6DDE, 6 at the start. $6DFC decrements it on each pass that finds screen code $60; at zero the cell's colour bit 0 is toggled and $6E0B reloads 6. Referenced at $6DFC (DEC), $6E0B (STA).
Computes world-space view origins and selected map cells from viewport and fine-scroll state. Arithmetic and cached cell values depend on the current mode.

This immediate operand is patched to $4D69 XOR 7 and added to the low byte of the Y origin; the carry is added to its high byte. The following instructions multiply $569B by eight into $56A5/$56A6 and patch $4D6A XOR 7 into $6E64.

Multiply $569B by eight into the 16-bit pair $56A5/$56A6. XOR $4D6A with 7, patch that value into $6E64 and add it to the pair; the preceding block calculates $569F/$56A0 the same way from $569D and $4D69.

This immediate operand is patched to $4D6A XOR 7 and added to the low byte of the X origin; the carry is added to its high byte. When $7A is nonzero, the following instructions sample two map rows at column $6F3C into $61D6/$61D7. They then store the shifted player X at $4DAE.

If $7A is nonzero, use row index $6F3D and the following row to read two little-endian pointers from $85CF/$8620. At column offset $6F3C, copy the two selected bytes into $61D6/$61D7. If $7A is zero, leave those bytes unchanged.
Shift the low bit of $48 into bit 7 of $47 shifted right once; store the resulting eight-bit value in $4DAE and return.

Compute map column $6F3C, row $6F3D and horizontal and vertical offsets $527C/$527D from player coordinates, fine scrolling and the view origin. With decimal mode clear, the horizontal calculation retains nine low bits before its three right shifts, and the carry from the last shift enters the addition of $569B. The vertical calculation subtracts $43 and then $4D69 without resetting carry: an underflow in the first subtraction subtracts one more. An odd $569B adds 8 before masking the horizontal offset; an odd $569D masks the vertical offset to 3 bits. Arithmetic wraps; the code does not clamp indices.
Low X scratch byte used by view-coordinate calculations. Referenced in the resident code at $6EAF (STA), $6EB9 (LDA), $6EBF (STA), $6ECA (LDA), $6ED0 (LDA), $6ED6 (STA), $6EE1 (LDA).
High X scratch byte paired with $6F3A. Referenced in the resident code at $6EB6 (STA), $6EC2 (LDA), $6EC7 (STA), $6ED9 (LDA), $6EDE (STA), $6EE4 (LSR).

Tile-column coordinate produced by the view calculations. Referenced in the resident code at $0481 (LDA), $0C51 (LDY), $0C73 (LDY), $0EA1 (INC), $0EB1 (LDY), $0EBF (DEC), $103B (DEC), $104B (LDY), $1058 (INC), $47A5 (CMP), $48C6 (CMP), $6E81 (LDY), $6E97 (LDY), $6EF1 (STA). 67 instructions in 22 loads also use it, the first at $9669 in load 2.

Tile-row coordinate produced by the view calculations. Referenced in the resident code at $0458 (LDA), $0C43 (LDY), $0C65 (LDY), $0EA4 (LDY), $103E (LDY), $47AD (CMP), $48CE (CMP), $6E74 (LDY), $6E89 (LDY), $6F1F (STA). 12 instructions in 12 loads also use it, the first at $95A0 in load 6.
Switches screen buffer and maps displayed character values to colour RAM for 20 rows of 39 characters.

Row countdown shared by the two colour-mapping loops. $6F54 sets it to $13 and $6F66 decrements it after each 39-byte row; $70E2 sets it to $13 and $70F8 decrements it after each 40-byte row. Each loop ends when the decrement goes negative, after 20 rows.

Compare $4DCD,Y with $4DA2 and return if equal. Otherwise cache that value, clear 64 bytes at $C400–$C43F, load the selected player index from $4DBD and compute half of (its $4DCD value plus one) using ADC and ROR. Store $21 at $4C6F/$4C70/$6E when the sum is odd, or $20 when it is even.

Load the half meter value, (meter + 1) / 2, that $6FA5 stored in the operand at $6FBA. If it is at least 20, draw a 20-unit segment with X=0 (the clearing loop leaves X at 0), then draw the rest with X=$18, eight rows lower. Otherwise draw the whole value with X=0. The meter never exceeds its limit at $4DCF, which starts at $28 and grows to at most $50, so the value is at most 40 and the rest at most 20.

Immediate half-meter value loaded at $6FB9. Compare with 20; values below 20 enter $6FCD directly. Otherwise subtract 20 using the comparison carry, save the remainder at $6FCA, draw 20 units through $6FCD, and reload that remainder before drawing the second segment.

Immediate operand of the LDA at $6FC9, which reloads the meter remainder (half value minus 20, 0–20) after the first segment's draw at $6FC6 used A. $6FC1 stores it; the load holds $FF. The LDX #$18 that follows places the second segment eight rows lower.
For a remainder below 8, fetch the mask from $6FFF,Y and store it in eight bytes separated by three positions at $C400,X. For a remainder of at least 8, enter $6FEE.

Write A into eight meter bitmap bytes at $C400+X, $C403+X, $C406+X, $C409+X, $C40C+X, $C40F+X, $C412+X and $C415+X, then return. These addresses are three bytes apart; X is an eight-bit index added to each 16-bit base address.
Write eight $FF bytes through $6FD5, subtract 8 from the saved remainder, increment X and repeat at $6FCD.
Saved meter remainder loaded at $6FF6. Subtract 8 with carry set, increment X and jump to segment drawing at $6FCD. The arithmetic follows a completed eight-unit segment.

Eight partial-byte masks for the meter renderer at $6FCD. Index n from 0 to 7 gives n leading one bits and 8 minus n zero bits, from $00 to $FE; the full eight-bit case is handled by the separate $FF segment path.

One $FF byte after the eight partial-meter masks at $6FFF. It would be the mask for 8, but the lookup at $6FD2 is reached only with Y below 8: $6FCD sends 8 and above to the full-segment path at $6FEE, which loads $FF as an immediate. No instruction in the resident part or in any load reads this byte.
Patch $7117 with the incoming X, call the compressed-screen decoder at $7011, then tail-jump to the colour-mapping routine at $70D0, which restores X from $7117.

Set $54 to $4D71 and $55 to ($46 XOR 4) plus $4D8A modulo 256. Set $7063 and $7062 to 10, set Y and $7061 to zero, and enter the compressed-token loop. The input offset is eight-bit; the source pointer is not advanced here.
Read a token from ($52),Y. A byte other than $FF is drawn once by $7064. Return if $7062 is zero; otherwise increment Y and read another token if Y is nonzero, returning if it wrapped.

After $FF, increment Y and save the next byte in the immediate operand at $704D; increment Y again and save the next byte as $7060. Draw the saved byte repeatedly until $7062 becomes zero or decrementing $7060 reaches zero. A zero initial count underflows after the first draw. On a completed run, increment Y and jump back to $702E.
Immediate operand patched at $7043 with the metatile byte following a $FF run marker.
Remaining run count loaded by $7049 and decremented after each draw while the screen remains active.
Current character-column offset within the pair of rows being drawn; advanced by 2 for each metatile.
Decoder-active byte initialized to 10 and cleared after the tenth metatile row.
Metatile-row countdown initialized to 10 and decremented after each 20-metatile row.

If $7062 is zero return. Otherwise save Y in $70CA, multiply the incoming metatile byte by 4, add the pointer at $5A/$5B and patch the source address at $708A/$708B. Copy four bytes to ($54),Y at the current column plus offsets 0, 1, 40 and 41.

Low byte of the address operand of the LDA at $7089, which reads the metatile's four character codes. $707D patches it with the low byte of the pointer at $5A/$5B plus four times the metatile number; $7084 patches the high byte at $708B.

High byte of the absolute,X source operand at $7089, patched at $7084 after calculating $5A/$5B plus four times the metatile index. The drawing loop uses that patched source to read the four character codes; changing this byte changes their source page.
Add 2 to $7061. At $28 reset it to zero, add $50 to $54/$55 and decrement $7063; when the count reaches zero clear $7062. Restore the saved input Y from $70CA and return.
Branch to $70C9 when the row counter decremented at $70BD is nonzero. If the counter became zero, fall through to the redundant BNE at $70C2 and then clear the decoder-active byte at $7062.
This second BNE has the same target as the BNE at $70C0 and no intervening instruction changes flags. If execution falls through the first branch, zero is set and this branch also falls through.
Immediate operand patched at $706A with the compressed-input Y offset for restoration after drawing a metatile.
Four destination offsets within a two-by-two metatile: 0, 1, 40 and 41.
Set the source pointer $54/$55 to low byte $C8 and high byte $46 XOR 4; set destination $52/$53 to $D8C8. Set $6F85 to $13 and enter the row loop at $70E5.

For 40 bytes in a row, use each source character byte as an index into the table at $6C/$6D and write the selected byte to the destination. Save and restore the row offset through the patched operand at $70F0.
Immediate operand patched by $70E9 to restore the row offset after using Y as the colour-table index.

Decrement the row counter. If it becomes negative, restore X from $7117 and return; otherwise add 40 to both source and destination pointers and process another row. Starting from $13 processes 20 rows.
Immediate operand of $7116, patched by the entry at $7008 with X for restoration after the colour mapping.

Call the selected stage resource loader at $7130, then write $30 to CPU port $01 and copy 80 bytes from $C808–$C857 to RAM $D7B0–$D7FF in descending index order. Write $35 to $01 and return. The copy requires RAM visibility beneath I/O; the preceding loader has separate behavior.
Use X to select low and high bytes from $7F9E/$7FA5 into $6C/$6D, $7F82/$7F89 into $5A/$5B, and $7F90/$7F97 into $52/$53. Call $7008. The code uses X again after that call without restoring it.

Use the returned X to load a source pointer from $7FAC/$7FB3 into $52/$53. Set $4D69 to zero and $4D6A to 4; copy $7FBA,X to $6F, $7FC1,X to $529C and $7FC8,X to $529D. Toggle bit 2 of $46 and continue at $717C.
Banks I/O out, copies eight pages from a source pointer to RAM at $d000–$d7ff and restores the CPU port to $35. The destination high byte is patched during the copy.

Copy 256 bytes per page from ($52),Y to the address whose high byte is patched at $7188, starting at Y=0 and then descending from $FF to 1. Increment $53 and $7188 after each page. After eight pages restore $7188 to $D0 and write $35 to the processor port.
High byte of the destination address at $7186, incremented after each page and reset to $D0 after the eight-page copy.

Write $0A and $09 to VIC sprite multicolour registers $D025 and $D026. Copy X to $4C73/$4C74 and Y to $4CD3/$4CD4. Clear $4C53, $4C54, $4CB3 and $4C33; set $4C34 and $4CB4 to 1, and $4C93/$4C94 to $97/$98. Clear $79 and return.
Subtract $005A from the 16-bit Y position $197F,X:$1990,X modulo 65536, shift it right four bits and retain the low byte at $7226. Then subtract $001B from $193B,X:$194C,X modulo 65536.

Save the low byte of the adjusted X position, shift the adjusted 16-bit X position right four bits and retain the low result at $7225. Compare the original adjusted X low nibble with 7. Return A=the incoming entity index, X=$7225, Y=$7226 and carry set exactly when that nibble is at least 7.
Low byte of the adjusted X coordinate after four right shifts, returned in X by $71DB.
Low byte of the adjusted Y coordinate after four right shifts, returned in Y by $71DB.
Return carry clear when $4DDD is nonzero or $49 equals $FE. Otherwise construct a contact rectangle and call $75E3.
Set the first rectangle to X=$4DAE+2, Y=$49+9, width 8 and height 12, with byte additions modulo 256. Call $75E3; return immediately if it clears carry.
On carry set from $75E3, call $727F and then $72FC. If $72FC returns carry set, write $FF to $4DB0 and $0E to $1177; otherwise write 1 and zero respectively. Return carry set.

Six recoil speeds: 6, 5, 4, 8, 3 and 2. $727F loads Y from the selected player's armour profile $4DD9 and $728B copies entry Y to the horizontal speed at $4DAF; the duration comes from the paired table at $7279. The profile is 0 after the player set-up at $6BE4 and 1 to 5 once armour is bought, since each shop's items 6–10 store their item number minus 5, so every entry is used.

Six recoil durations, 5, 4, 4, 4, 3 and 3, one per armour profile. $7291 loads entry Y, with Y the selected player's profile $4DD9 from $7288, and $7298 stores it in the vertical-state countdown at $1178. The profile is 0 after the player set-up at $6BE4 and 1 to 5 once armour is bought, since each shop's items 6–10 store their item number minus 5, so every entry is used.

Save the incoming X and Y in the operands at $7295 and $7297. Take the selected player's armour profile $4DD9,X as Y: 0 from $6BE4 at the start, 1–5 after an armour purchase (items 6–10, which store the item number minus 5). Copy the recoil speed $7273,Y to $4DAF and load the duration from $7279,Y. Restore X and Y and continue at $7298, which stores the duration.
Immediate operand patched by $727F to restore the incoming X.
Immediate operand patched by $7282 to restore the incoming Y.
Store A at $1178, set $4DB3, $4DB5 and $4D55 to 1, and return.

Map-trigger callback, named by trigger records in loads 6, 9, 18, 19, 20, 23, 26 and 27; the dispatcher at $48BF jumps here with the record's argument in A and its index in X, after decrementing $487F,X. Push A, increment $487F,X, which puts the count back, and patch the saved-X operand at $72C0. If $527D is below $0B, restore A and X and return. Otherwise, if $1919 is zero, initialize a temporary entity at $72CA; if nonzero, discard the saved A, restore X, load A=$10 and branch to $7298.
Increment the trigger count at $487F,X; the following STX at $72AF patches the saved-X operand at $72C0.
Immediate operand patched by $72AF with the incoming X; both return paths restore that index.
The preceding LDA #$10 sets Z clear, so this BNE is unconditional in ordinary execution.
Call $5D2C, then set $1AB1 to 8 and $19F6 to $0F. Restore the saved A into $19E5 and $19C3, set $1919 to $2B and jump to $72BF, which restores X and enters the $10-duration recoil path.
Decrement $1AB1,X modulo 256. If it becomes zero, tail-jump to $4454. Otherwise set $19C3,X to $19E5,X plus 2 when the decremented byte is odd or plus zero when it is even, modulo 256, then return.

Save Y in the immediate operand at $7328 and select the entity's display slot from $1A29,X. Form an eight-bit half-coordinate by shifting the low bit of $4C4F,Y into bit 7 of $4C6F,Y; when bit 0 of $192A,X is set, add 6 with eight-bit wrap. Compare that result with the analogous half-coordinate from player $48:$47. Return A as the adjusted entity half-coordinate and carry set when it is greater than or equal to the player half-coordinate. X is unchanged and Y is restored. The restoring LDY changes N and Z after the comparison; carry still reflects CMP.

Compare the entity half-coordinate in A with the player half-coordinate patched into this immediate operand by $7321. The following LDY restores Y and replaces the comparison's N and Z flags, but preserves its carry.

Immediate operand of CMP at $7325; the instruction uses this byte as its arithmetic or comparison input. Direct stores or updates at $7321 write this operand, replacing the byte the load holds here. The following instruction at $7327 is LDY with its own immediate operand.
Immediate operand of the LDY at $7327; $72FC stores the caller's Y here before selecting a display slot.
Call the player attack-box routine at $7430 first. If it returns carry set, return immediately; otherwise continue to the entity-contact scan at $7330.

Save the original entity index X. If its display-slot byte at $1A29,X is zero, return carry clear with X restored. Otherwise save Y for $74BE. When $6F equals 1, use twice the selected player's action tier, modulo 256, as damage to the original entity and jump to the shared subtraction at $74BE. For other $6F values scan the entity types beginning at $7358.

Scan entity indexes 16 down through 0 for type $27. For each match, build the rectangle at $7367 and test overlap. On the first overlap use damage 1; after exhausting this type, continue to the $29 scan at $7396.

For this $27 entity's display slot, form half its X from the low bit of $4C4F,Y and $4C6F,Y, add 4, and use width 4. Add 13 to $4CCF,Y for the top and use height 8. Values wrap to eight bits. Test the rectangle at $75E3; a hit selects damage 1 and marks this scanned entity.
Scan indexes 16 down through 0 for type $29 after all $27 candidates miss. The first overlapping candidate selects damage 2; if none overlaps, continue to type $28 at $73D4.

For this $29 entity's display slot, form the half X coordinate, add 3 and use width 6; add 10 to its Y and use height 11. Values wrap to eight bits. Test the rectangle at $75E3; a hit selects damage 2 and marks this scanned entity.
Scan indexes 16 down through 0 for type $28 after all $27 and $29 candidates miss. The first overlap selects damage 3; otherwise restore the original X and return carry clear.

For this $28 entity's display slot, form the half X coordinate, add 1 and use width 10; add 5 to its Y and use height 15. Values wrap to eight bits. Test the rectangle at $75E3; a hit selects damage 3 and marks this scanned entity.

Save the selected damage in the immediate operand at $74C5, set $1B17,X to $80 for the scanned entity, restore the original entity index from $742F and subtract the damage from its $1A6D value via $74BE. That routine returns carry set.
Saved entity X index while performing contact checks. Referenced at $7330 (STX), $7354 (LDX), $7429 (LDX).

Return carry clear when the attack-contact budget at $5285 is zero, player Y at $49 is $FE, the selected player's action tier at $4DDB,Y is zero, or the player frame at $4A is neither $6E nor $7C. Otherwise build a player attack rectangle and test it against the already prepared second rectangle. A miss returns carry clear without spending the budget.

Set the attack box Y to $49 plus $0D, its height to 3, and its width to 5 plus the selected player's action tier. All values wrap to eight bits. When $1177 is nonzero, set the box X to $4DAE plus 8; when it is zero, use the left-facing calculation at $747B.
Set the left-facing attack box X to $4DAE minus (box width minus 4), with eight-bit wrap. The intermediate offset is patched into the immediate operand at $7489 before the subtraction.
Patched left-facing attack offset subtracted by SBC at $7488 after carry is set. Store the result in attack-box X $762A and continue into the rectangle-overlap test at $748D.
Call the rectangle-overlap test with the box just prepared and the existing second box. Return carry clear on a miss; on carry set, continue to spend one contact and apply damage.

Decrement the attack-contact budget, preserve Y through the immediate operand at $74BF, and use the selected player's action tier as the damage. When bit $20 of that player's flags is set, decrement $4DDF and double the damage byte even on the contact that makes the countdown zero.

Decrement the Gauntlet counter. If it becomes zero, clear bit $20 of the selected player's flags and call $7A91 with A=$0C for the “Gauntlet is broken.” message before doubling this contact's damage. A zero starting counter wraps to $FF.
Shift the patched damage byte at $74C5 left one bit, discarding the high bit. This doubles damage modulo 256 before the shared health subtraction.

Restore Y from the immediate operand at $74BF, subtract the patched damage byte at $74C5 from $1A6D,X, and store zero on borrow. When the result is nonzero, set $1A8F,X to 8. Return carry set in either case. The same subtraction entry is also used by entity-contact paths.
Saved Y immediate in LDY at $74BE. Restore Y, load entity health/parameter $1A6D,X, set carry and execute the patched damage subtraction at $74C4.

Damage operand of SBC at $74C4. Carry is set at $74C3, so subtract this byte from the incoming health. Clamp a borrow to zero and store $1A6D,X; nonzero health also sets $1A8F,X to 8. Return with carry set. The parent entry $74BE restores Y before this subtraction.

Scan entity indexes from $10 down to zero. Skip nonnegative $1919,X values and those whose $1902 slot test returns carry clear; otherwise check the display mode at $74E6. A contact dispatch tail-jumps to its selected handler rather than resuming this scan.
If $7A is nonzero, continue to the contact rectangle. If it is zero, skip this entity unless $19B2,X is nonzero.

Build rectangle A with X=$4DAE+4, Y=$49+9, width 4 and height 12. Use the entity display slot from $1A29,X to build rectangle B with its 16-bit X shifted right once plus 2, Y=$4CCF,Y+5, width 8 and height 16. Call $75E3; carry set enters $7536, otherwise continue scanning.

Negate the entity type $1919,X modulo 256 into Y, use Y to select low and high target bytes from $754E and $7560, patch the jump at $754B and execute it. Only negative types reach here (the BPL at $74DB skips the others), and the negative types that the entity records and the set-up routines store run from $FF down to $EF, so Y is 1 to $11, within the 18 entries.
Patch the dispatch target low byte from the contact-handler table.
Patch the dispatch target high byte from the contact-handler table.

Store the high byte read from $7560,Y at $754D, completing the operand of the JMP at $754B; $7542 stored the low byte from $754E,Y. Y is the negated entity type, 1 to $11 for the negative types $FF to $EF that reach $7536. The bytes as loaded read JMP $FF00 until the first patch.
Low byte of the contact-handler jump, patched by $7542 before $754B executes.
High byte of the contact-handler jump, patched by $7548 before $754B executes.

Low bytes of the contact handlers for the negative entity types, paired with the high bytes at $7560 and indexed by the negated type, so index 1 is type $FF. $753F copies the low byte to $754C. Types $FF, $F7 and $F6 go to $74E2 (no action), $FE and $FD to $7632, $FC and $F5 to $763E, $FB to $7646, $FA to $7656, $F9 to $7661, $F8 to $7707, $F4 to $7678, $F3 to $7688, $F2 to $769D, $F1 to $76B2, $F0 to $76C7 and $EF to $76CD. Entry 0 ($74E2) is never read, since positive types skip the dispatch at $74DB.

High bytes of the contact handlers, paired with the lows at $754E. $7536 negates the entity type into Y, $7542 and $7548 copy the pair into the operand at $754C/$754D, and the JMP at $754B goes there. Only negative types reach this path ($74DB skips the rest), and they run from $FF to $EF, indexes 1–17.
Scan slots 7 down to 0, testing only slots whose $4D21,X byte is zero. Return after slot 0.

Set the first rectangle to X=$4DAE+4, Y=$49+9, width 4 and height 12. Set the second X to the low byte of the 16-bit $4D31,X:$4D29,X shifted right once plus 2, Y=$4D39+5, width 8 and height 16. Call $75E3; if carry is clear continue the scan.
For an overlap, set $4D21,X to 1, save X at $75E2 and call $4B0E with A=2. Call $7874 with A=$15 when $4D51 is negative or A=5 otherwise. Restore X and continue the scan.
Slot index saved across the score and amount callbacks by the $7572 contact scan.

In binary arithmetic, compute B's bottom as ($762F+$7631) modulo 256 and its right as ($762E+$7630) modulo 256, storing them at $7628/$7629. Compare the rectangles using the following eight-bit tests. The routine does not clear decimal mode itself.

Return carry clear if A's X is at least B's computed right. Otherwise add A's width and B's width to A's X, discarding carry after each addition; return carry clear if that result is below B's right. Thus touching on the tested left edge can pass while touching on the tested right edge fails.

Return carry clear if A's Y is at least B's computed bottom. Otherwise add A's height; carry from that sum returns set immediately. If there is no carry, add B's height; carry again returns set immediately. With no carry from either sum, compare the result with B's bottom and return carry set when it is at least that value, clear otherwise.
Return the carry from the vertical tests. The following $7626 entry clears carry and returns for a failed test.

Shared collision-test scratch: the first two bytes are the second box's computed bottom and right edges; the remaining bytes hold the two boxes' coordinates and dimensions. Arithmetic is 8-bit and uses carry conditions.
Temporary right edge used by the second collision rectangle. Referenced at $75F4 (STA), $75FA (CMP), $7607 (CMP).

X of the first collision rectangle, read by $75E3 at $75F7. Set from $4DAE plus 10 or 0 at $119A/$11AB, plus 2 at $7245, plus 4 at $7502 and $7590, and for the attack box plus 8 at $7475 or minus the width less 4 at $748A. $7375, $73B3 and $73F1 set it to half the slot X of a type $27, $29 or $28 entity plus 4, 3 or 1.

Y of the first collision rectangle, read by $75E3 at $760C. Set to $49 plus 6 at $11B8, $49 plus 9 at $7237, $74F4 and $7582, and $49 plus $0D at $7456 for the attack box. $7383, $73C1 and $73FF set it to the slot Y of a type $27, $29 or $28 entity plus 13, 10 or 5.

Width of the first collision rectangle, added by $75E3 at $7600. Set to 4 at $11C2, $737A, $7507 and $7595, to 8 at $724A, 6 at $73B8 and 10 at $73F6. For the attack box $7467 stores 5 plus the selected player's action tier, and $747B reads it back.
Height of the first collision rectangle, added by $75E3 at $7615. Set to 11 at $11BD and $73C6, to 12 at $723C, $74F9 and $7587, to 8 at $7388, 15 at $7404, and 3 at $745B for the attack box.

X origin of the second collision rectangle. Referenced in the resident code at $7518 (STA), $75A3 (STA), $75ED (LDA), $7944 (STA). 7 instructions in 3 loads also use it, the first at $A622 in load 14.

Y origin of the second collision rectangle. Referenced in the resident code at $7526 (STA), $75B1 (STA), $75E3 (LDA), $7954 (STA). 7 instructions in 3 loads also use it, the first at $A630 in load 14.

Width of the second collision rectangle. Referenced in the resident code at $751D (STA), $75A8 (STA), $75F1 (ADC), $7604 (ADC), $794A (STA). 5 instructions in 3 loads also use it, the first at $A627 in load 14.

Height of the second collision rectangle. Referenced in the resident code at $752B (STA), $75B6 (STA), $75E7 (ADC), $761B (ADC), $795A (STA). 5 instructions in 3 loads also use it, the first at $A635 in load 14.
Push $1AB1,X, call $4454 to release the entity, restore the saved byte into A, call $771F to calculate and display the reward, then return. Saving the byte preserves it across the release reset.

Contact handler that turns the hourglass back, selected through the table at $754E for entity type $FB, the hidden hourglass that $5CFE creates. Call $4B0E with A=2 to add to the score, write 1 to the flag at $4DD3 and to the countdown at $4B0D so that the next call of $4A43 takes the backward step, then release the entity’s display.

Saved Y operand of LDY at $7673, followed by a tail jump to entity release at $4454. The following separate entry $7678 preserves Y at $7684 and X at $7682 across meter-to-score conversion $6097, then begins restoring those registers.

Immediate operand of the LDX at $7681, which restores X after the $6097 call, before the jump to $4454. $767B stores X here (with Y at $7684, stored at $7678); no other instruction writes it. The load holds $FF here.
Saved Y operand at $7683, restored after meter-to-score conversion. Tail-jump to entity release $4454 after the register restoration.

Save X and Y in the immediate operands at $7697 and $7699, call $76E9 to set the Gauntlet flag and its ten-contact counter, and display message 11, “Wore the Gauntlet.” Restore X and Y and release the entity's display slots.

Immediate operand of the LDX at $7696, which restores X after message 11 (“Wore the Gauntlet.”) is prepared through $77E2, before the jump to $4454. $768B stores X here (with Y at $7699, stored at $7688); no other instruction writes it. The load holds $FF here.

Immediate LDY operand patched with incoming Y by the message-11 handler at $7688. After calling the flag helper and message routine, the handler restores X from $7697 and Y here, then tail-jumps to $4454.
Save incoming X and Y in the immediate operands at $76AC/$76AE. Call $76F3 to set selected-player flag $80 and counter $4DDE=5, pass A=9 to $77E2, restore X and Y, then tail-jump to $4454.

Immediate operand of the LDX at $76AB, which restores X after message 9 is prepared through $77E2, before the jump to $4454. $76A0 stores X here (with Y at $76AE); no other instruction writes it. The load holds $FF here.
Immediate LDY operand patched with incoming Y at $769D. The message-9 handler reloads X from $76AC and Y here after its calls, then jumps to the display-slot release entry at $4454.

Immediate operand of the LDX at $76C0, which restores X after message 5 is prepared through $77E2, before the jump to $4454. $76B5 stores X here (with Y at $76C3, stored at $76B2); no other instruction writes it. The load holds $FF here.

Immediate operand of LDY at $76C2, patched with the incoming Y at $76B2. The handler saves X at $76C1, sets bit $08 in the selected player flags, calls $77E2 with A=5, restores X and Y from the patched operands and tail-jumps to $4454.

Immediate operand of the LDX at $76DD, which restores X after message 8 is prepared through $77E2, before the jump to $4454. $76D2 stores X here (with Y at $76E0); no other instruction writes it. The load holds $FF here.
Saved Y operand restored at $76DF after the flag/message handler. Tail-jump to entity release $4454 with the restored registers.
Load A=$10 and tail-jump to $21F0, setting bit 4 of the selected player’s flags while retaining the other bits.

Set the Gauntlet counter at $4DDF to 10 and set bit $20 in the selected player's flags through $21F0. Each successful player attack contact consumes one count at $74A9; the contact that reaches zero still receives doubled damage.
Set protection charge count $4DDE to 5, then tail-call the selected-player OR helper $21F0 with A=$80 to set that flag.
Set the wing-boots counter at $4DE0 to $FF and set flag $08 for the selected player. The movement code at $0A92 consumes the counter when its input and fall-step conditions hold.

Immediate operand of the LDY at $7718, which restores the Y that type $F8's contact handler had on entry, after the message call at $7715. $7707, the handler's first instruction, stores it, and $770A saves X at $771B; the load holds $FF. The handler then releases the entity with JMP $4454.

Immediate operand of the LDX at $771A, which restores X after message 7 is prepared through $77E2, before the jump to $4454. $770A stores X here (with Y at $7719, stored at $7707) before X is loaded from $4DBD; no other instruction writes it. The load holds $FF here.

Save A in the immediate operand at $7731 and call $3020 with decimal mode clear. Set decimal mode and mask its result to three bits. Values 0–4 remain unchanged; values 5–7 are masked to 1–3. Add the resulting offset to the saved byte in decimal mode with carry clear, then clear decimal mode.
Immediate operand patched at $771F with the incoming reward byte. The ADC at $7730 uses it in decimal mode and clears decimal mode afterward.
Save the calculated amount, call $7874 to add it to the selected balance, restore it and call $36E9 to split its nibbles. Call $77E2 with A=2 to prepare the message.
Copy $370A to $4F16. Copy $3709 to $4F15 unless it equals 1, then call $4B0E with A=2 and return.

Push incoming A, clear $778B, and shift A left four times, rotating each shifted-out bit into $778B. Call $4B0E with the low byte of the resulting 16-bit product, then call $4B20 with $778B. Call $77E2 with A=3, restore the original byte and call $36E9 to split its nibbles. Copy the low-nibble result to $4F13; copy the high-nibble result to $4F12 only when it differs from 1, then return. The split routine adds one to each nibble.
Immediate operand of the LDA at $778A. It is cleared at $7774 and rotated four times at $7778–$7784 to hold the high byte of the incoming value shifted left four places.
Adds A to the selected meter modulo 256, then compares the wrapped result with the meter limit. Carry out is not included in the comparison, so large inputs can wrap below the limit.
Subtracts A from the selected meter and floors the result to zero when the result's sign bit is set. This is not a general unsigned saturation test for all byte values.
Patched subtraction operand at $77C6. The result is tested by sign, not by carry: replace a negative result with zero, store to selected-player meter $4DCD,Y and return.

No instruction in the resident part or in any load jumps or branches here, and the byte pair $D0 $77 occurs in none of them, so no trigger record names it as a callback. If entered, it preserves A while comparing horizontal sub-tile offset $527C with 8. At offsets 8–255, increment $487F,X, restore A and return. At offsets 0–7, restore A and branch to $77E2 when nonzero; zero falls through $77E0, which also loads zero before preparing the message.
Select direct-pointer message mode by loading A=0, then fall through to $77E2. X/Y supply the pointer for that mode; the common entry also accepts nonzero message selectors.

A nonzero A selects a message record; zero with nonzero X/Y uses a direct pointer, while A=X=Y=0 clears message state. It copies three zero-terminated fields into 20-byte buffers, translating spaces to zero, then reads a control byte. A message number runs from 1 to 22, and $77E7 subtracts one to index the 22-entry pointer tables at $5636 and $564C. The copy loops stop only at a zero byte, and no line of the 22 records or of the messages passed by address is longer than 20 characters, so each line fits its buffer. Control $FF waits for Fire before changing to 5.

Set decimal mode, load player index X from $4DBD and add the packed-decimal byte in A to $4DC9,X, propagating carry into $4DC7,X. Clear decimal mode and return; a carry out of the high byte is not stored.

Set decimal mode and split A into $78CF=(A AND $0F) shifted left four bits and $78D0=A shifted right four bits. Load X from $4DBD and subtract those bytes from $4DC9,X and $4DC7,X with decimal borrow.
If the two-byte subtraction borrowed, add $78CF and $78D0 back to the selected player balance in decimal mode; both the successful and restored paths clear decimal mode and return.
Low packed-decimal byte of the amount formed by $7889 from its input nibble.
High packed-decimal byte of the amount formed by $7889 from its input nibble.

Set decimal mode and save A at $7900. Subtract it from $4DC9,X and subtract the borrow from $4DC7,X, with X loaded from $4DBD. If that borrowed, add the saved byte and carry back; clear decimal mode and return.
Packed-decimal byte saved from A for the subtraction and possible restoration at $78D1.

Set decimal mode and load X from $4DBD. Subtract the packed-decimal low byte at $7D from $4DC9,X and the high byte at $7E plus borrow from $4DC7,X. If the high-byte subtraction does not borrow, clear decimal mode and return with carry set.
On borrow, add the low and high bytes at $7D/$7E back into the selected balance in decimal mode, clear carry and decimal mode, and return.

Double $1919,X modulo 256 into Y and save X in the immediate operand at $795E. Load the display-slot index from $1A29,X. Shift the slot X position $4C4F,X:$4C6F,X right one bit and add $79B6,Y; store the low result in $762E. Store $79B7,Y in $7630.

Add $7A12,Y to the display-slot Y byte at $4CCF,X and store the result in $762F. Store $7A13,Y in $7631, restore the saved entity X from $795E and return. X is the entity's display slot from $1A29, which the allocators at $1C30 and $1E35 set from a search of the 32 slots and the releases set to 0; Y is twice the entity type, and only the handlers of types $01 to $26, $2C and $2D call $792C, so Y stays within the 46 pairs for types 0 to $2D.
Immediate operand patched by $7931 with the entity index so that $795D can restore X after using it as a display-slot index.

Copies the load's six-byte trigger records, from the pointer at $7F52/$7F53, into the parallel arrays at $485F, $486F, $487F, $48AF, $488F and $489F, 16 bytes apart, after storing $FF in $E1. The count at $7F54 is the load's own: from 1 to 12 across the 31 loads, 8 in load 1 and 12 in loads 26 and 27. It is tested only after incrementing an 8-bit index: zero would cause 256 iterations, and a count above 16 would overlap neighbouring fields.

Horizontal collision offset and width for entity types 0–$2D, two bytes per type. $792C doubles the type into Y; $7941 adds $79B6,Y to half the display slot's X position for the box's left edge ($762E), and $7947 loads $79B7,Y as its width ($7630). Type 0 and types $27–$2B have zero pairs.

Horizontal collision parameters continuing from $79B6: each pair gives the offset added to the halved display-slot X coordinate and the rectangle width, indexed by twice the entity type. The first byte here is the width for type 0; the pairs continue through the offset for type 32. Only the handlers of types $01 to $26, $2C and $2D call $792C, so the pairs it reads stay within the 46 for types 0 to $2D.

Continuation of the horizontal collision parameter pairs through type 45. This first byte is the width for type 32; the following pairs give each type’s offset and width. Only the handlers of types $01 to $26, $2C and $2D call $792C, so the pairs it reads stay within the 46 for types 0 to $2D.

Vertical collision offset and height for entity types 0–$2D, two bytes per type, indexed by twice the type from $792C. $7951 adds $7A12,Y to the display slot's Y position for the box's top ($762F), and $7957 loads $7A13,Y as its height ($7631). Type 0 and types $27–$2B have zero pairs.

Vertical collision parameters continuing from $7A12: each pair gives the offset added to the display-slot Y coordinate and the rectangle height, indexed by twice the entity type. The first byte here is the height for type 0; the pairs continue through the offset for type 32. Only the handlers of types $01 to $26, $2C and $2D call $792C, so the pairs it reads stay within the 46 for types 0 to $2D.

Continuation of the vertical collision parameter pairs through type 45. This first byte is the height for type 32; the following pairs give each type’s offset and height. Only the handlers of types $01 to $26, $2C and $2D call $792C, so the pairs it reads stay within the 46 for types 0 to $2D.
Push incoming A, write $35 to processor port $01 and call $6A75. Wait until $D012 equals $80, then write zero to $D021, $D418 and $D015 and write $0B to $D011. Pull A and jump to $7A9A.

Patch the immediate operand at $7A98 with incoming X, call $77E2 to prepare the message whose number is in A, reload X from that operand and return. Its one caller is $74B8, which passes 12 for “Gauntlet is broken.”
Immediate operand of the LDX at $7A97, patched with incoming X at $7A91 and used after the $77E2 call.
Patch the stage selector into $2A91, set $2C15 to $FF and call the sound sequencer at $2201. Clear the three SID voice control registers, write $35 to the CPU port and continue to save memory.

Copy all 256 bytes of pages $0000, $0200 and $0300 to $C000, $C100 and $C200. Clear pages $0200 and $0300 and bytes $0002–$00FF; leave CPU port bytes $0000/$0001 in place. The loop visits index 0 first and then $FF down to 1.
Copy the 53 bytes at $7BF7–$7C2B into $0300–$0334, descending from offset $34, then jump to $7AF8 for the transfer. The rest of page $0300 remains cleared.

Load the stage selector from $2A91 and call the transfer routine at $7D1B with X=0 and Y=2. Mode zero selects the decoder at $7C2C and the saved count requests two calls. On carry clear, branch to the transfer-failure path at $7B58; on carry set, call the selector-specific patches at $2A90 and continue to restore the saved pages.

Clear the transition display: with X=0 on entry, the unrolled stores and decrement loop write zero to $C000–$C3E7 and $C400–$C7E7, and write $08 to $D800–$DBE7. The latter accesses colour RAM when I/O is visible. It then jumps to $6A75. The final 24 bytes of each 1,024-byte screen page are outside these stores; other code writes sprite pointers there.
Read $D020 into Y and continue at $7B5B, preserving that byte until the retry path writes it back.

Load the immediate byte at $7B5C, XOR it with 8 and write the result to $D020. Starting X at zero, write the result to $7B5C and decrement X until it returns to zero, then AND reads from $DC01 and $DC00 and test bit 4, Fire on either joystick port, active low. When that bit is set, repeat; otherwise write saved Y to $D020 and jump to $7AE3. The loop makes 256 decrement iterations per flash.
Immediate operand of the LDA at $7B5B, repeatedly patched at $7B64 with the XOR result to alternate bit 3 on the next pass.

Ten stage-counter values: 1, 4, 7, 11, 17, 19, 22, 25, 27 and 30. Two loops compare $073E with them: $7BC8 in the path at $7BA8, and $2B38 in the path at $2B21. On a match $7BC8 goes on to clear $5284 and $2B38 jumps to $0699; with no match both jump to $0732, which advances the stage. No instruction in the resident part or in any load jumps or branches to either path.

Returns the game status byte $5284 in A; called from $0448. If player action tier $4DDB is zero, jump straight to the return at $7BDA. Otherwise load several immediate values and the player fields $4DDB, $4DD9, $4DD5 and $4DD7 without using them, set CIA1 port-A direction $DC02 to $FF, read the byte at $29A3 as data and jump to $7BDA, where the load of $5284 overwrites A. The JMP at $7BA5 passes over the path at $7BA8, and no instruction patches it.

No instruction in the resident part or in any load jumps or branches here, and the JMP at $7BA5 before it is not patched. If entered, it loads the stage counter $073E, writes $7F to CIA1 port A, selecting keyboard row 7, and reads port B: anything but $FD (the left-arrow key alone) goes to the return at $7BDA. With the key held, $1F jumps to $98D9 in load 31 through $7BDE, and $10 first sets bit $40 of the selected player's flags through $21F0. Then one of the ten values at $7B7A clears $5284 and returns, and any other value, $10 among them, drops one return address and jumps to $0732, which advances the stage.

Jump to $98D9. The branch at $7BB9 that reaches this is taken when the stage counter $073E is $1F, when load 31 is in memory; there $98D9 is the LDA #$FE inside the routine at $98CE, after its calls to $4B20, $4454 and $331D, and it goes on to store $FE at $2C15 and $49. Bytes of other loads at this address are not instructions. No instruction enters the path at $7BA8 that holds the branch.
Load the service counter from the immediate operand at $7BE2. Its zero/nonzero paths either reset the counter and delay or decrement it and call $2201, as described at the operand.

Self-modified immediate counter for $7BE1. A nonzero value is decremented before calling the SID sequencer at $2201. Zero skips that call, resets the counter to 6 and runs a delay with X starting at $40 and ending at $FF. Without other writes, initial value 6 gives six sequencer calls followed by one skipped call.

The 53 bytes that $7AD8 copies to $0300–$0334 for the length of a transfer, after $7AB4 has saved page 3 at $C200 and cleared it; $7B07 puts the saved page back afterwards. $0300–$0333 is where BASIC and the KERNAL keep their RAM vectors, and these are ROM addresses, low byte first: $E38B, $A483, $A57C, $A71A, $A7E4 and $AE86 for $0300–$030B, four zero bytes, $4C $48 $B2 (JMP $B248) and a zero for $0310–$0313, then sixteen addresses for $0314–$0333, among them $EA7E for the IRQ vector at $0314, $EA86 for the NMI vector at $0318 and $F4A5 for the load vector at $0330. The last byte, $01, goes to $0334.

Set Y to zero and fetch three bytes into $69, $68 and $67 in that order. The first two form the initial output pointer high and low bytes; $67 is the bit reservoir. Build 52 decoding-table entries at $7C38, reset Y to zero and enter the item decoder at $7C96. The transfer callback and later item decoding have separate paths.

Build 52 entries in the stack-page tables: bit counts at $0104–$0137, base low bytes at $0138–$016B and base high bytes at $016C–$019F. For entries 0, 16, 32 and 48, start the 16-bit base at 1. For each other entry, add 2 raised to the preceding entry's bit count to the preceding base, modulo 65536. Read four bits through $7C6A for this entry's bit count; after entry 51, continue at $7C66. The header loop of the decoder at $7C2C falls into this loop from $7C36, and the item decoder reads the tables at $7CBD–$7CCA and $7CF2–$7D06.

Clear A and the high accumulator at $66. If X is zero, return immediately; otherwise read X bits through $7C72. Bits are taken least-significant first from each fetched byte and shifted into the 16-bit accumulator $66:A, with A as the low byte; X reaches zero and Y is unchanged. The byte reader at $7D89 returns the carry it was called with. A refill from here calls it with carry set, the marker bit just shifted out of $67, provided $67 was not already zero, so the BCC at $7C7A to $7C91 is not taken on this path; it is taken when the literal copy at $7C8D enters $7C77 with carry clear.

Shift the reservoir at $67 right. If the result is zero, save A, call the buffered-byte reader and, when carry is set, rotate the fetched byte right with a high sentinel bit before restoring A. Rotate the selected bit into A and then $66, decrement X and repeat until X is zero. If that fetch returns carry clear, branch to the output store at $7C91 instead of restoring A here.
Decrement X and the high bytes of both the output pointer at $69 and the source pointer at $65. Continue to the backward byte-copy loop at $7C8C; this entry handles the next full page of a copy.

Decrement Y. With carry clear, call the buffered-byte reader through $7C77; when it returns carry clear, store the fetched byte at the output pointer plus Y. With carry set, load from the source pointer at $64–$65 plus Y and store it at the same output position. The ordinary buffered-byte reader preserves carry; its refill and failure paths are separate.
Store A at the output pointer $68–$69 plus Y. This entry is shared by fetched literal bytes and source-pointer copies.
Transfer Y to A. If Y is nonzero, copy another byte at $7C8C; otherwise continue to $7C96, which either advances a full page or decodes the next item.

If X is nonzero, go to $7C87 to advance another page of the current copy. Otherwise increment X and read one bit with $7C6A. A nonzero result goes to $7CB5; zero begins the prefix loop at $7CA0. These statements describe the ordinary returning bit-reader path.

Increment X, read through $7C72, shift A right and increment Y. Repeat while the shifted bit is clear. If Y wraps to zero, branch to $7CE4. Otherwise, Y below $11 selects $7CBD, Y equal to $11 returns from the decoder, and Y above $11 reads 16 bits before continuing at $7CB5.

Save A as the low length byte at $63, load X from the high accumulator at $66 and clear Y. If carry is clear, branch to the destination adjustment at $7CE4; otherwise continue into the table-based length decoder at $7CBD.

Read the bit count indexed by Y from $0103, read that many bits, and add the indexed low base from $0137 using the returned carry. Store the low result at $63, add the indexed high base from $016B to $66 with the low addition's carry, and push the high result. If it is nonzero, use class 3; otherwise use the low result as class when it is below 4, or class 3 when it is not.

Read the bit count indexed by Y at $7D14, call the bit reader and add the indexed adjustment from $7D17 using its returned carry. Move that result to Y, reload the low length at $63 and continue to the destination adjustment at $7CE4. The bit-count lookup overlaps adjacent instruction and table bytes.

Subtract the output-pointer low byte at $68 from A using the incoming carry. If the subtraction sets carry, decrement the output-pointer high byte at $69. Invert the subtraction result and store it at $68. Compare Y with 1: zero selects $7D10, while a nonzero Y continues to $7CF2.

Read the bit count at $0104,Y and use $7C6A to read that many bits. Add the indexed low base at $0138,Y with the returned carry; if that addition carries, increment $66. Clear carry and add the adjusted value to output-pointer low byte $68 to form source-pointer low byte $64. Continue forming its high byte at $7D04.

Add the indexed high base at $016C,Y and the output-pointer high byte $69 to $66, propagating carry between the additions, and store the result at source-pointer high byte $65. Pop the saved high length into X, set carry and continue to $7D10.
Load Y from the low length at $63 and jump to $7C93. Carry is retained through that jump and selects literal-byte fetching or the source-pointer copy when the backward loop copies bytes.

High address byte of the JMP at $7D12, paired with $7D13; its value is $7C. It also sits at entry 0 of the bit-count table that $7CD8 reads as $7D14,Y, but Y there is the copy length, 1 to 3 ($7CD0–$7CD6), so $7CD8 never reads this byte; entries 1 to 3 are the 2, 4 and 4 at $7D15–$7D17.

Bit counts 2 and 4 for the unpacker's copy distance, entries 1 and 2 of the table that $7CD8 reads as $7D14,Y: Y is the copy length, at least 1 since every length base that the table builder at $7C38 makes starts at 1, and $7CD0–$7CD6 use 3 for any length of 3 or more, which reads the 4 at $7D17. $7D3F also loads $7D15,X into Y, with X the transfer mode, 0 from $7AFD or 2 from $7AEA, but $7DAB loads Y with 2 before Y is read, so that value is never used.

Four bytes. The 4 at $7D17 is the last entry of the bit-count table that $7CD8 reads as $7D14,Y, used for a copy length of 3 or more. $30, $20 and $10 at $7D18–$7D1A are the distance adjustments that $7CDE adds as $7D17,Y for lengths 1, 2 and 3 or more: Y is the copy length capped at 3 and is never 0, since every length base that the table builder at $7C38 makes starts at 1, and the bit reader $7C6A keeps Y. $7D3F also loads this byte into Y when the transfer mode X is 2 ($7AEA), but $7DAB loads Y with 2 before Y is read.

Runs a resident serial transfer with patched mode callbacks. The bytes, where they go and when the transfer ends are decided by the device at the other end of the serial bus; its waits poll CIA2 port A $DD00 with no counter.
Set the low byte of the transfer-mode call from the indexed table.
Set the high byte of the transfer-mode call from the indexed table.

Call the transfer-mode handler that $7D45 and $7D4B patch into the operand from the tables $7DFC,X and $7DFF,X, with X the mode passed to $7D1B: $7C2C decodes the transition bit stream (mode 0, from $7AFF), $7E02 receives a block into memory (mode 1) and $7E25 sends memory out (mode 2, from $7AEC). The load holds JSR $7E02. DEC $61 and BNE repeat the call for each unit.

Low byte of the target of the JSR at $7D72, whose high byte is $7D74. The load holds $02 here, so the instruction reads JSR $7E02 until it is patched. $7D45 stores it from $7DFC,X and $7D4B the high byte from $7DFF,X, so the call goes to $7C2C, $7E02 or $7E25; every path from $7D42 to the call passes those stores. No other instruction writes it.
High byte of the mode-selected JSR at $7D72. After a transfer-unit call, decrement zero-page count $61 and repeat the call while nonzero; completion falls through to stack/port restoration at $7D79.

Decrement the transfer count at $61 and call the patched target at $7D72 again while it is nonzero. A count of 2 therefore makes two calls, provided the target returns normally. Continue to stack and port restoration when the count reaches zero.

Restore the stack pointer from the immediate operand at $7D7A, which $7D37 patched after saving the CIA2 port and processor port. Pop and restore $01 and $DD00, then wait until bit 6 of $DD00 is set and return. The wait polls $DD00 with no counter; this code does not change carry.

Immediate stack pointer restored into X at $7D79. Transfer it to SP, pop the saved processor-port byte to $01, then pop the saved CIA2 port-A byte to $DD00. Continue into the serial ready wait at $7D83.
Use BIT on CIA2 port A $DD00 and loop while bit 6 is clear (overflow clear). Return once it is set. The loop has no counter, so it waits for as long as the bit stays clear.

Save processor flags with PHP and test the low address operand at $7D9C. When it is nonzero, read the buffered byte at $7D9B. When it is zero, first enter the refill path at $7D8F. On the ordinary buffered return, PLP restores the incoming flags, including carry, while A holds the fetched byte.

Save Y into the immediate operand at $7D9A, increment the processor port at $01, call $7DAB for a transfer-block header, decrement $01 and restore Y from the patched immediate. Continue to read the buffered byte at $7D9B; the transfer routine has its own failure and stack paths.
The low address operand $7d9c is also the mutable buffer position; it is incremented during reads.

Immediate operand of the LDY at $7D99, which restores the caller's Y after the buffer refill ($7D92–$7D97) used Y, so the unpacker at $7C2C keeps its index. $7D8F stores Y here when the buffer read position at $7D9C has reached zero; the load holds $00.

Load a byte through the absolute address whose low operand is $7D9C and high operand is $7D9D; the high byte is $C3. Increment the low operand, restore the flags saved by $7D89 and return. Incrementing $FF wraps the low operand to zero so the next call enters the refill path.
Low byte of the buffer-read address in LDA at $7D9B. Increment it after each byte, restore saved processor flags with PLP and return. The high operand at $7D9D selects the buffer page.
Clear carry and branch unconditionally to $7D79, which restores the transfer stack and processor port. This is a transfer-failure path rather than the ordinary buffered return.
Patch the receive-mode opcode at $7DBF with $60 (RTS), then enter the block-header receiver at $7DAB.

Begin a transfer block header: set Y and the buffer read position at $7D9C to 2 and patch $7DED with opcode $60 (RTS), then call the byte receiver $7DC4. A received byte equal to 1 branches to the transfer-failure path $7DA3; any other value is stored at $7DBC in the CPY operand at $7DF8, the index at which the block ends. Completion depends on the external serial peer.

Opcode patched to choose what follows a block header. $7D53 writes $A9, making this LDA #$99: the STA at $7DC1 then patches $7DED to STA $C300,Y and execution falls into $7DC4, which receives the block into the buffer at $C300 from index 2 up to the end index at $7DF8. $7DA8 writes $60, an RTS: the header routine returns after the header byte and its caller receives the bytes itself.

Wait until bit 6 of $DD00 is set. Execute two CMP ($C1,X) reads, write $20 and then $00 to $DD00, and take four more $DD00 samples. Starting with the first sample shifted right twice, XOR the second and shift right twice, XOR the third and shift right twice, then XOR the fourth. Continue at the runtime-patched opcode at $7DED. The wait polls $DD00 with no counter.

Runtime-patched opcode: $60 returns immediately with the reconstructed byte in A; $99 uses the following bytes $00,$C3 to store A at $C300,Y, then decrements and increments the border register, increments Y and compares it with the operand at $7DF8. These are the only two values written: $60 by $7DB2, and $99 by $7D5B and $7DC1.

When the patched receive opcode at $7DED stores a byte instead of returning, decrement and then increment border register $D020, increment Y, and compare it with the patched count operand at $7DF8. The next branch determines whether to receive another byte.
Compare receive index Y with the patched count at $7DF8. The following BNE repeats byte reception when they differ.

Immediate operand of the CPY at $7DF7. In the $99 store mode, incremented Y is compared with this byte; a mismatch branches back to $7DC4 and a match returns. The operand is patched by the transfer header path.
After comparing the receive index with the patched count at $7DF7, BNE branches to $7DC4 for another byte; equality returns with RTS.
Three low bytes for the transfer-mode handler table. The paired high bytes at $7DFF complete the call targets selected by the transition mode.
Three high bytes paired with transfer-mode target lows at $7DFC.

Start X at zero and Y at 4. Receive a byte, temporarily decrement processor port $01 while storing it through the pointer at $64/$65, restore $01, and increment the pointer with carry into its high byte. Increment Y and compare it with $7DF8. A nonzero matching Y returns; a zero match calls $7DA6 for the next block's header, which sets Y to 2 and $7DF8 to the new end index, and continues receiving.

After waiting for serial readiness, read successive bytes through $64/$65 with Y zero, temporarily decrementing $01 around each read. Send each byte with $7E53 and increment the pointer. With decimal mode clear, the comparison stops once the incremented pointer is at least $4DC1, so the last byte sent is $4DC0, the low byte of the record score. This is the mode-2 handler in the tables at $7DFC/$7DFF: $7D72 calls it when $7AE6 starts a transfer with X=2, after $2B80 has turned the JMP at $7AE3 into a BIT to save a new record score. $7D68 receives the start address into $64/$65 first.

Return from the memory send at $7E25, transfer mode 2, once the pointer $64/$65 reaches $4DC1: the subtraction at $7E39–$7E3F leaves carry set when the pointer is $4DC1 or more, so the last byte sent is the one at $4DC0. The waits on the way, $7D83 for bit 6 of $DD00 and the two clock waits in $7E53, loop on the port with no counter, so the send finishes only as fast as the other machine answers.

Start the serial handshake by writing $1F to CIA2 data direction $DD02. Load Y=$3F and wait while unsigned $DD00 is greater than $3F, then write $3F to $DD02 and fall through to the byte sender at $7E53. There is no timeout in this local wait loop; an external peer supplies the line state.

Save incoming X and Y into the immediate operands at $7E7D and $7E7F and store incoming A at $62. Shift $62 left eight times, sending its original bits most significant first. For each bit, select $2F if the shifted-out bit is 1 or $1F if it is 0. Wait while $DD00 is at most $3F, write the selected value to $DD02, then wait while $DD00 is greater than $3F and write $3F to $DD02. Restore X and Y and return. Both waits poll $DD00 with no counter. The memory sender calls it at $7E30, and the handshake at $7E44 falls into it to send the byte $7D3C passes in A at the start of every transfer.
LDX opcode that restores caller X from the patched immediate at $7E7D after serial transmission.
Immediate operand of the LDX at $7E7C, patched with incoming X by the serial sender at $7E53.
LDY opcode that restores caller Y from the patched immediate at $7E7F before the serial sender returns.
Immediate operand of the LDY at $7E7E, patched with incoming Y by the serial sender at $7E56.

RAM vectors that $6A75 writes: NMI $11E8 ($6A95, $6A9A), reset $121B ($6A8B, $6A90) and IRQ $005D ($6A9F, $6AA4). The game runs with the KERNAL ROM switched out ($01=$35, set at $6A7D), so the CPU takes its NMI and IRQ vectors from this RAM. The reset word is never fetched: a hardware reset clears the processor port's direction register $00, the KERNAL ROM reappears, and the CPU reads its own vector. $121B is the RTI that ends the NMI handler.

RAM word under the hardware reset vector. $6A8B and $6A90 store $1B and $12, pointing it at $121B, the RTI that ends the NMI handler. The CPU never reads it: a hardware reset clears the processor port's direction register $00, which brings the KERNAL ROM back over $E000–$FFFF before the vector is fetched.

RAM IRQ vector, set to $005D by $6A9F and $6AA4. $020C stores a JMP opcode at $005D, and the raster-interrupt handlers write the next handler's address into its operand at $5E/$5F ($1663, $1773 and seven other pairs), so each IRQ goes through zero page to the handler for the next screen split. The CPU reads this word while the KERNAL ROM is switched out, as it is with $01=$35.
